# Storage design — Stage 1 implementation plan: everything under `~/.openalpaca/`

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build Part I of the storage design: no folder written inside a user's project any more — each project gets a folder under `~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/` named after its path, with a permanent id in `project.json`; projects are found by a pure resolver and registered where the daemon accepts work; content, memory and rows address a project by that folder; a project can be listed, re-pointed after a move, and have its data deleted; the app shows the projects.

**Architecture:** Six slices built in order, each leaving the tree compiling and green. S1 adds `openalpaca_storage::store::projects` (names, `project.json`, lookup/list/register) and a test-build guard that stops any test registering under the real home; S2 switches resolution to the new resolver and registers at the four sites (content still in the project); S3 flips content under `projects/<name>/`, adds migration 003, the re-point core and its boot recovery; S4 keys memory by project id; S5a builds "delete its data", the routes and the CLI; S5b builds the app's Projects surfaces; S6 updates the text, runs the gate and the live check, and writes the records. The names and signatures every slice shares are fixed in the interfaces sheet each slice was drafted against.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.93.0 (edition 2024), rusqlite, serde, tokio, axum; React 19 + TypeScript + Vitest (bun) for the app; `cargo test` per crate; the local Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` for the live check only.

**Spec:** `tasks/storage-design/design.md` rev 0.8 (approved 2026-10-05; Stage 0 built) — §0.1 (owner decisions ST-1…ST-22), Part I §1–§9, §16 *Order*, §17 *Records*. **Lead's rulings on the drafts:** R-S1…R-S18 (three rounds), in the section *Rulings* below — binding on every implementer.

**Where this plan came from:** an interfaces sheet, six slice drafts and S6, each written against the tree at `6aecb614`/`32292608` by an Opus drafter and corrected in place by an Opus verifier; a cross-slice consistency check; two rounds of the lead's rulings applied and verified. Line numbers are of that tree and drift as slices land: **locate code by content**.

## Global Constraints

- **Model policy (owner, 2026-10-06):** Opus 5.5 does every job — implementing, each task's review, the final review. Fable 5.1 only as the advisor.
- **Order:** S1 → S2 → S3 → S4 → S5a → S5b → S6, tasks in their numbered order. Each commit leaves the workspace compiling and its own crate's tests green.
- **One cargo process at a time**, always (`pgrep -x cargo` before each). Per task: `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>` as the task gives it. The workspace run happens **once**, at S6.4, then `pkill -f "sleep 3600"`.
- **The owner's store is never touched.** `~/.openalpaca` is never read, written, listed or pointed at — not by a command, not by a test, not even read-only. Every test that touches a store uses a tempfile directory and the crate's home-store guard; from S1.9 on, the `test-home-guard` feature makes `register` under an unguarded home fail loudly; from S2.5 on, a turn with no client path resolves no project (R-S13), so no test walks the process's current directory into `projects/`.
- **No test reaches `localhost:11434`** (a test enabling a provider uses a mock or `127.0.0.1:1`). The live check (S6.5) is the one place the local model is used, under the owner's standing authorization, with the daemon under `scripts/eval/memory/loopback-only.sb` from its first launch.
- **Clippy baseline 80** (`CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo clippy --workspace --exclude openalpaca_gui --all-targets`, lines starting `warning` minus the `generated N warnings` lines) — **78** from S5a on, which deleted two (the lead's ruling). A slice may not add one.
- **Routes:** a commit that changes a route or a migration regenerates `docs/api` with `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py` in the same commit; `--check` is clean at every slice's end.
- **GUI:** a commit under `apps/openalpaca-gui/` runs all four bun gates (`bun run check`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run build` in `apps/openalpaca-gui`); `cargo check -p openalpaca_gui` at the gate.
- **Migration 003** follows CLAUDE.md's recipe (the file's number is its version; `MIGRATIONS` entry; the comment bump; `gen_api_docs` parity). The memory index's `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes 5 → 6 in S4 (rows change with the partition key); no retrieval-proxy run is needed, since tables, tokenizers and ranking are unchanged.
- **Code rules:** no `&s[..n]` string cut; `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` only inside `unsafe { }` where no other thread can touch the environment, with a `// SAFETY:` comment; snake_case sentence test names; anchored edits (never BSD `sed -i`); a new `.md` under `tasks/` is git-ignored unless whitelisted.
- **Commits:** conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line naming the command and its result, last line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Stage explicit paths only (an untracked `tasks/deps-upgrade/` belongs to another session).
- **Scope:** a task does what its text and the spec ask, nothing more. A spec conflict a draft records is settled by R-S14 or a named ruling; anything new is reported, not improvised.

## Review Focus

Input classes the spec implies that are most likely to bite a person; each is pinned by a test in the owning task (the task names are in the slice drafts below).

1. **A project path that is not plain ASCII, or whose plain folder name is already taken** (CJK, Thai, a combining mark; two roots that dash to the same name; a name over 200 bytes) — S1.2 and S1.8: the name keeps letters of every script, a collision or an over-long name gets the 8-hex suffix, and two registrations never share a folder.
2. **A project folder that was moved or deleted on disk** — S1.6/S5a.5 list it as missing with its data kept; S3.5/S5a.7 re-point it; a re-point onto a path that is already a project is refused (ST-20).
3. **A crash in the middle of a re-point** — S3.5/S3.6: the marker in `project.json` and the idempotent steps 2–4 finish it at the next boot; a failure is reported and retried, never half-applied.
4. **Deleting a project's data while another conversation still uses one of its files** — S5a.1/S5a.2: the file is kept in the root store and its row re-addressed; the repository's own files are never touched (S6.5 hashes them before and after).
5. **A test that would touch the owner's real store** — S1.7/S1.9 (the guard), S2.5 (R-S2's guards and R-S13), S3.7 (the audit): no test reads or writes `~/.openalpaca`.

## Rulings (the lead's; binding on every implementer)

R-S1. S6 (text and records) is drafted now, with the stage's gate, live check and records tasks (see s6-brief.md).
R-S2. The resolver tests that run with no home-store guard (from S2.5 on they read the real ~/.openalpaca/projects/) are guarded in S2.5 itself, the commit that switches resolution: runner/lead_agent/tests.rs (the three queue_followup tests), orchestrator/tests.rs (the callers of tool_context_for_turn), apps/openalpacad/src/routes/chat.rs tests (the callers of the `root` helper), apps/openalpaca/src/commands/sessions/tests.rs (the two workspace tests: `EnvSandbox::enter`, one line each). The rule: no test reads or writes ~/.openalpaca, even read-only.
R-S3. `MemoryService::known_project_roots` stays, reimplemented over `projects::list()` (S3.10), because the 30 s reconciliation timer calls it; S6 amends design §7's removal list to say so.
R-S4. The test guard is not called inside `repoint_with` or `remove_project_folder`: both act only on a project that a guarded `register` created, and S3.7's audit covers the tests. S1's ask is dropped.
R-S5. S2 adds one step that confirms the test guard is compiled into a daemon binary `cargo test` builds and not into one `cargo build` builds (a `strings target/debug/openalpacad | grep -c '<the guard's panic text>'` after each); the guard's panic text names the rebuild (`cargo build -p openalpacad`). Every live check builds with `cargo build -p openalpacad -p openalpaca` immediately before it launches anything.
R-S6. S5b's addition of `qk.statusAll()` to the invalidation lists is accepted.
R-S7. A registration failure answers the same on every route: the home-store overlap is `400 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME`, an I/O failure `500 WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED` — the memory-write route included (not `400 MEMORY_INVALID_INPUT`).
R-S8. Deleting a project's data takes the project exactly: `POST /v1/workspaces/purge` and `openalpaca store purge <project>` act only on a registered project's root as written (or, in the CLI, a folder name as `store list` prints it); a path inside a project is refused with an answer that names the project's root. This keeps the safety of the old "not a project root" refusal for the one verb that deletes conversations and notes. Applies to S5a.8 and S5a.11.
R-S9. The two daemon tests that wait a real 3 s stay (no tokio `test-util` dev-dependency is added to the daemon).
R-S10. `Delete data…` confirms with the dry-run plan and a danger button, no typed word — the app's other destructive dialogs' pattern (T33 stays the owner's pending question for typed words).
R-S11. A control snapshot whose project id names no registered folder (a project folder removed by hand) is not listed by the doctor; recorded as residue in design §18 by S6, not built.
R-S12. The wait_for_subagents fix (32292608) stays as built: its `#[cfg(test)]` one-shot hook in `SubagentTracker` is the only way to hit a window with no await point; both builds compile and clippy stays 80.

### Second round (2026-10-07, after the rulings were applied and S6 was drafted)
R-S7 (amended). The home-store overlap answers `409 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` on every route — HEAD's code and every draft already use 409; the ruling's "400" was the lead's slip. S6's `<is-home>` token becomes 409 everywhere.
R-S8 (code). The purge's inside-a-project refusal keeps HEAD's `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT`, for the purge only, as S5a.8 drafted.
R-S13. The daemon-CWD fallback goes: a turn whose client sent no path has no project — `MemoryScopeContext::for_request(None)` (and every equivalent) resolves nothing from the daemon's current directory. Reasons: the design's resolver takes "the path a client sent" (§3) and ST-6 makes the project the client's repository; both launchers start the daemon in the home store, where R13 already answers "no project"; and with resolution now reading `projects/`, the fallback makes ~80 tests (orchestrator/tests.rs, gateway/router/tests.rs, memory_commands, learning, daemon followup/command/scheduled_skills) read the real `~/.openalpaca/projects/`, which the owner's rule forbids even read-only. S2.5 removes the fallback in the same commit that switches resolution, updates every test that asserted a CWD-derived `workspace_id`/root, and adds one test: a turn with no path has no project even when the process's current directory is a git repository. Cost if wrong: a daemon started by hand inside a repository no longer treats that repository as the project of a client that sends no path (the CLI always sends its cwd; the app sends its chosen project).
R-S14. Every per-slice spec conflict a draft records with a "smallest correction" stands as drafted unless a ruling here says otherwise (S1: canonical_root refuses a relative path; the guard compares with starts_with; R11 reads "never listed and never bound by id" — lookup still answers for the plain-name folder; S2: for_turn before the gateway's turn guard, the dispatch registers first; S3: scope_root's return shape, fixture 04's cases, the PATCH's 404 for the home store as the source, the S3→S4 window in which a re-pointed project's notes read as quarantined — no build ships mid-stage; S4: the ST-21 check's place, fixture 17's 24 steps, derive_view through fresh_snapshot, the `unregistered:<root>` write-slot name; S5a: SC-1, SC-3, SC-7, SC-9, SC-10, the forget_session call; S5b: the window follows its project after a re-point and clears after a delete, the Choose… picker in Re-point). Two are recorded as residue in design §18 by S6, not built: a stranded `projects/.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp/` folder is never swept; the delete publishes no `memory_changed`, so an open Memory view refreshes at the next reconciliation (≤30 s). The final whole-stage review checks each against the spec.

### Third round (2026-10-07, after the second round was verified)
R-S15. The four tests the second-round verifier added to S2.5 (l) — the `/steer` turn test in orchestrator/tests.rs, the two project-switch tests in gateway/router/tests.rs, the sessions route's PATCH test — are guarded there, under R-S2's own rule; S2.6 replaces their guard lines with `guarded_home()` rather than adding a second (the core guard is one non-re-entrant lock).
R-S16. The tests that assert a `.git` lies above the test process's current directory (the R-S13 test and orchestrator/tests.rs (e)) stay: cargo runs a crate's tests from inside the checkout, and the alternative (`set_current_dir`) is process-global. A run from a source tarball fails them loudly, which is acceptable.
R-S17. S6.2's sweep includes the app's copy that says a relative path "would be read against the daemon's own directory" (apps/openalpaca-gui/src/views/settings/ConnectionSection.tsx, carried by S5b.4/S5b.6) and its pinned test: after S2 a relative path is no project; the sentence says so.
R-S18. The fields `ToolContext.workspace_id` and `request_workspace_root` are equal on every context after R-S13; collapsing them stays the follow-up `tools/registry/mod.rs` records — not in Stage 1.

## Shared interfaces — the contract every slice uses

Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`; the commit after `6aecb614` is the other session's
`wait_for_subagents` fix in `runner/lead_agent/`, unrelated). Every `file:line` below is from that HEAD.
The spec is `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8). This sheet fixes names, types, signatures and ownership
the slices share; it drafts no task. Where it departs from the spec it says so in §9 *Spec conflicts*,
and each departure is the smallest one that keeps every commit green.

### 0. Slice labels and order

| Slice | §16 item | Owns, in one line |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** | (1) | `openalpaca_storage::store::projects`: names, `project.json`, `lookup`, `list`, `by_id`, `register`, the lock, the test guard. Additive; nothing calls it. |
| **S2** | (2) | The resolver (`projects::resolve`, `resolve_and_register`, `choose`), the five registration sites, the `.openalpaca` marker and the walk's cache removed, `resolves_to_the_home_store` replaced, the `.openalpaca`-as-marker test and fixture migration. Content still in the project. |
| **S3** | (3) + the re-point | The flip (`store_root`, R12's typed error and its readers, R15, R17, `revealable_path`, the purge guard, migration `003`, fixtures 02/03/04, the `nth(4)` sites by folder, the guard audit) **and** §6's re-point core with R24's boot recovery, which replaces the move machinery (conflict C1). |
| **S4** | (4) | Memory by id: R18 key and binding, R19 snapshot field, R20 adopt, R21 index schema 6, R22, `quiesce` by id, ST-21, the doctor's move states gone, the `nth(4)` predicate swapped to the id, fixture 17 (all but step 12). |
| **S5a** | (5), daemon + CLI | The §9 wire (`GET` list, `GET ?path=`, `POST`, `PATCH`, the delete), ST-19's delete core, the quiesce retry, the CLI verbs, fixture 17 step 12. |
| **S5b** | (5), app | `lib/api/workspaces.ts`, `hooks/useWorkspaces.ts`, the Projects list, `Use`, `Re-point…`, `Delete data…`, the Memory view copy. |
| **S6** | (6) | R2 (`ContentKind` shrink + the home README), the factory-reset preview, `artifact_write`'s description, manuals, `API_MAP.md`, `DESIGN_SPEC.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, records. |

If only six drafters exist, S5a and S5b are one drafter's two halves (the daemon half lands first).

**Shared rules each slice carries** (CLAUDE.md is the authority): one cargo process at a time,
`cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`, never the workspace; a test that touches a store holds its crate's guard
(`crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard` in storage, `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard` in core and in the
daemon, `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox` in the CLI); no `&s[..n]`; `set_var` only under those guards with a
`SAFETY` comment; anchored edits only. **`python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check` runs at the end of every
slice**; it documents storage's top-level modules and `lib.rs` re-exports, every route's request struct,
the CLI's subcommands and flags, the GUI's `lib/api/*.ts` exports, and the migrations — so S3 (migration
`003`, the new top-level `project_life`), S5a (routes, CLI, re-exports) and S5b (GUI exports) regenerate
in the commit that changes them. S2, S3 and S4 run `cargo check -p openalpaca_core --features live-eval --tests`.

### 1. `openalpaca_storage::store::projects` (S1, extended by S2)

File `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects.rs`, tests `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects/tests.rs`
(the `reveal.rs` + `reveal/tests.rs` shape). `store/mod.rs` gains `pub mod projects;` beside `pub mod project_move;`.
Nothing is re-exported from `lib.rs`, so S1 changes no generated doc.

### 1.1 Constants

```rust
/// `<home>/projects` — one folder per project (ST-1). Not a `ContentKind`: it
/// exists only at the home root, and `content_dir(scope, kind)` stays `root/<kind>`.
pub const PROJECTS_DIR: &str = "projects";
pub const PROJECT_FILE: &str = "project.json";
pub const PROJECT_FILE_VERSION: u32 = 1;
/// R7: a plain name longer than this is cut at a char boundary and always hashed.
pub const NAME_MAX_BYTES: usize = 200;
/// R6: `<plain>-<8 hex of sha256(the canonical path)>`.
pub const NAME_HASH_HEX: usize = 8;
```

### 1.2 Identity

```rust
/// A project's permanent id (ST-13): a v4 UUID, written and read only in its
/// canonical hyphenated lowercase form — `NoteId::parse`'s rule
/// (`memory_files/note.rs:46`), copied, not shared.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct ProjectId(uuid::Uuid);

impl ProjectId {
    pub fn new() -> Self;                                   // Uuid::new_v4()
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String>;          // refuses a non-canonical spelling
    pub fn as_uuid(&self) -> &uuid::Uuid;
}
impl Default for ProjectId { /* new() */ }
impl std::fmt::Display for ProjectId { /* self.0.hyphenated() */ }
impl std::str::FromStr for ProjectId { type Err = String; /* parse */ }
impl serde::Serialize for ProjectId { /* serialize_str(&self.to_string()) */ }
impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for ProjectId { /* String, then parse; error = serde::de::Error::custom */ }
```

`ProjectId` is the type every later slice passes: the snapshot field, the partition key, `quiesce`.
A typed id makes every old `project_partition_key(owner, dir_string)` call a compile error in S4.

### 1.3 The file and the entry

```rust
/// `projects/<name>/project.json` exactly as R9 writes it. **Not**
/// `deny_unknown_fields`: R11's "no readable project.json" means unparseable or
/// another `version`, never "a newer build added a key". `version != 1` reads as
/// unreadable (R11).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProjectFile {
    pub version: u32,                 // PROJECT_FILE_VERSION
    pub id: ProjectId,
    pub root: String,                 // the canonical root, the string the rows hold (R4, R14)
    pub created_at: String,           // Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub previous_root: Option<String>, // only while a re-point is in flight (§6)
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub previous_name: Option<String>,
}
```

Serialized with `serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&file)` plus one `\n`, field order as declared, mode 0600,
written atomically (§1.6). `created_at` is a `String` so the bytes are fixed by one formatter and no
serde helper is shared with `memory_files`.

```rust
/// One project as its folder records it — what `lookup`, `list` and `by_id` return.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Project {
    pub id: ProjectId,
    pub root: PathBuf,                   // ProjectFile::root
    pub name: String,                    // the folder's name under projects/
    pub dir: PathBuf,                    // canonical_root(projects_dir()?.join(&name))
    pub created_at: String,
    pub missing: bool,                   // !root.is_dir(), read when the entry was read (ST-7)
    pub previous_root: Option<PathBuf>,  // Some only mid re-point
    pub previous_name: Option<String>,
}

impl Project {
    /// `root.to_string_lossy().into_owned()` — the value the five path columns hold.
    pub fn root_string(&self) -> String;
    /// The file this entry was read from, for a rewrite (§6 steps 1 and 4).
    pub fn file(&self) -> ProjectFile;
}
```

**`dir` is canonical**, built once in `read_project_dir`: `put` canonicalizes the content root before it
writes `storage_path` (`artifacts/mod.rs:889`, `uploads/mod.rs:213`) and a snapshot's `root` is canonical
(`fsx.rs:205`), so `store_root`, §4.3's `starts_with(&p.dir)` and `repoint_rows`' `old_dir`/`new_dir`
prefixes all compare like with like. With `home_root()` as set they would not on macOS, where a tempdir home
is `/var/folders/…` and its canonical form `/private/var/folders/…`.

### 1.4 The error

Storage convention (`ArtifactError`, `artifacts/mod.rs:243`): a hand-written enum with `code()` and a
one-sentence `Display`, returned **inside** `anyhow::Error`; a caller recovers it with `downcast_ref`.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ProjectError {
    /// R12: a root with no folder under projects/. `store_root` returns it (S3).
    NotRegistered { root: String },
    /// R13: the path is the home store, inside it, or contains it.
    IsHome { path: String },
    /// The path does not exist or is not a directory (register, choose, re-point target).
    NotADirectory { path: String },
    /// ST-20: the re-point target is already a project, or one of the five path columns names it.
    Exists { path: String },
    /// A re-point onto the path the project already has.
    SamePath { path: String },
}

impl ProjectError {
    pub fn code(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::NotRegistered { .. } => "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND",
            Self::IsHome { .. } => "WORKSPACE_IS_HOME",
            Self::NotADirectory { .. } => "WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY",
            Self::Exists { .. } => "WORKSPACE_EXISTS",
            Self::SamePath { .. } => "INVALID_PATH",
        }
    }
}
impl std::fmt::Display for ProjectError { /* below */ }
impl std::error::Error for ProjectError {}

/// Whether `e`, anywhere in its chain, is `ProjectError::NotRegistered` — how a
/// reader learns a root is unregistered after the fact (R12). Chain-aware so a
/// `.context(..)` added by a caller never hides it.
pub fn is_not_registered(e: &anyhow::Error) -> bool;
```

`Display`, exactly (tests may pin them):

| Variant | Text |
|---|---|
| `NotRegistered` | `{root} is not a project OpenAlpaca knows: no folder under projects/ records it` |
| `IsHome` | `{path} is, contains or lies inside the OpenAlpaca home store, so it cannot be a project. Name the project directory itself` |
| `NotADirectory` | `{path} is not a directory. Create it first, or name the folder the project is in now` |
| `Exists` | `{path} is already a project of its own, or OpenAlpaca's records already name it. Re-pointing onto it would merge two projects: delete that project's data first, or re-point onto another path` (ST-20: both ways out) |
| `SamePath` | `{path} is already where the project is` |

HTTP statuses are the daemon's (`routes/workspaces.rs`, `project_error_response`, §6.4):
404, 409, 422, 409, 400 in that order.

### 1.5 Functions (S1)

```rust
/// `home_root()?.join(PROJECTS_DIR)`. Creates nothing.
pub fn projects_dir() -> Result<PathBuf>;

/// R4, R5, R7 — pure. NFC of `root.to_string_lossy()`; each char kept when
/// `c.is_alphanumeric() || unicode_normalization::char::is_combining_mark(c)`,
/// else one `-`; runs not collapsed. Longer than NAME_MAX_BYTES: cut with
/// `let end = s.floor_char_boundary(NAME_MAX_BYTES); s.truncate(end);` and
/// suffixed `-<path_hash>` (R7: always hashed).
pub fn folder_name(root: &Path) -> String;

/// R6 — pure. `<folder_name>-<path_hash>`; for a name R7 already cut and hashed,
/// that same name. path_hash = first NAME_HASH_HEX chars of
/// `crate::memory_files::sha256_hex(root.to_string_lossy().as_bytes())` — the
/// raw canonical string, not its NFC form.
pub fn hashed_folder_name(root: &Path) -> String;

/// The canonical form of a path that may not exist: the deepest existing
/// ancestor canonicalized, the missing tail appended as written
/// (`memory_files::fsx::canonical_string_lenient`'s rule, which S1 makes
/// `pub(crate)`). Errors only for a path with no existing ancestor (a relative one).
pub fn canonical_root(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf>;

/// R13, replacing `resolves_to_the_home_store` (removed in S2): canonical
/// `root` equals the canonical home root, starts with it, or is an ancestor of
/// it. `false` when `home_root()` fails or `canonical_root` errors (a relative
/// path) — never propagated.
pub fn overlaps_home_store(root: &Path) -> bool;

/// §3 lookup: `canonical_root(root)`, then `projects/<folder_name>/project.json`
/// and, when that is absent or names another root, `projects/<hashed_folder_name>/`.
/// `Ok(None)` = not registered. A folder whose file is unreadable is skipped with
/// one WARN per folder per process (R11). Two small reads; no scan; no lock.
pub fn lookup(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>>;

/// §3 list: every directory under projects/ (dot-prefixed names and links
/// skipped) with a readable file, sorted by `name`. Two folders carrying one id
/// (R11, a copied folder): both left out, one WARN. A missing `projects/` is an
/// empty list. Entries mid re-point are included (R24 reads them).
pub fn list() -> Result<Vec<Project>>;

/// `list()` filtered by id. `Ok(None)` for no folder, or for two (R11).
pub fn by_id(id: &ProjectId) -> Result<Option<Project>>;

/// §3 register: create-if-absent under `lock()`. In order: the test guard
/// (§1.7); `canonical_root(root)`; `lookup` → an existing entry is returned as
/// it is (a missing project included); `overlaps_home_store` → `IsHome`; not a
/// directory → `NotADirectory`; the name (`name_for`); then the folder is built
/// as `projects/.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp/` holding project.json (0700 / 0600,
/// fsync) and renamed to `projects/<name>` — the rename is the create-if-absent,
/// so a crash never leaves a folder without its file. Returns the entry read back.
pub fn register(root: &Path) -> Result<Project>;

/// The one process-wide lock: `register`, the re-point and the delete's folder
/// removal hold it. Poison is recovered (`unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())`).
/// **Lock order: this lock, then the database mutex — never the reverse.** The
/// re-point holds it across `repoint_rows`' `with_connection`, so nothing may
/// call `register` (or take this lock) inside a `with_connection` closure:
/// `dispatch_lead_agent_inner` (§2.2 row 2) registers before its first
/// repository call.
pub struct ProjectsLock(std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, ()>);
pub fn lock() -> ProjectsLock;

// crate-private, for `crate::project_life` (S3, S5a):
pub(crate) fn name_for(root: &Path, this: Option<&ProjectId>, held: &ProjectsLock) -> Result<String>;
pub(crate) fn write_project_file(dir: &Path, file: &ProjectFile) -> Result<()>;   // atomic 0600
pub(crate) fn read_project_dir(dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>>;            // R11 rules
```

`name_for`: the plain name unless `projects/<plain>` exists and is not this project's — its file names
another root and (when `this` is `Some`) carries another id, or it has no readable file; then the hashed
name; if that is taken the same way, an `anyhow` error naming both folders. `this` is `Some(id)` only on a
re-point, so a project whose new plain name equals its own folder keeps it (no rename).

S1 also widens `memory_files::fsx` to `pub(crate) mod fsx;` (`memory_files/mod.rs:40`) and makes
`create_private_dir`, `write_atomic_private`, `read_if_exists`, `remove_dir_all_if_exists`, `fsync_dir` and
`canonical_string_lenient` `pub(crate)`, updating the module comment (`fsx.rs:5-7`) that says it carries
its own copies. That is S1's only edit outside the new file and `store/mod.rs:27`.

### 1.6 Atomicity and modes

`projects/` and each project folder: `create_private_dir` (0700). `project.json`: `write_atomic_private`
(0600, no-follow, temp + fsync + rename + dir fsync). R3: a project folder holds `project.json` and content
directories only.

### 1.7 The test guard (spec §3 last bullet; conflict C2)

`crates/openalpaca_storage/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[features]
# Test builds of the crates that depend on this one turn it on through their
# [dev-dependencies], so `store::projects::register` refuses an unguarded home
# store in every test binary and in no release or `cargo run` build.
test-home-guard = []
```

In `projects.rs`:

```rust
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-home-guard"))]
fn refuse_unguarded_test_home() {
    let set = std::env::var_os(super::HOME_STORE_ENV);
    let default = directories::BaseDirs::new()
        .map(|b| b.home_dir().join(super::STORE_DIR_NAME));
    let unguarded = match &set {
        None => true,
        Some(value) => default.as_deref().is_some_and(|real| Path::new(value).starts_with(real)),
    };
    if unguarded {
        panic!(
            "store::projects::register in a test build with {} {}: take the crate's home-store \
             guard (HomeStoreGuard; EnvSandbox in the CLI) first, so no test writes into the \
             developer's ~/.openalpaca. A daemon binary `cargo test` built carries this check \
             too: rebuild it with `cargo build -p openalpacad` before running it by hand",
            super::HOME_STORE_ENV,
            if set.is_none() { "unset" } else { "pointing into the real home store" },
        );
    }
}
#[cfg(not(any(test, feature = "test-home-guard")))]
fn refuse_unguarded_test_home() {}
```

S1.7 is the code of record (its pure `unguarded_home` beside it): a store set *inside* the real one is refused
too (`starts_with`, S1's *Spec conflicts*), and the last sentence is the lead's R-S5 — `cargo test -p openalpacad`
builds `target/debug/openalpacad` with this feature on, which a checkout's `openalpaca daemon start` spawns; S2's
slice gate proves the guard is in that binary and gone after `cargo build -p openalpacad`. The phrase
`take the crate's home-store guard` is what tests and that gate match.

Dependents add, beside their normal dependency (the `openalpaca_mcp` `test-utils` precedent in
`crates/openalpaca_core/Cargo.toml` and `apps/openalpacad/Cargo.toml`):


in `crates/openalpaca_core`, `apps/openalpacad`, `apps/openalpaca`, `crates/openalpaca_plugins` and

### 1.8 Resolution (S2 adds to the same file)

```rust
/// What a client path resolves to (§3). `project: None` = a root with no
/// folder under projects/ yet — a git repository nobody has used (R12).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ResolvedProject {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub project: Option<Project>,
}
impl ResolvedProject {
    pub fn is_registered(&self) -> bool;     // project.is_some()
    pub fn root_string(&self) -> String;     // root.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
}

/// §3 *Resolve* — pure, creates nothing, no cache. `Ok(None)` = no project.
/// A relative path is `Ok(None)` (R22: never read against the daemon's CWD).
/// Existing path: walk `canonicalize(path)` and its ancestors; at each folder,
/// first `overlaps_home_store` → `Ok(None)` (R13; every further ancestor also
/// contains the home store), then `lookup` → registered root, then
/// `<folder>/.git` exists (directory or file) → unregistered root. Nearest wins.
/// Path that cannot be canonicalized: walk `canonical_root(path)` and its
/// ancestors matching `lookup` only (a missing project resolves to itself).
pub fn resolve(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<ResolvedProject>>;

/// `resolve`, then `register(root)` when the root is unregistered. The one
/// call every registration site makes (§2.2).
pub fn resolve_and_register(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>>;

/// R10, the app's `Use` and `chat --project`: `resolve_and_register(path)`;
/// when that finds nothing, the folder itself — `IsHome` when it overlaps the
/// home store, `NotADirectory` when it is not one, else `register`.
pub fn choose(path: &Path) -> Result<Project>;
```

`GET /v1/workspaces?path=` answers from `resolve` (§6): an unused git repository has `root` set, `id`,
`name` null, `missing: false`.

### 5.1 Re-point (S3)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RepointStep { Marked, RowsRewritten, Renamed, Cleared }   // after §6 steps 1, 2, 3, 4

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]

    pub before: Project,
    pub after: Project,
    pub rows: RebaseCounts,

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RepointInterrupted(pub RepointStep);   // Display "the re-point stopped after {step:?}"; impl Error

/// §6 *Re-point*. Under `projects::lock()` for the whole call: `old_path` must
/// `resolve` to a registered project (else NotRegistered); `new_path`
/// canonicalized must be a directory (NotADirectory), must not overlap the home
/// store (IsHome), must differ from the old root (SamePath), must not be
/// registered nor named by any of the five path columns (Exists, via
/// `ArtifactStore::workspace_rows(new, None)`). Then steps 1–4. A step-2 failure
/// rewrites project.json without the two keys and returns the error.
pub fn repoint(db: &Database, old_path: &Path, new_path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Repointed>;

/// R24's crash hook: `checkpoint` after each step; `false` stops with
/// `RepointInterrupted(step)` and the disk as that step left it.
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn repoint_with(
    db: &Database,
    old_path: &Path,
    new_path: &Path,
    checkpoint: &mut dyn FnMut(RepointStep) -> bool,
) -> anyhow::Result<Repointed>;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecoveryReport {
    pub finished: Vec<PathBuf>,            // the new roots
    pub failed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,    // tried again at the next boot
}
/// R24: every `list()` entry carrying `previous_root` runs steps 2–4 again,
/// each idempotent.
pub fn recover_repoints(db: &Database) -> RecoveryReport;
```

```rust
}
```

`ArtifactStore::workspace_rows` (`:1580`) counts all five. Boot: new `apps/openalpacad/src/bootstrap/repoints.rs`,
`pub fn recover_repoints(db: &Database)` (INFO per finished, WARN per failure naming the project and "tried
again at the next boot"), re-exported from `bootstrap/mod.rs`, called in `main.rs` right after
`info!("Database initialized: {}", ...)` (`main.rs:229`) and before `sweep_interrupted_runs`.

### 5.2 Delete (S5a)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KeptFiles { pub uploads: usize, pub artifacts: usize }   // linked by a surviving conversation (step 1)

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DeletePlan {
    pub project: Project,
    pub counts: PurgeCounts,           // PurgeCounts gains `artifacts: usize` (by-product rows)
    pub kept: KeptFiles,
    pub sessions: Vec<PurgeSession>,   // for the route's live-run guard
    pub memory_partitions: usize,      // snapshots whose project_id is this id
    pub memory_notes: usize,           // note files under <dir>/memory/owners/*/notes/
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct DeleteOutcome {
    pub counts: PurgeCounts,
    pub kept: KeptFiles,
    pub session_ids: Vec<String>,
    pub message_ids: Vec<i64>,
}

/// Reads only. Never iterates storage_path.
pub fn delete_plan(db: &Database, project: &Project) -> anyhow::Result<DeletePlan>;
/// §6 Delete steps 1 and 2: linked files moved to the root store and re-addressed
/// with no project (a kept by-product as its newest version only), then one
/// transaction deleting every row naming the project in the five columns and the
/// rows hanging off its sessions and runs, `learning_cursor` included.
pub fn delete_project_data(db: &Database, project: &Project) -> anyhow::Result<DeleteOutcome>;
/// The last part of step 3, under `projects::lock()`: removes `project.dir`
/// (never through a link). `Ok(false)` when already gone.
pub fn remove_project_folder(project: &Project) -> anyhow::Result<bool>;
```

Route order (S5a), all under `quiesce(&project.id)`: `delete_project_data` → session directories (writers stood
down, as `remove_purged_bytes` does today) → `routes::sessions::forget_conversation_summaries(..)` (`sessions.rs:841`,
before the partitions go) → `MemoryService::remove_project(&project.id)` → `remove_project_folder` →
`session_changed{status:"deleted"}` per session.

### 6.2 The CLI (S5a)

`StoreCommands::{List, Rebase { old, new, dry_run }, Purge { project, dry_run, yes }}` (`--all` gone;
`project` required); its view structs mirror §6.1 field for field (`ProjectView`, `WorkspaceView`,
`RowCounts`, `RepointResult`, `DeleteResult`). `purge`'s `project` is a root, made absolute and sent as written, or
a folder as `store list` prints it, `projects/<name>`, sent as that project's root (`purge_target`, R-S8); the
daemon refuses a path inside a project. `chat --project <dir>`: `POST /v1/workspaces {path}` first,
then every turn's `x-workspace-path` is the answered `root`.

### 8. Choices this sheet made where the spec is open

- `project.json` is not `deny_unknown_fields`; `created_at` is a formatted `String` (one formatter, fixed bytes).
- The registration helper is `resolve_and_register`, one call at every site, so no site resolves twice.
- The register folder is built under a dot-prefixed temp name and renamed into place: the rename is the
  create-if-absent.
- `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY` (422) and `WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED` (500) are the two new codes.
- `rows` gains `messages` and `followups`: the re-point rewrites five columns, and a dry run that showed three
  would under-report.
- The delete answers one project, flat, since `all` is gone.
- `quiesce` retries for 3 s every 100 ms, in the route.
- **`WORKSPACE_BUSY` is not a `ProjectError` variant.** Storage cannot see the lane registry or the memory
  service's slots, so the route composes it from `workspace_rows(..).active_tasks` (re-point) or
  `busy_tasks` (delete), `session_has_live_run`, and a `quiesce` that fails; no slice adds a `Busy` variant.

### 9. Spec conflicts

- **C1 — §16 puts the re-point in (4); the flip in (3) breaks today's PATCH.** Today's re-base finds the store
  by joining `.openalpaca` onto the project (`store/project_move.rs:35-37`, `:58-60`), rewrites `storage_path` by
  the old *project* prefix (`artifacts/mod.rs` `rebase_project`, `:1520`), and re-keys memory through
  `project_of_partition_root`'s `nth(4)` (`partition.rs:2749`). After (3) every one matches nothing: PATCH moves
  the rows, leaves `projects/<old>/` and every `storage_path` behind, and `a_move_re_keys_the_projects_memory_partition`,
  `a_store_still_at_the_old_root_is_moved_after_the_transaction` and the crash test (`workspaces/tests.rs:1450`,
  `:847`, `:1628`) go red until (4) — the sceptic's finding in `panel/digest.txt` (BUILD-1). **Correction:** §6's
  steps 1–4, R24's recovery and the removal of the move machinery's writers land in S3, since they need DB and
  files only and "a re-point touches no snapshot and no index row". S4 keeps the id key, which is what makes
  notes survive a re-point; until S4 a re-point leaves a project's partitions bound to the old folder (unreleased
  commits only), and S4 adds the test that they survive.
- **C2 — the guard cannot be a `cfg(test)` check.** The panel's "one `cfg(test)` check in the register function"
  (`panel/digest.txt`, BUILD-4) compiles only into storage's own test binary; `cargo test -p openalpacad` and
  `-p openalpaca_core` build storage without `cfg(test)`, so BUILD-4's files would never meet it.
  **Correction:** the `test-home-guard` feature of §1.7 (the `openalpaca_mcp` `test-utils` pattern).
  `cfg(debug_assertions)` is not it either: `cargo run -p openalpacad` is a debug build with no override.
- **C3 — §7 removes `project_root_of` "(no caller)".** R15 needs exactly what it does (`store/mod.rs:568`: the one
  place a scope becomes a stored address) at `artifacts/mod.rs:914` and `uploads/mod.rs:220`. **Correction:** keep
  it; remove `project_root_at` only.
- **C4 — registration sites.** §3 names a chat turn, an upload, a memory write through a route and choosing a
  folder. A run dispatched with no turn of its own — `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/rerun` of a project only an earlier
  build's rows name — would write artifacts under an unregistered root and meet R12's error (`tasks.rs:850` →
  `dispatch_lead_agent_inner`, `lead_agent.rs:212`). **Correction:** the dispatch registers too (§2.2 row 2). Sites
  1 and 2 are core code; the gateway and the dispatcher run only in the daemon, so "only the daemon" holds by
  process.
- **C5 — §7 says fixtures 03, 04 and 17 are rewritten; seven more mention the marker.** 01, 07, 08, 09 and 24
  declare `"marker": ".openalpaca"`, 02's prose names the folder, and `README.md` documents both. After S2 a
  `.openalpaca` directory resolves to nothing. **Correction:** §7.3.
- **C6 — §5 lists `memory/.gitignore`'s removal under Memory.** Fixture 03 asserts that file
  (`03-git-repo-lazy-partition.json`, `notes_for_implementer`), and the flip rewrites 03. **Correction:** S3 removes it.
- **C7 — §16 puts the guard audit in (3); the guard bites in (2).** `register` is first called from S2's sites, so
  every test that drives a turn with a project panics in S2 without its guard. **Correction:** §7.4 splits the
  audit by what the test reaches.
- **C8 — `GET ?path=` reads `<root>/.openalpaca/.layout` until S5a** (`workspaces.rs:342-357`), against ST-9, in the
  commits between S3 and S5a. Not corrected: those commits are never released; S5a removes the read with
  `recorded_project_root`. Recorded so no drafter "fixes" it twice.

### 11. As built (the final fix wave, 2026-10-08)

Recorded by S6.6 once Stage 1 was built (`b8b768b6^..44d53783`): the whole-stage review's fix wave and its residual
pass (`b923c81e..909e724c`) changed these contracts — the numbers below are that review's findings (R1…R33)
and the residual pass's (X1…X10), not the design's rulings. The sections above are the contract the slices were drafted
against and stay as written; the design's rev 0.9 (§3, §5, §9 *As built*, §18) records the behaviour.

- **§1.7 and §7.4 — the guard is a backstop** (S1's fix round, `ecfd8db3`). `register` reads `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE`
  and the user's home once (`register_home`); the guard judges that reading as written and where it leads (a link, a
  `..`, another case), and every read and write of the call is under that one store, so no test can pass the check
  and then write into `<HOME>/.openalpaca`. Detection stays probabilistic: an unguarded test that calls `register`
  while another test of its crate holds that crate's guard passes the check and writes into that test's temp store,
  unreported; a `~/.openalpaca` that is itself a link, with the variable set to the link's target, is not recognised
  as the real store, because the guard resolves the user's home and appends `.openalpaca` rather than read the real
  store, not even its metadata. The audit, not the panic, is what makes a test guarded: every test that resolves,
  registers or lists projects holds its crate's guard.
- **§1.4 — `ProjectError::RepointUnfinished { path }`**, a sixth variant: code `WORKSPACE_EXISTS`, `409` on the wire;
  its sentence names the next start of the daemon, which finishes that re-point (X7). The re-point refuses with it a
  target that is an unfinished re-point's new or old root, before `Exists` (R9).
- **§1.5 — two readers.** `projects::by_recorded_root(root)`: the project whose recorded root is `root` as written,
  compared component by component, nothing resolved, an entry mid re-point never the answer (R1; the routes trim the
  path and strip a trailing `/` first). `projects::unfinished_repoint_at(root)`: a marked project recording `root` as
  its new or its old root (R9, R11). `read_project_dir` answers `Ok(None)` for a folder or a `project.json` that
  vanishes while it is read, and `list` and `by_id` pass it over (R2).
- **`store::create_below(base, rel)`** (`pub(crate)`): creates `rel` below `base` one level at a time, accepts an
  existing level only when it is a real directory, never creates `base`, and answers `NotFound` when `base` is gone.
  `content_dir` for a project scope, the upload writer and the artifact writer (the leaf and the `.versions`
  rotation) use it, and the memory files through `memory_files::fsx` (R16, R-F3).
- **§5.1 — the re-point.** `repoint_rows` takes an `InFlightRuns` (`openalpaca_storage::artifacts::InFlightRuns`,
  not re-exported at the crate root): the live re-point counts the runs `queued`, `running` or `paused` under the old
  root inside step 2's transaction and refuses with `project_life::RunsInFlight` (`409 WORKSPACE_BUSY`), the delete's
  error, now the `PATCH`'s too; recovery does not count, since it runs before the interrupted runs are swept (R10). A
  step-2 failure whose marker could not be cleared carries `project_life::RepointLeftMarked`, and the route answers
  it `500 WORKSPACE_MOVE_FAILED` with the whole chain, never "nothing was re-pointed" (X3). `project_life::registered`
  matches a recorded root first and propagates a listing failure (R1, X1).
- **§5.2 — the delete.** `KeptRow` carries the version it was copied at, and the transaction refuses a kept file whose
  row changed since, its version or its address (R18); `copy_fresh` never overwrites a kept file a committed row
  names (S5a's re-review); `remove_project` and `remove_project_folder` run straight after `delete_project_data`, and
  the folder's removal takes `project.json` last (R16, R3).
- **§6.1 — the routes.** A recorded root sent as written is matched before anything is resolved, and `GET ?path=`
  answers it as sent (R1). A marked project at either path is `409 WORKSPACE_BUSY` naming the next start (R11). Once
  the memory slot is held, the re-point and the delete read the project again by id (`still_the_project`) and answer
  `409 WORKSPACE_BUSY`, "nothing was re-pointed / deleted", if it was re-pointed or deleted meanwhile (R15).
  `RunsInFlight` is the `PATCH`'s too, and its pre-check counts queued runs beside running and paused ones (R10).
  `GET ?path=`, `PATCH` and the purge answer `500 IO_ERROR` when `projects/` cannot be listed (X1). A delete that kept
  the folder counts only the notes that went (R26), and a real delete's plan lines are built from its counts (S5a M1).
- **§4.4 — memory writes.** `MemoryService::store` refuses a write whose effective scope is the project when the
  context's root no longer looks up (`MemoryAccessContext`'s stale root) or resolved to an unregistered root:
  `MemoryError::Internal`, one sentence, `500 MEMORY_INTERNAL` on `POST /v1/memories`; learning's and the episode's
  existing `Internal` arms hold the cursor (R19, closing R5 and R13's memory half). A conversation's close checks its
  project before its refresh reads the forgets (R20). The handler is handed the root the gateway recorded
  (`HandleRequest.workspace_path`, R7).
- **§4.5 — ST-21's check.** `extractor::check_project` runs under `projects::lock()` (R2);
  `learning::queue::check_project_now` (`pub(crate)`) runs it on the blocking pool, and task extraction calls it there
  too — the learning module no longer re-exports `check_project` (X5). The 30 s reconciliation logs a project root
  that names no project at debug (X6).
- **§6.3 — the app.** `qk.followups.all()` joins the project-data invalidation set (R24). `oa-project` holds
  `{root, id}` — a root-only value an earlier build wrote migrates with `id: null` — and `useProjectFollow` follows the
  project by id to the root a re-point made elsewhere, reading a fresh list (R22, X8). `Delete data…` and `Re-point…`
  refuse a plan or a count the daemon read as another project, and `Re-point…` stays off while runs are running or
  queued (R1, X2). An upload into a bound conversation carries that conversation's `workspace_id` (R6).

## Stage 1 plan — slice S1: `store::projects`, additive, plus the test-build guard

Draft for the Stage 1 plan. Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`; the commit after `6aecb614` is the other
session's `wait_for_subagents` fix in `runner/lead_agent/`, which S1 does not touch). Every `file:line` is from that
commit. The spec is `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8: §1–§3, §16 Stage 1 step (1)); the shared names, types and
signatures are `interfaces.md` §1, followed except where *Spec conflicts* says otherwise (§7.4 only for what *Open
points* hands to S2 and S3).

### What this slice does

It adds one module, `openalpaca_storage::store::projects`, and nothing calls it yet. The module computes a project's
folder name under `~/.openalpaca/projects/` from its canonical root (R4–R8), reads and writes that folder's
`project.json` (R9), finds a project by its root in two small reads (`lookup`), lists every project (`list`,
`by_id`), and creates a project's folder under one process-wide lock (`register`). A folder it cannot read, or two
folders carrying one id, is never opened and never deleted, and is reported once at WARN (R11). A folder under
`projects/` holds `project.json` and nothing else when `register` makes it (R3). The slice also adds the owner's
backstop: in a test build, `register` panics when the home store was not set through `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE`, or was
set into the developer's real store. The check is compiled into storage's own tests and, through a `test-home-guard`
feature turned on in five crates' `[dev-dependencies]`, into their test builds, and into no release or `cargo run`
build. Nothing in S1 calls `register`, so no existing test's behaviour changes and none writes anywhere new (S1.7
widens `HomeStoreGuard` and S1.9 appends one test to five files); the audit of which guard
each project-path test holds is S2's and S3's (spec §16 (3), `interfaces.md` §7.4 and C7), and what this draft found
for it is handed over under *Open points*. R1 (`projects/` is the user's) is stated in the module's
documentation; R2 (the `ContentKind` shrink and the home README's rows) is S6's, as `interfaces.md` §0 and §7.1 assign
it (*Spec conflicts*, first item).

### Rules every task follows

- **One cargo process at a time.** Each step names one `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`; never `--workspace`.
- **No test touches `~/.openalpaca`.** Every test here that reaches a home store holds storage's
  `crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard` (`store/tests.rs:16`), directly or through the `World` helper of S1.3. The
  guard test of S1.7 also moves `HOME` to a temp directory, so even a guard that failed to fire could write nothing
  into the real store.
- **No `&s[..n]` string cut.** The one cut in this slice is `String::truncate` at `str::floor_char_boundary`, which
  core already calls on the pinned 1.93.0 (`crates/openalpaca_core/src/memory/learning/episode.rs:195`).
- **`std::env::set_var` only under the crate's env lock**, inside `HomeStoreGuard`, with a `SAFETY` comment.
- **Anchored edits.** Every edit to an existing file names the exact text it replaces; that text occurs once. Use the
  Edit tool or a Python script that asserts one match — never BSD `sed -i`.
- **Test names** are snake_case sentences.
- **Formatting.** Before each commit, run `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the files this slice creates
  (`store/projects.rs`, which also formats `store/projects/tests.rs`) and on the two existing files it edits that are
  rustfmt-clean at `32292608`: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/memory_files/fsx.rs` and
  `crates/openalpaca_core/src/test_util.rs`. Five other files it edits already carry formatting drift at `32292608`
  — `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file> | grep -c '^Diff in'` gives `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/tests.rs`
  2, `apps/openalpacad/src/test_util.rs` 1, `apps/openalpaca/src/test_util.rs` 1,
  `crates/openalpaca_plugins/src/permission_gate/tests.rs` 5, `crates/openalpaca_connectors/src/common/tests.rs` 3:
  never run rustfmt on those (it would reformat code the task did not touch); insert the code exactly as written
  below and check that the same command gives the same count after the edit, with no `Diff in` line inside the
  inserted lines. Never run it on `store/mod.rs` or `memory_files/mod.rs` either: rustfmt follows `mod` declarations
  and would reformat sibling modules the task did not touch. The code below is written in rustfmt's style, but
  rustfmt decides for the files it formats; `git status` must then list only the task's files.
- **Commits** use a conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line, and end with
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git add` names explicit paths only (another agent may
  commit in `crates/openalpaca_core/src/runner/lead_agent/` meanwhile).
- **No generated doc changes.** S1 adds no top-level module and no `lib.rs` re-export, so
  `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check` stays clean (the slice gate runs it).

The expected counts below are for macOS and Linux; on a platform without `cfg(unix)` the symlink tests are not
compiled and the counts are lower by the number of `#[cfg(unix)]` tests named in each step.

```rust
//! A project's folder in the home store (storage design rev 0.8, Stage 1:
//! ST-1, ST-3…ST-6, ST-13; the lead's rulings R1…R13).
//!
//! `<home>/projects/<name>/` holds one project's content — `artifacts/`,
//! `uploads/`, `memory/` — beside its `project.json`, which records the
//! project's permanent id and its canonical root path. `projects/` is the
//! user's, like everything at the home root but `state/` (R1), and a folder
//! under it holds `project.json` and content directories, nothing else (R3).
//!
//! There is no registry object (§3): these are functions over the files under
//! the **current** home root, read on demand, so the daemon, the CLI and the
//! app's shell agree and a test's `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` holds. The file
//! decides whose folder it is, never the name (R6), and a name is never
//! parsed back into a path (R8).

use std::fmt;
use std::str::FromStr;

use uuid::Uuid;

/// `<home>/projects` — one folder per project (ST-1). Not a
/// [`super::ContentKind`]: it exists only at the home root, and
/// `content_dir(scope, kind)` stays `root/<kind>`.
pub const PROJECTS_DIR: &str = "projects";

/// The file in a project's folder that says whose folder it is (R9).
pub const PROJECT_FILE: &str = "project.json";

/// The one `version` this build reads and writes; any other reads as
/// unreadable (R11).
pub const PROJECT_FILE_VERSION: u32 = 1;

/// R7: a plain name longer than this is cut at a character boundary and
/// always hashed.
pub const NAME_MAX_BYTES: usize = 200;

/// R6: `<plain>-<8 hex of sha256(the canonical path)>`.
pub const NAME_HASH_HEX: usize = 8;

// ============================================================================
// Identity (ST-13)
// ============================================================================

/// A project's permanent id (ST-13): a v4 UUID, written and read only in its
/// canonical hyphenated lowercase form — `NoteId::parse`'s rule
/// (`memory_files/note.rs`), copied rather than shared, so neither id can
/// drift into the other's meaning.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct ProjectId(Uuid);

impl ProjectId {
    /// A fresh v4 id.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self(Uuid::new_v4())
    }

    /// Strict: only the canonical hyphenated lowercase spelling is an id.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let uuid = Uuid::parse_str(s).map_err(|e| format!("`{s}` is not a UUID: {e}"))?;
        if uuid.hyphenated().to_string() != s {
            return Err(format!(
                "`{s}` is not the canonical hyphenated lowercase form of a UUID"
            ));
        }
        Ok(Self(uuid))
    }

    pub fn as_uuid(&self) -> &Uuid {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl Default for ProjectId {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ProjectId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.0.hyphenated())
    }
}

impl FromStr for ProjectId {
    type Err = String;
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        Self::parse(s)
    }
}

impl serde::Serialize for ProjectId {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.serialize_str(&self.to_string())
    }
}

impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for ProjectId {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        ProjectId::parse(&s).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

```rust
#[test]
fn a_folder_name_is_the_root_with_every_other_character_a_dash() {
    // R5's table, as the design writes it.
    for (root, name) in [
        (
            "/Users/tangyunpei/dev/AlpacaLink",
            "-Users-tangyunpei-dev-AlpacaLink",
        ),
        ("/Users/tangyunpei/dev/my_app", "-Users-tangyunpei-dev-my-app"),
        ("/Users/tangyunpei/文档/笔记", "-Users-tangyunpei-文档-笔记"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(folder_name(Path::new(root)), name, "{root}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn runs_of_other_characters_are_not_collapsed() {
    assert_eq!(folder_name(Path::new("/srv/a b/.c_d")), "-srv-a-b--c-d");
}

#[test]
fn a_folder_name_is_nfc_and_keeps_combining_marks() {
    // `e` + U+0301 composes to `é` (U+00E9) …
    assert_eq!(folder_name(Path::new("/srv/cafe\u{301}")), "-srv-caf\u{e9}");
    // … and a mark with nothing to compose with stays, as a mark.
    assert_eq!(folder_name(Path::new("/srv/x\u{301}")), "-srv-x\u{301}");
    // Devanagari: the virama (U+094D) is a mark and not a letter, and the
    // word is not whole without it (R5).
    let hindi = "\u{939}\u{93F}\u{928}\u{94D}\u{926}\u{940}";
    assert!(!'\u{94D}'.is_alphanumeric(), "the case this test exists for");
    assert_eq!(
        folder_name(Path::new(&format!("/home/{hindi}"))),
        format!("-home-{hindi}")
    );
}

#[test]
fn two_roots_with_one_plain_name_have_two_hashed_names() {
    let (underscore, dash) = (Path::new("/a/b_c"), Path::new("/a/b-c"));
    assert_eq!(folder_name(underscore), "-a-b-c");
    assert_eq!(folder_name(dash), "-a-b-c");
    // R6: <plain>-<8 hex of sha256(the canonical path)>.
    assert_eq!(hashed_folder_name(underscore), "-a-b-c-df04c200");
    assert_eq!(hashed_folder_name(dash), "-a-b-c-693a1a8d");

    let decomposed = Path::new("/srv/cafe\u{301}");

    assert_eq!(folder_name(decomposed), folder_name(composed));
    assert_eq!(hashed_folder_name(decomposed), "-srv-caf\u{e9}-559b2d05");
    assert_eq!(hashed_folder_name(composed), "-srv-caf\u{e9}-9e472a79");

fn a_cut_never_splits_a_character() {

    assert_eq!(name, format!("-{}-479c5867", "文".repeat(66)));
    assert_eq!(name.len(), 199 + 1 + NAME_HASH_HEX);
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// Folder names (R4…R8)
// ============================================================================

/// The folder name of a project root (R4, R5, R7). Pure; the caller passes
/// the **canonical** root (R4), and nothing ever parses a name back into a
/// path (R8).
///
/// The path is normalized to NFC; a character that is a Unicode letter,
/// digit or combining mark is kept — marks because a Thai or Devanagari word
/// is not whole without them — and every other character becomes one `-`,
/// runs not collapsed (R5): `/Users/me/dev/my_app` is `-Users-me-dev-my-app`.
/// A name longer than [`NAME_MAX_BYTES`] is cut at the last character
/// boundary at or below it and always given [`hashed_folder_name`]'s suffix
/// (R7).
pub fn folder_name(root: &Path) -> String {
    name_parts(root).0
}

/// The name a project takes when its plain name belongs to another folder
/// (R6): `<folder_name>-<the first NAME_HASH_HEX hex of sha256(root)>`, the
/// hash over the canonical path as the volume spells it, not its NFC form. A
/// name R7 already cut carries the suffix and is returned as it is.
pub fn hashed_folder_name(root: &Path) -> String {
    match name_parts(root) {
        (name, true) => name,
        (name, false) => format!("{name}-{}", path_hash(root)),
    }
}

/// The folder name, and whether R7 already gave it the hash suffix.
fn name_parts(root: &Path) -> (String, bool) {
    let written = root.to_string_lossy();
    let mut name: String = written
        .nfc()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_alphanumeric() || is_combining_mark(c) {
                c
            } else {
                '-'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if name.len() <= NAME_MAX_BYTES {
        return (name, false);
    }
    let end = name.floor_char_boundary(NAME_MAX_BYTES);
    name.truncate(end);
    name.push('-');
    name.push_str(&path_hash(root));
    (name, true)
}

/// The first [`NAME_HASH_HEX`] hex characters of SHA-256 over the root as
/// written — truncated, never cut with a byte range.
fn path_hash(root: &Path) -> String {
    let mut hash = crate::memory_files::sha256_hex(root.to_string_lossy().as_bytes());
    hash.truncate(NAME_HASH_HEX);
    hash
}
```

```rust
/// The canonical path of a directory that may not exist yet: the deepest
/// existing ancestor is canonicalized and the missing tail is appended as
/// written. A lazy partition therefore derives the same key before and after
/// it is created, and the caller has already refused any link on the way.
/// A missing tail that ends in `..` has no file name, so the walk refuses it
/// rather than leave a `..` in the answer.
pub(crate) fn canonical_path_lenient(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let mut existing: &Path = path;
    let mut tail: Vec<&std::ffi::OsStr> = Vec::new();
    while !existing.exists() {
        let name = existing
            .file_name()
            .with_context(|| format!("path has no existing ancestor: {}", path.display()))?;
        tail.push(name);
        existing = existing
            .parent()
            .with_context(|| format!("path has no existing ancestor: {}", path.display()))?;
    }
    let mut result = existing
        .canonicalize()
        .with_context(|| format!("failed to canonicalize {}", existing.display()))?;
    for component in tail.into_iter().rev() {
        result.push(component);
    }
    Ok(result)
}

/// [`canonical_path_lenient`] as the string a partition key and a snapshot's
/// `root` are derived from.
pub(crate) fn canonical_string_lenient(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {
    Ok(canonical_path_lenient(path)?.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
}
```

```rust
use std::fmt;
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// Roots (R4, R13)
// ============================================================================

/// The canonical form of a project root that may not exist: the deepest
/// existing ancestor canonicalized — links resolved, the volume's own
/// spelling — and the missing tail appended as written
/// (`fsx::canonical_path_lenient`). A relative path is refused before
/// anything is read: `Path::exists` and `canonicalize` would resolve it
/// against the process's working directory, which would make the daemon's
/// CWD a project (R22).
pub fn canonical_root(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    if !path.is_absolute() {
        bail!(
            "a project root must be an absolute path, got {}",
            path.display()
        );
    }
    fsx::canonical_path_lenient(path)
}

/// R13, which replaces `resolves_to_the_home_store` in S2: whether `root` is
/// the home store, lies inside it, or contains it — never a project, so
/// `$HOME` stays "no project" even with a `~/.git`. Both sides canonical, so a
/// link to the home store answers for the store it reaches. `false` when
/// there is no usable home root or `root` is relative: a question, never a
/// reason to fail.
pub fn overlaps_home_store(root: &Path) -> bool {
    let Ok(root) = canonical_root(root) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Ok(home) = super::home_root().and_then(|home| canonical_root(&home)) else {
        return false;
    };
    root.starts_with(&home) || home.starts_with(&root)
}
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// The file and the entry (R9)
// ============================================================================

/// `projects/<name>/project.json` exactly as R9 writes it: the authority for
/// the project's identity (there is no project table, R14). Not
/// `deny_unknown_fields`: "no readable project.json" (R11) means unparseable
/// or another `version`, never "a newer build added a key".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProjectFile {
    /// [`PROJECT_FILE_VERSION`]; any other reads as unreadable (R11).
    pub version: u32,
    pub id: ProjectId,
    /// The canonical root — the string the rows hold (R4, R14).
    pub root: String,
    /// RFC 3339, UTC, whole seconds: `2026-10-07T09:30:00Z`.
    pub created_at: String,
    /// Set only while a re-point is in flight (§6, R24).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub previous_root: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub previous_name: Option<String>,
}

/// One project as its folder records it — what `lookup`, `list` and `by_id`
/// return.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Project {
    pub id: ProjectId,
    /// [`ProjectFile::root`].
    pub root: PathBuf,
    /// The folder's name under `projects/`.
    pub name: String,
    /// The folder, canonical: what `store_root` answers for the project (S3)
    /// and the prefix every stored `storage_path` under it starts with.
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    pub created_at: String,
    /// The root is not a directory, read when this entry was read (ST-7).
    pub missing: bool,
    /// `Some` only mid re-point (§6).
    pub previous_root: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub previous_name: Option<String>,
}

impl Project {
    /// The root as the five path columns hold it.
    pub fn root_string(&self) -> String {
        self.root.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
    }

    /// The file this entry was read from, for a rewrite (§6 steps 1 and 4).
    pub fn file(&self) -> ProjectFile {
        ProjectFile {
            version: PROJECT_FILE_VERSION,
            id: self.id,
            root: self.root_string(),
            created_at: self.created_at.clone(),
            previous_root: self
                .previous_root
                .as_ref()
                .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
            previous_name: self.previous_name.clone(),
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Refusals (R12, R13, ST-20)
// ============================================================================

/// Why a project operation was refused — returned **inside** `anyhow::Error`
/// (the `ArtifactError` convention, `artifacts/mod.rs`), recovered with
/// `downcast_ref`. `Display` is one sentence a person can act on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ProjectError {
    /// R12: a root with no folder under `projects/`. `store_root` returns it (S3).
    NotRegistered { root: String },
    /// R13: the path is the home store, inside it, or contains it.
    IsHome { path: String },
    /// The path does not exist or is not a directory (register, choose,
    /// re-point target).
    NotADirectory { path: String },
    /// ST-20: the re-point target is already a project, or one of the five
    /// path columns names it.
    Exists { path: String },
    /// A re-point onto the path the project already has.
    SamePath { path: String },
}

impl ProjectError {
    /// The wire code the daemon answers with (S3, S5a).
    pub fn code(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::NotRegistered { .. } => "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND",
            Self::IsHome { .. } => "WORKSPACE_IS_HOME",
            Self::NotADirectory { .. } => "WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY",
            Self::Exists { .. } => "WORKSPACE_EXISTS",
            Self::SamePath { .. } => "INVALID_PATH",
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for ProjectError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::NotRegistered { root } => write!(
                f,
                "{root} is not a project OpenAlpaca knows: no folder under projects/ records it"
            ),
            Self::IsHome { path } => write!(
                f,
                "{path} is, contains or lies inside the OpenAlpaca home store, so it cannot be a \
                 project. Name the project directory itself"
            ),
            Self::NotADirectory { path } => write!(
                f,
                "{path} is not a directory. Create it first, or name the folder the project is in now"
            ),
            Self::Exists { path } => write!(
                f,
                "{path} is already a project of its own, or OpenAlpaca's records already name it. \
                 Re-pointing onto it would merge two projects: delete that project's data first, \
                 or re-point onto another path"
            ),
            Self::SamePath { path } => write!(f, "{path} is already where the project is"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for ProjectError {}

/// Whether `e`, anywhere in its chain, is [`ProjectError::NotRegistered`] —
/// how a reader learns after the fact that a root is unregistered (R12).
/// Chain-aware, so a `.context(..)` a caller adds never hides it.
pub fn is_not_registered(e: &anyhow::Error) -> bool {
    e.chain().any(|cause| {
        matches!(
            cause.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>(),
            Some(ProjectError::NotRegistered { .. })
        )
    })
}
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// Reading (§3, R9, R11)
// ============================================================================

/// `home_root()/projects`. A path query: creates nothing.
pub fn projects_dir() -> Result<PathBuf> {
    Ok(super::home_root()?.join(PROJECTS_DIR))
}

/// §3 *lookup*: the project registered at `root`, or `None`. Two small
/// reads, no scan and no lock: `projects/<folder_name>/project.json` and,
/// when that is absent, unreadable or records another root,
/// `projects/<hashed_folder_name>/project.json`. Creates nothing. A folder
/// with no readable file is passed over with one WARN per folder per process
/// (R11). An error is a relative `root`, no home root, or a folder that
/// cannot be resolved.
pub fn lookup(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>> {
    let root = canonical_root(root)?;
    let want = root.to_string_lossy();
    let projects = projects_dir()?;
    let plain = folder_name(&root);
    let hashed = hashed_folder_name(&root);
    let names = if hashed == plain {
        vec![plain]
    } else {
        vec![plain, hashed]
    };
    for name in names {
        if let Some(project) = read_project_dir(&projects.join(name))?
            && project.root_string() == want.as_ref()
        {
            return Ok(Some(project));
        }
    }
    Ok(None)
}

/// The project a folder under `projects/` records, or `None`: no folder
/// there, or one OpenAlpaca does not open (R11) — a link, a file, no
/// `project.json`, a `project.json` that is a link, has another hard link, is
/// not one this build parses, has another `version`, or records a root that is
/// not absolute. Each of those is one WARN per folder per process, and
/// nothing is deleted.
pub(crate) fn read_project_dir(dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>> {
    match fs::symlink_metadata(dir) {
        Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() => {
            return Ok(unreadable(dir, "it is a symbolic link"));
        }
        Ok(meta) if !meta.is_dir() => return Ok(unreadable(dir, "it is not a directory")),
        Ok(_) => {}
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
        Err(e) => return Ok(unreadable(dir, &format!("it cannot be read ({e})"))),
    }
    let bytes = match fsx::read_if_exists(&dir.join(PROJECT_FILE)) {
        Ok(Some(bytes)) => bytes,
        Ok(None) => return Ok(unreadable(dir, "it has no project.json")),
        Err(e) => {
            return Ok(unreadable(
                dir,
                &format!("its project.json cannot be read ({e:#})"),
            ));
        }
    };
    let file: ProjectFile = match serde_json::from_slice(&bytes) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(e) => {
            return Ok(unreadable(
                dir,
                &format!("its project.json is not one this build reads ({e})"),
            ));
        }
    };
    if file.version != PROJECT_FILE_VERSION {
        return Ok(unreadable(
            dir,
            &format!(
                "its project.json has version {}, and this build reads version {PROJECT_FILE_VERSION}",
                file.version
            ),
        ));
    }
    if !Path::new(&file.root).is_absolute() {
        return Ok(unreadable(
            dir,
            &format!(
                "its project.json records a root that is not an absolute path ({:?})",
                file.root
            ),
        ));
    }
    let name = dir
        .file_name()
        .with_context(|| format!("{} names no folder", dir.display()))?
        .to_string_lossy()
        .into_owned();
    let dir = dir
        .canonicalize()
        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to resolve {}", dir.display()))?;
    let root = PathBuf::from(&file.root);
    Ok(Some(Project {
        id: file.id,
        missing: !root.is_dir(),
        root,
        name,
        dir,
        created_at: file.created_at,
        previous_root: file.previous_root.map(PathBuf::from),
        previous_name: file.previous_name,
    }))
}

/// R11's report for `dir`, the first time this process meets it; always
/// `None`, so a reader can return it.
fn unreadable(dir: &Path, why: &str) -> Option<Project> {
    if first_warning(format!("unreadable {}", dir.display())) {
        tracing::warn!(
            "{} is not opened as a project: {why}. OpenAlpaca leaves the folder as it is and never deletes it",
            dir.display()
        );
    }
    None
}

/// What this process has already reported (R11: "reported once at WARN").
static WARNED: Mutex<BTreeSet<String>> = Mutex::new(BTreeSet::new());

/// `true` the first time this process sees `key`.
fn first_warning(key: String) -> bool {
    WARNED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).insert(key)
}
```

```rust
    // A folder `register` is still building, a link, and a stray file.
    w.plant(".-half-built.1-0.tmp", &file_for(&w.folder("half")));
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&kept, w.projects().join("a-link")).unwrap();
    fs::write(w.projects().join("notes.txt"), "mine").unwrap();

    let names: Vec<String> = list().unwrap().into_iter().map(|p| p.name).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, vec![folder_name(&root)]);
}

fn two_folders_with_one_id_are_both_left_out_and_reported_once() {
    let w = World::new();
    let root = w.folder("copied");
    let file = file_for(&root);
    let original = w.plant(&folder_name(&root), &file);
    let copy = w.plant("copy-of-it", &file);
    let other_root = w.folder("other");
    let other = file_for(&other_root);

    for _ in 0..2 {
        let ids: Vec<ProjectId> = list().unwrap().into_iter().map(|p| p.id).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, vec![other.id]);
    }
    assert_eq!(by_id(&file.id).unwrap(), None);
    assert!(original.join(PROJECT_FILE).exists() && copy.join(PROJECT_FILE).exists());
    let id = file.id.to_string();
    logs_assert(move |lines: &[&str]| {
        let n = lines
            .iter()
            .filter(|l| l.contains("WARN") && l.contains(&id))
            .count();
        if n == 1 {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(format!("one WARN for the shared id, got {n}"))
        }
    });

fn an_entry_mid_re_point_is_listed_with_where_it_was() {
    let w = World::new();
    let (old, new) = (w.folder("old"), w.folder("new"));
    let mut file = file_for(&new);
    file.previous_root = Some(old.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    file.previous_name = Some(folder_name(&old));
    w.plant(&folder_name(&old), &file);

    let listed = list().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(listed.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(listed[0].root, new);
    assert_eq!(listed[0].previous_root.as_deref(), Some(old.as_path()));
    assert_eq!(

        Some(folder_name(&old).as_str())
    );
    assert_eq!(listed[0].file(), file);
```
