```rust
// ============================================================================
// Listing (§3, R11)
// ============================================================================

/// §3 *list*: every project whose folder under `projects/` this build reads,
/// sorted by folder name; entries mid re-point included (R24 reads them).
/// Dot-prefixed names — a folder `register` is still building — links and
/// files are passed over without a word. A missing `projects/` is an empty
/// list, and nothing is created. Two folders carrying one id — a copied
/// folder — are both left out with one WARN (R11): neither can be told from
/// the other, so neither is opened, and neither is deleted.
pub fn list() -> Result<Vec<Project>> {
    let projects = projects_dir()?;
    let entries = match fs::read_dir(&projects) {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(Vec::new()),
        Err(e) => {
            return Err(e).with_context(|| format!("Failed to read {}", projects.display()));
        }
    };
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for entry in entries {
        let entry = entry.with_context(|| format!("Failed to read {}", projects.display()))?;
        if entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().starts_with('.') {
            continue;
        }
        // `DirEntry::file_type` does not follow a link, so a link is passed
        // over here, like a file.
        if !entry.file_type().is_ok_and(|kind| kind.is_dir()) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(project) = read_project_dir(&entry.path())? {
            found.push(project);
        }
    }

    let mut dirs_by_id: BTreeMap<ProjectId, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for project in &found {
        dirs_by_id
            .entry(project.id)
            .or_default()
            .push(project.dir.display().to_string());
    }
    let mut shared = BTreeSet::new();
    for (id, mut dirs) in dirs_by_id {
        if dirs.len() < 2 {
            continue;
        }
        dirs.sort();
        if first_warning(format!("shared id {id}")) {
            tracing::warn!(
                "{} carry the same project id {id}, as a copied folder does; none of them is \
                 opened as a project, and none is deleted",
                dirs.join(" and ")
            );
        }
        shared.insert(id);
    }
    found.retain(|project| !shared.contains(&project.id));
    found.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
    Ok(found)
}

/// [`list`] narrowed to one id: `None` when no folder carries it, or when two
/// do (R11).
pub fn by_id(id: &ProjectId) -> Result<Option<Project>> {
    Ok(list()?.into_iter().find(|project| project.id == *id))
}
```

```rust
/// The message a call panicked with, or `None` when it returned.
fn panic_of(f: impl FnOnce()) -> Option<String> {
    std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(f))
        .err()
        .map(|payload| {
            payload
                .downcast_ref::<String>()
                .cloned()
                .or_else(|| payload.downcast_ref::<&str>().map(|s| s.to_string()))
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// The test-build guard (§3, last bullet)
// ============================================================================

/// Whether this build refuses to register under an unguarded home store:
/// storage's own tests, and the test builds of the crates that enable
/// `test-home-guard` through their `[dev-dependencies]`. Never a release or
/// `cargo run` build.
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn test_home_guard_armed() -> bool {
    cfg!(any(test, feature = "test-home-guard"))
}

/// Why a test build may not write under the home store it would use, or
/// `None`: the store must have been set through `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE`, and
/// not into the developer's own store. `set` is the variable;
/// `default_store` is `<user home>/.openalpaca`, `home_root`'s fallback.
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-home-guard"))]
fn unguarded_home(
    set: Option<&std::ffi::OsStr>,
    default_store: Option<&Path>,
) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match set {
        None => Some("unset"),
        Some(value) if default_store.is_some_and(|real| Path::new(value).starts_with(real)) => {
            Some("pointing into the real home store")
        }
        Some(_) => None,
    }
}

/// The owner's rule that no test writes into a developer's real store:
/// panics, before anything is read or written, in a test build whose home
/// store was not set through `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` or was set into the real
/// one.
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-home-guard"))]
fn refuse_unguarded_test_home() {
    let set = std::env::var_os(super::HOME_STORE_ENV);
    let default_store =
        directories::BaseDirs::new().map(|b| b.home_dir().join(super::STORE_DIR_NAME));
    if let Some(why) = unguarded_home(set.as_deref(), default_store.as_deref()) {
        panic!(
            "store::projects::register in a test build with {} {why}: take the crate's \
             home-store guard (HomeStoreGuard; EnvSandbox in the CLI) first, so no test writes \
             into the developer's ~/.openalpaca. A daemon binary `cargo test` built carries this \
             check too: rebuild it with `cargo build -p openalpacad` before running it by hand",
            super::HOME_STORE_ENV,
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
pub(crate) struct HomeStoreGuard {
    _lock: MutexGuard<'static, ()>,
    prev: Option<OsString>,
}

impl HomeStoreGuard {
    pub(crate) fn set(path: &Path) -> Self {
        let lock = ENV_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let prev = std::env::var_os(HOME_STORE_ENV);
        // SAFETY: serialized by ENV_LOCK; every test that reads the variable
        // holds the same guard.
        unsafe { std::env::set_var(HOME_STORE_ENV, path) };
        Self { _lock: lock, prev }
    }
}

impl Drop for HomeStoreGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: as above — still holding ENV_LOCK.
        match self.prev.take() {
            Some(v) => unsafe { std::env::set_var(HOME_STORE_ENV, v) },
            None => unsafe { std::env::remove_var(HOME_STORE_ENV) },
        }
    }
}
```

  with

```rust
pub(crate) struct HomeStoreGuard {
    _lock: MutexGuard<'static, ()>,
    prev: Option<OsString>,
    /// `HOME` as it was, when [`HomeStoreGuard::for_user_home`] moved it.
    prev_home: Option<Option<OsString>>,
}

impl HomeStoreGuard {
    pub(crate) fn set(path: &Path) -> Self {
        let lock = ENV_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let prev = std::env::var_os(HOME_STORE_ENV);
        // SAFETY: serialized by ENV_LOCK; every test that reads the variable
        // holds the same guard.
        unsafe { std::env::set_var(HOME_STORE_ENV, path) };
        Self {
            _lock: lock,
            prev,
            prev_home: None,
        }
    }

    /// Moves the user's home directory — `HOME`, which `directories::BaseDirs`
    /// reads, so `home_root()`'s fallback becomes `<home>/.openalpaca` — and
    /// sets `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` to `store`, or removes it for `None`. For
    /// the test-build guard of `store::projects::register`: its "unset" and
    /// "the real store" cases then name a temp directory, so even a guard that
    /// failed to fire could write nothing into the developer's store. Same
    /// lock, no second one. Panics, restoring both variables, if `BaseDirs`
    /// does not answer with `home`.
    pub(crate) fn for_user_home(home: &Path, store: Option<&Path>) -> Self {
        let lock = ENV_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let guard = Self {
            _lock: lock,
            prev: std::env::var_os(HOME_STORE_ENV),
            prev_home: Some(std::env::var_os("HOME")),
        };
        // SAFETY: serialized by ENV_LOCK, which `guard` holds until it drops
        // and restores both variables.
        unsafe {
            std::env::set_var("HOME", home);
            match store {
                Some(store) => std::env::set_var(HOME_STORE_ENV, store),
                None => std::env::remove_var(HOME_STORE_ENV),
            }
        }
        let resolved = directories::BaseDirs::new().map(|b| b.home_dir().to_path_buf());
        assert_eq!(
            resolved.as_deref(),
            Some(home),
            "HOME did not move the user's home directory; refusing to run"
        );
        guard
    }
}

impl Drop for HomeStoreGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: as above — still holding ENV_LOCK.
        if let Some(prev_home) = self.prev_home.take() {
            match prev_home {
                Some(v) => unsafe { std::env::set_var("HOME", v) },
                None => unsafe { std::env::remove_var("HOME") },
            }
        }
        match self.prev.take() {
            Some(v) => unsafe { std::env::set_var(HOME_STORE_ENV, v) },
            None => unsafe { std::env::remove_var(HOME_STORE_ENV) },
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
    for path in [w.home(), w.home().join("inside"), w.tmp.path().to_path_buf()] {
        let err = register(&path).unwrap_err();
        let refusal = err.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>().expect("a ProjectError");
        assert!(
            matches!(refusal, ProjectError::IsHome { .. }),
            "{path:?}: {refusal}"
        );
        assert_eq!(refusal.code(), "WORKSPACE_IS_HOME");
    }
    assert!(!w.projects().exists(), "a refusal creates nothing");
}

#[test]
fn a_path_that_is_not_a_directory_is_refused_and_so_is_a_relative_one() {
    let w = World::new();
    let file = w.folder("parent").join("notes.txt");
    fs::write(&file, "x").unwrap();
    for path in [w.tmp.path().join("work").join("never-made"), file] {
        let err = register(&path).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>(),
                Some(ProjectError::NotADirectory { .. })
            ),
            "{path:?}: {err}"
        );
    }
    let relative = register(Path::new("relative/project")).unwrap_err();
    assert!(relative.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>().is_none());
    assert!(relative.to_string().contains("absolute"), "{relative}");
    assert!(!w.projects().exists());
}

#[test]
fn a_root_whose_plain_name_another_root_holds_takes_the_hashed_name() {
    let w = World::new();
    let (underscore, dash) = (w.folder("b_c"), w.folder("b-c"));
    let first = register(&underscore).unwrap();
    let second = register(&dash).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first.name, folder_name(&underscore));
    assert_eq!(second.name, hashed_folder_name(&dash));
    assert_ne!(first.id, second.id);
    assert_eq!(lookup(&underscore).unwrap(), Some(first));
    assert_eq!(lookup(&dash).unwrap(), Some(second));
}

#[test]
#[tracing_test::traced_test]
fn a_hand_made_folder_at_the_plain_name_is_left_alone() {
    let w = World::new();
    let root = w.folder("handmade");
    let squatter = w.projects().join(folder_name(&root));
    fs::create_dir_all(&squatter).unwrap();
    fs::write(squatter.join("notes.txt"), "mine").unwrap();

    let project = register(&root).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(project.name, hashed_folder_name(&root));
    assert_eq!(register(&root).unwrap(), project);
    // R11: never opened, never deleted — and reported once.
    assert_eq!(names_in(&squatter), vec!["notes.txt".to_string()]);
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(squatter.join("notes.txt")).unwrap(), "mine");
    let shown = squatter.display().to_string();
    logs_assert(move |lines: &[&str]| {
        let n = lines
            .iter()
            .filter(|l| l.contains("WARN") && l.contains(&shown) && l.contains("has no project.json"))
            .count();
        if n == 1 {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(format!("one WARN for the hand-made folder, got {n}"))
        }
    });
}

#[test]
fn when_both_names_are_taken_register_says_so_and_creates_nothing() {
    let w = World::new();
    let root = w.folder("crowded");
    let elsewhere = w.folder("elsewhere");
    w.plant(&folder_name(&root), &file_for(&elsewhere));
    w.plant(&hashed_folder_name(&root), &file_for(&elsewhere));

    let err = register(&root).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(err.contains(&folder_name(&root)), "{err}");
    assert!(err.contains(&hashed_folder_name(&root)), "{err}");
    assert_eq!(names_in(&w.projects()).len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn a_re_point_keeps_its_own_folder_when_the_new_plain_name_is_the_same() {
    let w = World::new();
    let (old, new) = (w.folder("x_y"), w.folder("x-y"));
    let project = register(&old).unwrap();
    let held = lock();
    assert_eq!(
        name_for(&new, Some(&project.id), &held).unwrap(),
        project.name
    );
    assert_eq!(
        name_for(&new, None, &held).unwrap(),
        hashed_folder_name(&new)
    );
}

#[test]
fn concurrent_registrations_of_one_root_make_one_folder() {
    let w = World::new();
    let root = w.folder("busy");
    let ids: Vec<ProjectId> = std::thread::scope(|s| {
        let handles: Vec<_> = (0..8).map(|_| s.spawn(|| register(&root).unwrap().id)).collect();
        handles.into_iter().map(|h| h.join().unwrap()).collect()
    });
    assert!(ids.iter().all(|id| *id == ids[0]), "{ids:?}");
    assert_eq!(names_in(&w.projects()).len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn the_projects_lock_is_taken_again_after_a_holder_panicked() {
    let _ = std::thread::spawn(|| {
        let _held = lock();
        panic!("a holder that panics");
    })
    .join();
    let _again = lock();
}

#[test]
fn register_refuses_an_unguarded_home_store_and_writes_nothing() {
    let user_home = tempdir().unwrap();
    let project = tempdir().unwrap();
    let real_store = user_home.path().join(".openalpaca");
    for store in [None, Some(real_store.clone())] {
        let _env = HomeStoreGuard::for_user_home(user_home.path(), store.as_deref());
        let message = panic_of(|| {
            let _ = register(project.path());
        })
        .expect("register must refuse");
        assert!(
            message.contains("take the crate's home-store guard"),
            "{message}"
        );
    }
    assert!(!real_store.exists(), "nothing was written under the user's home");
}
```

  (b) insert immediately after the closing `}` of `refuse_unguarded_test_home` (the S1.7 section):

```rust
// ============================================================================
// Registering (§3, R6, R10, R13)
// ============================================================================

/// The one process-wide lock over the folders under `projects/`.
static PROJECTS_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

/// Holding it is the right to create, rename or remove a folder under
/// `projects/`: `register`, the re-point (S3) and the delete's folder
/// removal (S5a) take it. **Lock order: this lock, then the database mutex —
/// never the reverse.** The re-point holds it across one database
/// transaction, so nothing may take it, or call `register`, inside a
/// `with_connection` closure. Not `Send`: it is held on one thread.
pub struct ProjectsLock {
    _held: MutexGuard<'static, ()>,
}

/// Takes [`ProjectsLock`]. A poisoned lock is recovered: the folders on disk
/// are the state, not anything the mutex holds.
pub fn lock() -> ProjectsLock {
    ProjectsLock {
        _held: PROJECTS_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()),
    }
}

/// §3 *register*: the project at `root`, its folder created when there is
/// none — create-if-absent under [`lock`]. In order: the test-build guard;
/// [`canonical_root`]; an entry [`lookup`] finds is returned as it is, a
/// missing project's included (ST-7); a root that overlaps the home store is
/// [`ProjectError::IsHome`] (R13), one that is not a directory
/// [`ProjectError::NotADirectory`]; then the folder is built as
/// `projects/.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp/` holding `project.json` (0700 / 0600,
/// fsynced) and renamed to `projects/<name>`, so a crash never leaves a
/// folder without its file; a build that fails is removed. The lock makes it
/// create-if-absent within the process; the rename refuses a non-empty
/// target, though POSIX lets it replace an empty directory another process
/// made in between — and only the daemon registers, only where it accepts
/// work for a root (§3), so no other process does.
pub fn register(root: &Path) -> Result<Project> {
    refuse_unguarded_test_home();
    let root = canonical_root(root)?;
    let held = lock();
    if let Some(existing) = lookup(&root)? {
        return Ok(existing);
    }
    let path = root.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    if overlaps_home_store(&root) {
        return Err(ProjectError::IsHome { path }.into());
    }
    if !root.is_dir() {
        return Err(ProjectError::NotADirectory { path }.into());
    }
    let name = name_for(&root, None, &held)?;
    let projects = projects_dir()?;
    fsx::create_private_dir(&projects)?;
    let target = projects.join(&name);
    let building = fsx::temp_path_for(&target)?;
    let file = ProjectFile {
        version: PROJECT_FILE_VERSION,
        id: ProjectId::new(),
        root: path,
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true),
        previous_root: None,
        previous_name: None,
    };
    if let Err(e) = build_project_folder(&building, &target, &file) {
        let _ = fsx::remove_dir_all_if_exists(&building);
        return Err(e);
    }
    read_project_dir(&target)?
        .with_context(|| format!("{} was created but cannot be read back", target.display()))
}

/// The folder name `root` (canonical) takes (R6): the plain name unless
/// `projects/<plain>` exists and is not this project's — its file records
/// another root and, when `this` is `Some`, carries another id; or it holds
/// no readable file — then the hashed name under the same test; neither free
/// is an error naming both. `this` is `Some` only on a re-point (S3), so a
/// project whose new plain name is its own folder's keeps it.
pub(crate) fn name_for(
    root: &Path,
    this: Option<&ProjectId>,
    _held: &ProjectsLock,
) -> Result<String> {
    let projects = projects_dir()?;
    let want = root.to_string_lossy();
    let usable = |name: &str| -> Result<bool> {
        let dir = projects.join(name);
        if let Err(e) = fs::symlink_metadata(&dir)
            && e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound
        {
            return Ok(true);
        }
        Ok(read_project_dir(&dir)?
            .is_some_and(|p| p.root_string() == want.as_ref() || this == Some(&p.id)))
    };
    let plain = folder_name(root);
    if usable(&plain)? {
        return Ok(plain);
    }
    let hashed = hashed_folder_name(root);
    if hashed != plain && usable(&hashed)? {
        return Ok(hashed);
    }
    let names = if hashed == plain {
        plain
    } else {
        format!("{plain} and {hashed}")
    };
    bail!(
        "no folder name is free for the project {}: {names} under {} belong to other projects \
         or hold no readable {PROJECT_FILE}",
        root.display(),
        projects.display()
    )
}

/// Writes `dir/project.json` (R9): pretty JSON in field order and one final
/// newline, mode 0600, through `fsx`'s atomic write (no-follow, temp file,
/// fsync, rename, directory fsync).
pub(crate) fn write_project_file(dir: &Path, file: &ProjectFile) -> Result<()> {
    let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(file).context("Failed to serialize project.json")?;
    bytes.push(b'\n');
    fsx::write_atomic_private(&dir.join(PROJECT_FILE), &bytes)
}

/// `building` (0700) with `file` in it, renamed onto `target`, `projects/`
/// fsynced after.
fn build_project_folder(building: &Path, target: &Path, file: &ProjectFile) -> Result<()> {
    fsx::create_private_dir(building)?;
    write_project_file(building, file)?;
    fs::rename(building, target).with_context(|| {
        format!(
            "Failed to move {} into place as {}",
            building.display(),
            target.display()
        )
    })?;
    if let Some(projects) = target.parent() {
        fsx::fsync_dir(projects)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

### Choices made where the spec is open

- **`created_at`** is `Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Secs, true)` — `2026-10-07T09:30:00Z` — because one
  formatter fixes the bytes and whole seconds are all a person reads.
- **A `project.json` whose `root` is not absolute reads as unreadable (R11)**, because a relative root could only ever
  match through the process's working directory, which R22 forbids.
- **The R11 report is keyed by folder path (unreadable) and by id (shared id)**, held in one process-wide set,
  because R11 says "reported once" and two different folders are two different reports.
- **A multiply hard-linked `project.json` reads as unreadable**, because `fsx::read_if_exists` refuses an inode with a
  second name everywhere else in the store and the rule is cheaper to keep than to special-case.
- **`projects/` and each project folder are 0700, `project.json` 0600**, the sheet's rule (`fsx` primitives), unlike
  today's umask-created content directories.
- **The build folder is named by `fsx::temp_path_for`** (`projects/.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp`), the shape the sheet
  describes, so one counter names every temp path in the crate. With R7's longest name (209 bytes) it is at most
  1 + 209 + 1 + 10 + 1 + 20 + 4 = 246 bytes, under the 255-byte name limit of APFS and ext4.
- **`ProjectsLock` holds its guard in a named `_held` field**, so the field the lock exists for never reads as dead
  code.
- **The guard also refuses a store set *inside* the real one** (`~/.openalpaca/scratch`), because the owner's rule is
  about the real tree, not one path.
- **`test_home_guard_armed()` is public and `#[doc(hidden)]`**, so each dependent crate's test can prove its
  dev-dependency line works without ever calling `register` (a failing step must not be able to write into a real
  store).
- **The guard's panic test moves `HOME`** (`HomeStoreGuard::for_user_home`) rather than pointing the store variable at
  the developer's real path, so a regression in the guard writes into a temp directory.

### Spec conflicts

- **R2 is assigned twice.** The slice brief gives S1 "R1–R3 (… `ContentKind` loses the reserved `skills` and `cache`
  kinds, the seeded home README's `state/` row gains `repl_history` and lists `projects/`)"; `interfaces.md` §0 and
  §7.1 give R2 and the README rows to S6. Followed the sheet: `ContentKind::ALL` (`store/mod.rs:407-415`) feeds
  `unknown_entries` (`store/mod.rs:524`), which the live purge plan calls (`routes/workspaces.rs:791`); shrinking it
  before S5a reshapes the purge changes that plan's output mid-stage. S1 builds R3 (pinned by
  `register_builds_a_folder_holding_project_json_and_nothing_else`) and states R1 in the module documentation.
  Smallest correction: the brief's R2 line belongs to S6.
- **Accepted (R-S14).** **`canonical_root` "errors only for a path with no existing ancestor (a relative one)"** (sheet §1.5) is wrong
  against `fsx::canonical_string_lenient` (`memory_files/fsx.rs:201-224`): `Path::exists` and `canonicalize` resolve a
  relative path against the process's working directory, so an existing relative path (`src` under the crate root)
  canonicalizes to an absolute one — the CWD dependence R22 forbids. Correction: `canonical_root` refuses a
  non-absolute path before reading anything (pinned by
  `a_relative_path_has_no_canonical_root_even_when_it_exists_here`). A `..` in a missing tail is already refused by
  the walk (`Path::file_name` of a path ending in `..` is `None`); no change, one test pins it.
- **Accepted (R-S14).** **The guard's equality test** (sheet §1.7: `default.as_deref() == Some(Path::new(value))`) lets a store set

  which is case-insensitive, returned the on-disk spelling for a mis-cased path (a probe in a scratch directory). A
  case-sensitive volume has one spelling anyway; other platforms' case rules are not checked.

## Stage 1 — slice S2: the resolver and registration (design §3); content still in the project

Draft for the Stage 1 plan. Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Every `file:line` is from that HEAD and is
a pointer only: each edit below is located by the text it quotes. Builds on S1 exactly as
`interfaces.md` §1.1–§1.7 gives it (`ProjectId`, `Project`, `ProjectError`, `projects_dir`, `canonical_root`,
`overlaps_home_store`, `lookup`, `list`, `register`, the `test-home-guard` feature); S2 adds §1.8 and §2.

### What this slice does

S2 puts the storage design's resolver behind every place a project root is found. `store::projects::resolve`
walks up from a client path to the nearest registered project or folder holding `.git`. It never answers the
home store, a folder inside it or a folder that contains it (R13). A path that cannot be canonicalised is matched
against registered roots only, and a relative path is no project (R22). `resolve` keeps no cache and creates
nothing. `resolve_and_register` and `choose` (R10) are added beside it. In core, `memory/workspace.rs` is deleted:
the marker walk, its process-lifetime cache and the uncached pair go with it. `.openalpaca` stops being a marker.
`MemoryScopeContext::for_request` (pure) and `service::context::resolve_project_root` both use the resolver now.
A turn whose client sent no path has no project, and nothing resolves the daemon's current directory any more (the
lead's R-S13): `for_request(None)` reads nothing.
A stored root is used as given only when it is registered; otherwise it is resolved like a fresh path.
`resolves_to_the_home_store` becomes `projects::overlaps_home_store` at its three callers, which widens R13's
refusal to the home store's insides and to the folders that contain it.

Four places now register a project, and only in the daemon. A chat turn registers through `Gateway::handle_event`
and `MemoryScopeContext::for_turn`. A dispatch registers too (`dispatch_lead_agent_inner`, conflict C4). So do an
upload (`register_request_project`) and a memory write through `/v1/memories*` (`MemoryApi::run_write`, through the
same `register_request_project`). The
fifth site, choosing a folder, gets its route in S5a and calls `projects::choose`, which this slice builds. Reads
never register: the status poll, sessions, follow-ups, steering, the Memory view and the CLI.

`store_root` does not change, so a project's content still lands in `<project>/.openalpaca/`. R12's typed error
and its readers come with the flip in S3 (Spec conflicts 1). S2 provides the fact they check:
`ResolvedProject::is_registered` and `projects::lookup`.

### Task S2.1: `projects::resolve` — a client path to its project, pure

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects.rs` (S1's file). Append the *Resolution* block after S1's last
  function. Add `#[cfg(test)] mod resolve_tests;` directly below S1's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`.
- Create: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects/resolve_tests.rs`
- Test: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects/resolve_tests.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (S1, interfaces §1.5): `pub fn lookup(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<Project>>`,
  `pub fn register(root: &Path) -> Result<Project>`, `pub fn overlaps_home_store(root: &Path) -> bool`,
  `pub fn canonical_root(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf>`, `pub fn projects_dir() -> Result<PathBuf>`,
  `pub struct Project { pub id: ProjectId, pub root: PathBuf, pub missing: bool, .. }`,
  `crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard::set(&Path)`.
- Produces: `pub struct ResolvedProject { pub root: PathBuf, pub project: Option<Project> }`,
  `ResolvedProject::is_registered(&self) -> bool`, `ResolvedProject::root_string(&self) -> String`,
  `pub fn resolve(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Option<ResolvedProject>>`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests.** Create `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects/resolve_tests.rs`:

```rust
//! Storage design §3 *Resolve* (Stage 1 S2): the walk from a client path to
//! its project — a registered root, else a folder holding `.git`, the nearest
//! winning — R13's home rule and R10's choice. Every test runs under its own
//! home store.

use super::*;
use crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard;
use std::fs;
use tempfile::{TempDir, tempdir};

/// One temp root: the home store at `<tmp>/home/.openalpaca` (so `<tmp>/home`
/// stands in for `$HOME`) and the folders a client names under `<tmp>/work`.
/// A walk from any of them stops at `<tmp>`, which contains the home store
/// (R13), so nothing above the temp root can answer.
struct Scene {
    _guard: HomeStoreGuard,
    tmp: TempDir,
}

impl Scene {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let tmp = tempdir().unwrap();
        let home_store = tmp
            .path()
            .canonicalize()
            .unwrap()
            .join("home")
            .join(".openalpaca");
        fs::create_dir_all(&home_store).unwrap();
        let guard = HomeStoreGuard::set(&home_store);
        Self { _guard: guard, tmp }
    }

    fn root(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.tmp.path().canonicalize().unwrap()
    }

    fn home(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.root().join("home")
    }

    fn home_store(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.home().join(".openalpaca")
    }

    /// `<tmp>/work/<rel>`, created.
    fn dir(&self, rel: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = self.root().join("work").join(rel);
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        dir
    }

    /// A git repository at `<tmp>/work/<rel>`: a `.git` directory in it.
    fn repo(&self, rel: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = self.dir(rel);
        fs::create_dir(dir.join(".git")).unwrap();
        dir
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_folder_inside_a_git_repository_resolves_to_the_repository_unregistered() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    let repo = s.repo("app");
    let deep = s.dir("app/src/lib");

    let found = resolve(&deep).unwrap().expect("inside a repository");
    assert_eq!(found.root, repo);
    assert!(!found.is_registered(), "nobody has used it yet (R12)");
    assert_eq!(found.root_string(), repo.to_string_lossy());
    assert_eq!(resolve(&repo).unwrap().map(|r| r.root), Some(repo));
}

#[test]
fn a_git_file_makes_a_worktree_its_own_project() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    s.repo("main");
    let worktree = s.dir("main/worktrees/feature");
    fs::write(worktree.join(".git"), "gitdir: ../../.git/worktrees/feature\n").unwrap();
    let inside = s.dir("main/worktrees/feature/src");

    let found = resolve(&inside).unwrap().expect("a worktree is a project");
    assert_eq!(found.root, worktree, "the nearest `.git`, a file here, wins");
}

#[test]
fn a_folder_with_no_git_and_no_registration_is_no_project() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    assert_eq!(resolve(&s.dir("notes/2026")).unwrap(), None);
}

#[test]
fn an_openalpaca_folder_is_not_a_project_marker() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    let old = s.dir("old-project");
    fs::create_dir(old.join(".openalpaca")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        resolve(&old).unwrap(),
        None,
        "ST-9: an in-project store is never read, and it marks nothing"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_registered_folder_resolves_itself_and_every_folder_below_it() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    let notes = s.dir("notes");
    let registered = register(&notes).unwrap();
    let below = s.dir("notes/2026/march");

    for path in [&notes, &below] {
        let found = resolve(path).unwrap().expect("a registered project");
        assert_eq!(found.root, notes);
        assert_eq!(found.project.as_ref().map(|p| p.id), Some(registered.id));
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_nearest_registered_root_or_repository_wins() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    // A folder registered inside a repository answers for itself; the rest
    // of the repository is still the repository's.
    let mono = s.repo("mono");
    let web = s.dir("mono/packages/web");
    register(&web).unwrap();
    let found = resolve(&s.dir("mono/packages/web/src")).unwrap().expect("project");
    assert_eq!(found.root, web);
    assert!(found.is_registered());
    let found = resolve(&s.dir("mono/packages/api/src")).unwrap().expect("project");
    assert_eq!(found.root, mono);
    assert!(!found.is_registered());

    // And a repository inside a registered folder answers for itself.
    let notes = s.dir("notes");
    register(&notes).unwrap();
    let code = s.repo("notes/code");
    let found = resolve(&s.dir("notes/code/src")).unwrap().expect("project");
    assert_eq!(found.root, code);
    assert!(!found.is_registered());
}

#[test]
fn a_registered_repository_resolves_as_registered() {
    let s = Scene::new();
    let repo = s.repo("app");
    let registered = register(&repo).unwrap();

    let found = resolve(&s.dir("app/src")).unwrap().expect("project");
    assert_eq!(found.root, repo);
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** Append to `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/store/projects.rs`, after S1's last
  function and before the `#[cfg(test)]` module declarations. The code uses `anyhow::` in full so it does not
  depend on S1's `use` lines; `Path` and `PathBuf` come from S1's `use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};`, which its

```rust
// ── Resolution (storage design §3 *Resolve*; Stage 1 S2) ──────────────────

/// What a client path resolves to (§3). `project: None` is a root with no
/// folder under `projects/` yet — a git repository nobody has used (R12).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ResolvedProject {
    /// The canonical root: the registered project's `root`, or the folder
    /// that holds `.git`.
    pub root: PathBuf,
    /// The project's entry, when the root is registered.
    pub project: Option<Project>,
}

impl ResolvedProject {
    /// Whether the root has a folder under `projects/` — R12: one that does
    /// not has no store.
    pub fn is_registered(&self) -> bool {
        self.project.is_some()
    }

    /// `root.to_string_lossy().into_owned()` — the value the path columns hold.
    pub fn root_string(&self) -> String {
        self.root.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
    }

    fn registered(project: Project) -> Self {
        Self {
            root: project.root.clone(),
            project: Some(project),
        }
    }
}

/// What makes a folder a project root without anyone choosing it (ST-6): a
/// `.git` directory, or a `.git` file — a worktree is its own project.
const GIT_MARKER: &str = ".git";

/// §3 *Resolve* — pure: no cache, creates nothing. `Ok(None)` is no project.
///
/// A relative path is no project (R22: it would be read against the daemon's
/// working directory). An existing path is canonicalised and walked up; at
/// each folder, in this order: a folder that is, lies inside or contains the
/// home store ends the walk with no project (R13 — every folder above it
/// contains the home store too); a registered project's root is that project;
/// a folder holding `.git` is an unregistered root. The nearest match wins. A
/// path that cannot be canonicalised — its folder is gone — is walked as
/// written ([`canonical_root`]) against registered roots only, so a missing
/// project still resolves to itself (ST-7). `.openalpaca` is no marker (ST-9).
pub fn resolve(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Option<ResolvedProject>> {
    if !path.is_absolute() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let Ok(canonical) = path.canonicalize() else {
        return resolve_missing(path);
    };
    for folder in canonical.ancestors() {
        if overlaps_home_store(folder) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if let Some(project) = lookup(folder)? {
            return Ok(Some(ResolvedProject::registered(project)));
        }
        if folder.join(GIT_MARKER).exists() {
            return Ok(Some(ResolvedProject {
                root: folder.to_path_buf(),
                project: None,
            }));
        }
    }
    Ok(None)
}

/// [`resolve`] for a path that cannot be canonicalised: its ancestors as
/// written, deepest first, against registered roots only.
fn resolve_missing(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Option<ResolvedProject>> {
    let written = canonical_root(path)?;
    for folder in written.ancestors() {
        if let Some(project) = lookup(folder)? {
            return Ok(Some(ResolvedProject::registered(project)));
        }
    }
    Ok(None)
}
```

`resolve_missing` skips the R13 check on purpose. It matches only registered roots, and `register` never records
a root that overlaps the home store (S1).

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** Append after `resolve_missing` in `projects.rs`:

```rust
/// [`resolve`], then [`register`] when the root it found has no folder yet —
/// the one call every registration site makes (§3: only the daemon, only
/// where it accepts work for a root). `Ok(None)`: no project, nothing
/// recorded. A registered project, missing or not, is returned as it is.
pub fn resolve_and_register(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Option<Project>> {
    match resolve(path)? {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some(ResolvedProject {
            project: Some(project),
            ..
        }) => Ok(Some(project)),
        Some(ResolvedProject {
            root,
            project: None,
        }) => register(&root).map(Some),
    }
}

/// R10 — choosing a folder (the app's `Use`, `openalpaca chat --project`):
/// resolved like any path, so inside a git repository it is the repository
/// and inside a chosen folder it is that folder. Only when nothing is found
/// does the folder itself become a project, through [`register`]. Its own
/// checks refuse a relative path before anything is read ([`canonical_root`],
/// R22), then the home store, the folders inside it and the folders around
/// it ([`ProjectError::IsHome`]), and anything that is not a directory
/// ([`ProjectError::NotADirectory`]). `POST /v1/workspaces` (S5a) is its
/// first caller.
pub fn choose(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Project> {
    match resolve_and_register(path)? {
        Some(project) => Ok(project),
        None => register(path),
    }
}
```

`choose` repeats none of `register`'s checks. S1 fixes them in `register`, in this order: the test guard, a
relative path (`canonical_root` bails, S1.3), `IsHome`, then `NotADirectory` (interfaces §1.5). `resolve` answers
`Ok(None)` for a relative path without reading anything, so a relative path reaches `register` and is refused
there. S5a's route refuses a relative path with `400 INVALID_PATH` (`canonical_path`) before it calls `choose`.

```rust
/// The marker walk of design §3 rule 1: `.openalpaca`, else `.git`, from the
/// request workspace upward; a directory with no marker above it is global.
fn find_project_root(from: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut cur = Some(from.to_path_buf());
    while let Some(dir) = cur {
        if dir.join(".openalpaca").exists() || dir.join(".git").exists() {
            return Some(dir);
        }
        cur = dir.parent().map(Path::to_path_buf);
    }
    None
}
```

```rust
/// The project root a request workspace resolves to: the store's own

/// registered project or folder holding `.git`, never the home store. A

fn find_project_root(from: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    crate::store::projects::resolve(from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("resolve {}: {e:#}", from.display()))
        .map(|found| found.root)
}
```

```rust
/// Storage design §3: a stored root is used as given only when it is a
/// registered project's root; anything else is resolved as a fresh path.
#[test]
fn a_stored_root_is_used_as_given_only_when_it_is_registered() {
    let h = Harness::new();
    let repo = h.workspace("repo", Some(".git"));
    let src = repo.join("src");
    fs::create_dir_all(&src).unwrap();

    // Unregistered: resolved like a client path — up to the repository.
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_project_root(WorkspaceHint::Root(&src)),
        Some(repo.clone())
    );
    // Registered: used as given, though a repository holds it.
    openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register(&src).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_project_root(WorkspaceHint::Root(&src)),
        Some(src.clone())
    );
    // A registered project whose folder is gone still scopes its notes
    // (ST-7), as given and from a path below it.
    let gone = h.workspace("gone", None);

    fs::remove_dir_all(&gone).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_project_root(WorkspaceHint::Root(&gone)),
        Some(gone.clone())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_project_root(WorkspaceHint::Path(&gone.join("sub"))),
        Some(gone)
    );
}
```

```rust
//! Workspace scope context: carries workspace identity through the request lifecycle.
//!
//! Created once in `handle_message()` and threaded to the call sites that need
//! the request's workspace: the memory service resolves its own partition from
//! `request_workspace_root` (design §2), and artifact placement reads it too.
//!
//! Two fields travel here, because their consumers differ and conflating them
//! is the defect ruling R22 fixed:
//!
//! - [`workspace_id`](MemoryScopeContext::workspace_id) is what a turn's tools
//!   carry for **memory** scoping (`ToolContext::workspace_id`).
//! - [`request_workspace_root`](MemoryScopeContext::request_workspace_root)
//!   scopes **content the request owns** (artifacts) and is what a run
//!   records.
//!
//! Both are the root of the path a client sent, and `None` when it sent none —
//! connector lanes, scheduled skills and every other turn without one. The
//! daemon's current directory is never read (R22; the lead's R-S13: the
//! resolver takes the path a client sent, storage design §3), so on a context
//! built from a request the two are equal.
//!
//! The root comes from one resolver, `openalpaca_storage::store::projects::resolve`
//! (storage design §3): walking up from the path, the nearest folder that is a
//! registered project's root or holds `.git` — never the home store, a folder
//! inside it or a folder containing it (R13). `.openalpaca` is no marker. The
//! resolver keeps no cache and creates nothing.

use std::path::Path;

use openalpaca_storage::store::projects;

/// Carries workspace scope context for a request.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct MemoryScopeContext {
    /// Detected workspace root path as scope_id. `None` if no workspace detected
    /// (e.g., a request that named none, or from Telegram).
    ///
    /// Memory scoping: the root the client's path resolved to — the same value
    /// as `request_workspace_root` on a context built from a request, and
    /// never derived from the daemon's current directory (R-S13).
    pub workspace_id: Option<String>,
    /// The project root the *request* supplied — `x-workspace-path` on
    /// `/v1/chat`, `workspace_path` on `/v1/command` — resolved to its root.
    /// `None` whenever no client sent one; never CWD-derived (R22), and never
    /// a root that is, lies inside or contains the home store (R13).
    ///
    /// This is the only field that may place a file on disk, and it is what a
    /// dispatched run records as its `task.workspace_id`.
    pub request_workspace_root: Option<String>,
}

impl MemoryScopeContext {
    /// Create a scope context with an optional workspace for **memory scoping**.
    ///
    /// `request_workspace_root` stays `None`: a caller that has a
    /// request-supplied workspace builds the context with
    /// [`MemoryScopeContext::for_request`] instead.
    pub fn new(workspace_id: Option<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            workspace_id,
            request_workspace_root: None,
        }
    }

    /// The workspace context of an incoming turn (R22) — the one place that
    /// knows the rule.
    ///
    /// `workspace_path` is what the client sent, if anything, and both fields
    /// are the root it resolves to. A turn that sent none has no project on
    /// either field: nothing is read from the daemon's current directory (the
    /// lead's R-S13). The CLI always sends its working directory; the turns
    /// with none are the connector lanes, the scheduled skills and an app
    /// window with no project chosen.
    ///
    /// **The home store is not a workspace on either field** (R13). The
    /// resolver answers no project for the home store, for any folder inside
    /// it and for any folder containing it. Nothing that writes a file reads
    /// `workspace_id`: the task-output extraction at `dispatcher/lead_agent.rs`
    /// takes `request_workspace_root`, like `task.workspace_id`.
    ///
    /// Pure: it records nothing, so a read — the status poll, the Memory
    /// view — may call it freely.
    pub fn for_request(workspace_path: Option<&str>) -> Self {
        let root = workspace_path.and_then(|path| resolved_root(Path::new(path)));
        Self {
            workspace_id: root.clone(),
            request_workspace_root: root,
        }
    }

    /// Recover the request's workspace context from a `ToolContext` that was
    /// built from one.
    pub fn from_tool_context(ctx: &crate::tools::registry::ToolContext) -> Self {
        Self {
            workspace_id: ctx.workspace_id.clone(),
            request_workspace_root: ctx.request_workspace_root.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Create a scope context with no workspace (Global-only).
    pub fn global_only() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Whether a workspace context is available.
    pub fn has_workspace(&self) -> bool {
        self.workspace_id.is_some()
    }
}

/// The project root [`projects::resolve`] finds for `path`, registered or
/// not, as the string the rows hold. An error reading `projects/` reads as no
/// project, logged at debug: the turn still runs, without one.
fn resolved_root(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    match projects::resolve(path) {
        Ok(found) => found.map(|r| r.root_string()),
        Err(e) => {
            tracing::debug!(
                path = %path.display(),
                "resolving a workspace path failed, so it names no project: {e:#}"
            );
            None
        }
    }
}
```

(c) `crates/openalpaca_core/src/memory/service/context.rs`: replace the `WorkspaceHint` enum with its doc, and the
whole of `resolve_project_root` with its doc:

```rust
/// Where the request says it is working (design §3 rule 1, MD-5; storage
/// design §3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum WorkspaceHint<'a> {
    /// The request named no workspace: the global partition only. The
    /// daemon's own CWD is never consulted.
    None,
    /// A root a turn resolved or a row stored
    /// (`ToolContext.request_workspace_root`, R22): used as given when it is
    /// a registered project's root, otherwise resolved as a fresh path.
    Root(&'a Path),
    /// A directory the request named (the `x-workspace-path` header, a CLI's
    /// CWD): resolved from it.
    Path(&'a Path),
}

/// Resolves a hint to the project root that scopes memory, or `None` for the
/// global partition only (storage design §3). The answer is the nearest
/// registered project or folder holding `.git`, registered or not; whether a
/// partition can open there is decided where it opens. A path under neither,
/// a relative path and the home store with its insides and the folders
/// around it (R13) are global. If `projects/` cannot be read, a stored root
/// is kept as given, so the write it carries fails where its partition opens
/// instead of landing in the global partition, and a client path scopes no
/// project.
pub fn resolve_project_root(hint: WorkspaceHint<'_>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    use openalpaca_storage::store::projects;
    match hint {
        WorkspaceHint::None => None,
        WorkspaceHint::Root(root) if root.is_absolute() => {
            let found = match projects::lookup(root) {
                Ok(Some(project)) => return Some(project.root),
                Ok(None) => projects::resolve(root),
                Err(e) => Err(e),
            };
            match found {
                Ok(found) => found.map(|r| r.root),
                Err(e) => {
                    tracing::debug!(
                        root = %root.display(),
                        "reading projects/ failed, so the stored root is kept as given: {e:#}"
                    );
                    Some(root.to_path_buf())
                }
            }
        }
        // A relative stored root is no project (R22).
        WorkspaceHint::Root(_) => None,
        WorkspaceHint::Path(path) => match projects::resolve(path) {
            Ok(found) => found.map(|r| r.root),
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::debug!(
                    path = %path.display(),
                    "resolving a memory workspace failed, so it scopes no project: {e:#}"
                );
                None
            }
        },
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Resolve a client-sent workspace path the way a chat turn would — and
/// record nothing.
///
/// One resolver, no second opinion: `MemoryScopeContext::for_request` owns the
/// rule (`openalpaca_storage::store::projects::resolve`: the nearest registered
/// project or `.git`, never the home store — R13), so a route never resolves a
/// header a second way. `None` means *no project*: no header, a path under no
/// project, or one that is, lies inside or contains the home store. Content
/// placement then falls back to the home store. Never the daemon's working
/// directory (ruling R22). The routes that only read call this — the status
/// poll, sessions, follow-ups, steering, the workspace routes — and a read
/// never records a project (storage design §3).
pub(crate) fn request_project_root(workspace_path: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {
    let path = workspace_path?;
    MemoryScopeContext::for_request(Some(path)).request_workspace_root
}
```

```rust
/// The user's `mv`: the whole store travels to the new root, marker and all,
/// so it still records the root it was seeded at. Nothing in the database moves
/// — which is precisely the state a re-base exists to fix.
fn move_the_store_by_hand(old: &str, new: &str) {
    let from = std::path::Path::new(old).join(store::STORE_DIR_NAME);
    let to = std::path::Path::new(new).join(store::STORE_DIR_NAME);

}
```

```rust
/// The user's `mv`: the whole store travels to the new root, marker and all,
/// so it still records the root it was seeded at — and the repository with it,
/// so the new root is a project and the old one a directory with nothing in it.
/// Nothing in the database moves — which is precisely the state a re-base
/// exists to fix.
fn move_the_store_by_hand(old: &str, new: &str) {
    let from = std::path::Path::new(old).join(store::STORE_DIR_NAME);
    let to = std::path::Path::new(new).join(store::STORE_DIR_NAME);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(new).expect("new project dir");
    std::fs::rename(&from, &to).expect("move the store");
    let git = std::path::Path::new(old).join(".git");
    if git.exists() {
        std::fs::rename(&git, std::path::Path::new(new).join(".git")).expect("move the repository");
    }
}
```

```bash
feat(core): one resolver for every project root; .openalpaca is no marker

MemoryScopeContext::for_request and memory's resolve_project_root ask
store::projects::resolve (storage design §3): the nearest registered
project or folder holding .git, never the home store or a folder around
or inside it (R13); a relative path is no project (R22). A stored root is
used as given only when it is registered; anything else is resolved
afresh. memory/workspace.rs goes whole: the .openalpaca marker, the
walk's process-lifetime cache and the uncached pair (for_request_uncached,
request_project_root_uncached). Nothing registers yet.

A turn whose client sent no path has no project (R-S13): the daemon-CWD
fallback of for_request goes with its seam, for_request_with_cwd, so
resolution reads nothing from the process's current directory and the
~80 tests that run a turn with no path read no projects/ folder. The
two tests that asserted a CWD-derived workspace_id now assert None inside
a git checkout, the CWD-injecting scope test goes, and the comments that
described the fallback as current are reworded.

Tests that leaned on .openalpaca as a marker now give their roots a .git:
the memory service harness (11 sites, two hand moves), the workspace
routes' project fixture, move-by-hand helper and two re-base destinations,
and the 422 remediation test.

The tests that resolve a project path and held no home-store guard now
take their crate's (three queue_followup tests, the two tool_context_for_turn
callers and the /steer test, the gateway's two project-switch tests, the
chat route's three R49 tests, the sessions route's PATCH test, the CLI's
two workspace-filter tests), so none reads the developer's
~/.openalpaca/projects/.

Verified: cargo test -p openalpaca_storage, -p openalpaca_core,
-p openalpacad, -p openalpaca (0 failed); cargo check -p openalpaca_core
--features live-eval --tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn for_turn_records_the_project_that_for_request_only_finds() {

        let home_store = root.join("home").join(".openalpaca");
```

```rust
/// A temp home store for a test whose turns name a project: the gateway
/// records every turn's project under `projects/` (storage design §3), and
/// recording outside a test's own home store panics in a test build.
fn guarded_home() -> (
    tempfile::TempDir,
    std::path::PathBuf,
    crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard,
) {
    let home = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let home_store = home.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join(".openalpaca");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&home_store).unwrap();
    let guard = crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set(&home_store);
    (home, home_store, guard)
}

/// Counts the turns that reached the handler.
#[derive(Default)]
struct CountingHandler {
    calls: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize,
}

#[async_trait]
impl MessageHandler for CountingHandler {
    async fn handle(&self, request: HandleRequest) -> Result<HandleResult, String> {
        self.calls.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
        Ok(HandleResult::text(format!("Echo: {}", request.content)))
    }
}

/// Storage design §3: a chat turn accepts work for its root, so the gateway
/// records the root under `projects/` before anything of the turn is written.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_turn_records_its_project() {
    let (_home, _home_store, _env) = guarded_home();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = openalpaca_storage::Database::open(&dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
    let gw = Gateway::new(
        Arc::new(SharedContext::new()),
        Arc::new(LaneManager::new()),
        Arc::new(StubHandler),
        EventBus::default(),
        Some(db),
    );
    let project = project_dir();

    let resp = gw
        .handle_event(learning_turn("in a project", Some(project_path(&project))))
        .await;
    assert!(!resp.is_error, "{}", resp.content);
    let root = project.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let recorded = openalpaca_storage::store::projects::lookup(&root)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("the turn recorded its project");
    assert_eq!(recorded.root, root);
}

/// A root that cannot be recorded ends the turn before anything of it is
/// persisted or run: no row would ever name a project with no folder.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_turn_whose_project_cannot_be_recorded_ends_before_anything_is_persisted() {
    let (_home, home_store, _env) = guarded_home();
    std::fs::write(home_store.join("projects"), "not a directory\n").unwrap();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = openalpaca_storage::Database::open(&dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
    let handler = Arc::new(CountingHandler::default());
    let gw = Gateway::new(
        Arc::new(SharedContext::new()),
        Arc::new(LaneManager::new()),
        handler.clone(),
        EventBus::default(),
        Some(db.clone()),
    );
    let project = project_dir();
    let path = project_path(&project);

    let resp = gw
        .handle_event(learning_turn("in a project", Some(path.clone())))
        .await;
    assert!(resp.is_error);
    assert!(
        resp.content
            .starts_with(&format!("Could not record the project for {path}: ")),
        "{}",
        resp.content
    );
    assert_eq!(
        handler.calls.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
        0,
        "nothing ran"
    );
    let rows = openalpaca_storage::ConversationRepository::new(&db)
        .list_by_lane("user1:gui", 50, 0)
        .unwrap();
    assert!(rows.is_empty(), "nothing was persisted");
}
```

```rust
    /// The daemon's turn entry (storage design §3): [`for_request`]'s answer
    /// for the client path, with its root recorded under `projects/` when
    /// nobody has used it yet — through `projects::resolve_and_register`, the
    /// one call every registration site makes. A chat turn and a follow-up's
    /// re-entry come through `Gateway::handle_event`, and an upload through
    /// the daemon's `register_request_project`; a read never does. A turn
    /// that names no workspace records nothing and has no project (R-S13).
    /// `Err` is a root that could not be recorded: the caller takes no work
    /// for it.
    pub fn for_turn(workspace_path: Option<&str>) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
        let Some(path) = workspace_path else {
            return Ok(Self::for_request(None));
        };
        let root = projects::resolve_and_register(Path::new(path))?
            .map(|project| project.root_string());
        Ok(Self {
            workspace_id: root.clone(),
            request_workspace_root: root,
        })
    }
```

```rust
/// [`request_project_root`] for a route that accepts work for the root — an
/// upload, a memory write (storage design §3): the root is also recorded
/// under `projects/`, through `MemoryScopeContext::for_turn`, the same call a
/// chat turn makes. A root that cannot be recorded is answered by
/// [`registration_refusal`], and the caller does nothing more.
#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
pub(crate) fn register_request_project(
    workspace_path: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Option<String>, Response> {
    let Some(path) = workspace_path else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    MemoryScopeContext::for_turn(Some(path))
        .map(|scope| scope.request_workspace_root)
        .map_err(|e| registration_refusal(path, &e))
}

/// How a route answers a root it could not record — the same on every route
/// that records one: the home store, a folder inside it or one around it is
/// `409 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` in `ProjectError`'s words, the status `PATCH` and
/// `POST /v1/workspaces` give it; anything else (I/O, no free folder name)
/// is `500 WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED`. Through `MemoryScopeContext::for_turn`
/// the first cannot happen today — the resolver answers no project for such a
/// root before anything registers it (R13) — so it is written down here
/// rather than left for a later caller to find.
fn registration_refusal(path: &str, e: &anyhow::Error) -> Response {
    match e
        .chain()
        .find_map(|cause| cause.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>())
    {
        Some(home @ ProjectError::IsHome { .. }) => {
            api_error(StatusCode::CONFLICT, home.code(), home.to_string())
        }
        _ => {
            tracing::warn!(path, "could not record the request's project: {e:#}");
            api_error(
                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                "WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED",
                format!("could not record the project for {path}: {e:#}"),
            )
        }
    }
}
```

(c) Directly after `run`'s closing brace — anchor on its last two lines,
`        .map_err(|e| MemoryError::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!("memory task failed: {e}")))?` and `    }` — insert:

```rust

    /// [`Self::run`] for a write (storage design §3): a memory write through a
    /// route accepts work for the header's root, so on the blocking pool the
    /// root is first resolved and recorded under `projects/` — through
    /// `register_request_project`, the upload's call, so a root that cannot be
    /// recorded is answered exactly as an upload's is and no note is touched —
    /// then `f` runs under a context built on the recorded root. A refusal of
    /// `f`'s is [`refusal`]'s answer.
    async fn run_write<T, F>(&self, headers: &HeaderMap, f: F) -> Result<T, Response>
    where
        T: Send + 'static,
        F: FnOnce(&MemoryService, &MemoryAccessContext) -> Result<T, MemoryError> + Send + 'static,
    {
        let service = self.service.clone();
        let owner_id = self.owner_id.clone();
        let workspace = workspace_header(headers);
        let joined = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            let root = register_request_project(workspace.as_deref())?;
            let hint = match &root {
                Some(root) => WorkspaceHint::Root(Path::new(root)),
                None => WorkspaceHint::None,
            };
            Self::context_with(&service, &owner_id, hint)
                .and_then(|ctx| f(&service, &ctx))
                .map_err(refusal)
        })
        .await;
        joined.unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            Err(refusal(MemoryError::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!(
                "memory task failed: {e}"
            ))))
        })
    }
```

### Spec conflicts

1. **R12 is listed under S2, but its typed error cannot land before the flip.** The slice brief puts R12 here: "store_root for it is a typed error that creates nothing; readers check registration". The same brief and interfaces §0/§3.2 keep `store_root` unchanged until S3, which owns "R12's typed error and its readers". In S2 an unregistered root's content is still at `<root>/.openalpaca`. S2 delivers the fact R12's readers will check (`ResolvedProject::is_registered`, `projects::lookup`). `resolve_project_root` keeps returning a root whether or not it is registered, as interfaces §2.1 says ("R12 is decided where a partition opens"). If S2 made the readers skip unregistered roots, learning from an earlier build's rows would write that project's facts into the global partition. **Correction:** none to the code; R12's readers and `store_root`'s error stay in S3.
2. **Interfaces §2.2 row 4 answered a failed registration with `MemoryError::invalid(..)`, which is a 400.** A registration failure is I/O, or no free folder name (S1's `name_for`), not bad input, and site 3 answers the same failure `500 WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED`. **Ruled (R-S7):** a registration failure answers the same on every route. S2.9's writers register through S2.8's `register_request_project` (`500 WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED`, `could not record the project for {path}: {e:#}`), and interfaces §2.2 row 4 now says so. R-S7 also named the home-store overlap's answer `400 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME`; `registration_refusal` answers it `409`, the status HEAD's `refuse_the_home_root`, interfaces §1.4/§6.1, S3.8's `project_error_response`, S5a.6 and S5b give it. **Settled (R-S7 as amended, second round):** the overlap answers `409 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` on every route — the ruling's "400" was the lead's slip — so S2.8 stands as drafted. Through `for_turn` the overlap cannot reach a registration today (R13: `resolve` answers no project first).
3. **Interfaces §7.4 lists `routes/status/tests.rs` and `scope_context.rs` among the tests "using `.openalpaca` as a marker"**, and the task brief adds `files.rs`. The `.openalpaca` in all three is the **home store** (`HomeStoreGuard::set(&home.join(".openalpaca"))`), not a marker, so nothing switches there. The real marker dependencies the sheet does not list are these. `routes/workspaces/tests.rs`'s `Fixture::project()` gets its root from `ensure_store` seeding `<dir>/.openalpaca`. `move_the_store_by_hand` moves only that store. Two re-base tests read the destination's memory through `WorkspaceHint::Path`. Two core service tests move `.openalpaca` by hand. **Correction:** S2.5 (j) and (g).
4. **Fixture 17 also declares `"marker": ".openalpaca"`** (`project_a`, `project_c`). Interfaces §7.3 assigns 17 wholly to S4/S5a, and C5 does not list it among the marker fixtures. No runner loads 17. **Correction:** S2.3 switches its two marker lines so the README's new vocabulary (`".git" | null`) holds for every file. S4's rewrite keeps `.git`.
5. **Interfaces §1.8's `choose` restates `register`'s two refusals.** `register` (§1.5, S1.8) already refuses, in order, a relative path (`canonical_root`), `IsHome` and `NotADirectory`. **Correction:** none to the contract: `choose` calls `register` when `resolve_and_register` finds nothing and adds no check of its own, so its refusals are exactly the sheet's.
6. **A relative path and the working directory.** `Path::canonicalize` and `Path::exists` read a relative path against the process's working directory, which R22 forbids. S1 already closes this for its own functions: `canonical_root` bails on a relative path before reading anything (S1.3), so `lookup` and `register` refuse one. `resolve` calls `Path::canonicalize` itself, so it checks `is_absolute()` first and answers `Ok(None)`. **Correction:** none needed in S1; S2's `resolve` keeps its own check.
7. **Accepted (R-S14).** **Interfaces §2.2 row 1 puts site 1 "in place of `for_request`" at `router/mod.rs:380`, inside `if let Some(ref p) = self.persistence`.** There, a gateway with no database would never register, though its handler still places content. A failure would also leave a learning in-flight entry already opened. **Correction:** `for_turn` runs before the turn guard. The persistence block reads its result.
8. **Accepted (R-S14).** **Interfaces §2.2 row 2 puts the dispatch's registration "before the row that records `workspace_id` (`:361`)".** The lock-order rule (§1.5) needs it before `active_session_id` (`:326`), the first `with_connection`. A failure placed at `:361` would also leave a spawned lead instance, a registry entry, a task lane and two published events behind. **Correction:** first in `dispatch_lead_agent_inner`.

### Open points

- **Between S2 and S5a/S5b, a folder with no git cannot become a project.** `.openalpaca` no longer marks one, and `POST /v1/workspaces` (`choose`) comes in S5a. The app's `Use` on such a folder now gives no project. This affects unreleased commits only.
- **The `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` messages still say "give {literal} a project marker of its own first"** (`routes/workspaces.rs`). Only a `.git` qualifies now. S5a removes that refusal, so S2 leaves the words.
- **Copy that S2 does not touch:**
  - The GUI copy naming `.openalpaca` as a marker: `stores/project.ts:5`, `lib/api/status.ts:15`, `views/chat/useSessionSidebar.ts:124`, `views/memory/MemoryList.tsx:145`. That is S5b/S6, because touching a `.ts` file means running all four bun gates.
  - `CLAUDE.md`'s Code Navigation row naming `memory/workspace.rs (marker walk)`. That is S6.
  - Comments in tests S3 deletes, for example `store/tests.rs:370` naming `walk_up_for_marker`.
- **Tests that resolve without a home-store guard would read `<real home>/projects/<name>/project.json` for each ancestor they walk.** The lead's R-S2: S2.5 (l) guards the ones named — `runner/lead_agent/tests.rs` (`:1145`, `:1190`, `:1277`), `orchestrator/tests.rs`'s two `tool_context_for_turn` callers, `routes/chat.rs`'s three tests that reach `root`, and the CLI's two `commands/sessions/tests.rs` workspace tests — and, under the same rule, four the list missed, which resolve through a turn or a route rather than a direct call (found verifying the second round): `orchestrator/tests.rs`' `a_steer_command_carries_the_turns_resolved_project_root`, `gateway/router/tests.rs`' two project-switch tests (guarded in S2.5, the guard swapped for `guarded_home()` in S2.6) and `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/sessions/tests.rs`' `patching_renames_and_binds_a_workspace_the_session_does_not_have`. **Settled (R-S13):** the turns with no workspace path — about 80 tests at `32292608` (43 `handle_message`/`handle_event` calls in `orchestrator/tests.rs`, 37 in `gateway/router/tests.rs`, more in `memory_commands/tests.rs`, the learning tests and the daemon's `followup.rs` / `routes/command.rs` / `scheduled_skills.rs` tests) — no longer resolve the daemon's working directory: S2.5 removes the CWD fallback in the commit that switches resolution, so `for_request(None)` and `for_turn(None)` read nothing and those tests need no guard.
- **Registration I/O runs on the async runtime at two sites:** `Gateway::handle_event` and `upload_scope`. That is a few syscalls under a std mutex. The memory routes do it inside their existing `spawn_blocking`. Moving the upload's call into the writer's `spawn_blocking` would need a second error path, so S2 keeps it inline.
- **`POST /v1/memories/sync` stays a read.** It reconciles the files and writes no note, and it is not in §2.2 row 4.
- **`POST /v1/sessions` and `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}` bind a session to a root without registering it,** per the interfaces' "never registering" list. The session's first turn registers it.
- **`run_write` registers before `service.context` checks the owner.** On the daemon the owner is always its own `local_user_id`, so an unknown owner cannot happen there.
- **R13's wider refusal changes `PATCH /v1/workspaces`.** A root inside the home store or around it (`/`, `/Users`) is now `409 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME`. Before, only `$HOME` and the home store itself were.
- **R49: a named session's stored root now goes through the new resolver.** `routes/chat.rs` passes a named session's stored `workspace_id` as the turn's path. Suppose an earlier commit on this branch bound a session to a root that only an `.openalpaca` marked. With no `.git` above it, that root now resolves to no project: the turn runs with none, and the session keeps its binding. With a `.git` ancestor it resolves to that ancestor, which differs from the binding, so `project_switched` opens a new session once. Both are ST-9 consequences, on unreleased commits only, and belong in S6's switch-over note.
- **A path that cannot be canonicalised resolves only to a registered root above it.** This is §3 as written. A CLI started in a since-deleted subfolder of a git repository nobody registered gets no project (`a_missing_path_is_matched_against_registered_roots_only`).
- **Settled: S1's `lookup` when `<home>/projects` is a regular file** (the failure tests' blocker). S1.5's `read_project_dir` meets `ENOTDIR` from `symlink_metadata`, which is not `NotFound`, so it reports the folder once at WARN and answers `None`: `lookup` is `Ok(None)` and `resolve` still finds the `.git` root. S1.8's `register` then finds neither name usable in `name_for` and fails with "no folder name is free for the project …". So `resolve_and_register`, `register`, `for_turn`, the dispatch, `register_request_project` and `run_write` all fail, which is what each failure test asserts (that it fails, and the sentence it starts with).
- **Settled: S1's `projects.rs` imports.** S1.3 and S1.5 give it `use std::fs;`, `use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};` and `use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};`, so S2's code may name `Path` and `PathBuf` bare. It still spells `anyhow::Result` in full, which compiles either way.
- **Settled: pass counts.** `store::projects` is pinned (S2.1: 67; S2.2: 76, from S1.8's 55). Every other run is pinned by `0 failed` and by the new tests each step names, since the whole-crate totals move with whatever lands before S2.
- **R13's and §3's rule also move stored roots that only an earlier build's `.openalpaca` marked.** `resolve_project_root(WorkspaceHint::Root(r))` now resolves an unregistered `r` as a fresh path, so a learning chunk, a run's task extraction or a forget whose stored root has no `.git` and no registration lands in the partition of a `.git` ancestor, or the global one. Every test's root has a `.git` (checked: the learning, dispatcher, lead-agent, memory-command, tool-suggestion and episode harnesses), so none changes. On a real store this is the same ST-9 consequence as the R49 point above, on unreleased commits only, and belongs in S6's switch-over note.
- **The core module doc of `memory/service/mod.rs` (`:10`, "the marker walk from the request workspace") and `routes/memories.rs`'s module doc (`:8`, "the same marker walk a chat turn uses") are left.** A `.git` walk is still a walk; S6's text pass rewords them. `runner/lead_agent/tests.rs:1125` cites `memory/workspace.rs:81-86` in a comment, which S2.5 deletes; S2.5 (l) rewords that comment while it guards the test (R-S2).

## Stage 1, slice S3 — the flip (draft)

Draft for the Stage 1 plan, slice **S3** of `interfaces.md` §0: design rev 0.8 §16 Stage 1 step (3), §4, §7's
non-memory removals and §8, plus §6's re-point core and R24's boot recovery (interfaces conflict C1). Read at
`32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Every `file:line` is from that commit; locate code by the quoted content,
because S1 and S2 land first and move lines. Names from S1/S2 are the ones `interfaces.md` fixes
(`store::projects::{register, lookup, list, by_id, lock, resolve, resolve_and_register, choose, projects_dir,
folder_name, canonical_root, overlaps_home_store, is_not_registered, name_for, write_project_file,
read_project_dir, Project, ProjectFile, ProjectError, ProjectsLock, ResolvedProject, PROJECTS_DIR, PROJECT_FILE}`).

### What this slice does

After S3 a project's content lives at `~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/{artifacts,uploads,memory}` and nothing is
written into the project's own folder. `store_root(StoreScope::Project(root))` is the project's folder found by
`projects::lookup`, or a typed `NotRegistered` error that creates nothing (R12). Rows record the turn's project
root (R15), upload dedup stops crossing projects (R17), the CLI's `--file` upload carries its turn's project, and
Reveal admits files under the home root only. Migration `003` drops the rows whose bytes lie inside a project's
own folder (R25). `PATCH /v1/workspaces` becomes §6's re-point (`project_life::repoint`: `project.json` marked,
five columns and both `storage_path` prefixes in one transaction, the folder renamed, the marker cleared), the
daemon finishes an interrupted one at boot (R24), and the in-project move machinery goes with its last caller.
The memory file layer learns R12 (`MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered`), its readers treat an unregistered project
as empty, "known projects" come from `projects::list()`, and the memory partition moves with the store (no
`.gitignore`, a link at `projects/` refuses it). Fixtures 02/03/04 and every test that writes under a project
scope are moved to the new layout, each holding its crate's home-store guard. What S3 leaves to S4: the
partition key by project id (R18), snapshot binding (R19), `adopt` by id (R20), index schema 6 (R21), the doctor's
move states, and the `nth(4)` site in `adopt` and the `is_dir()` in `classify_move_snapshots` — so between S3 and
S4 a re-pointed project's notes read as quarantined (unreleased commits only).

### Order and why

Every commit is green. Independent work first (S3.1–S3.6), then the tests are made to register their projects
while the old layout still stands (S3.7), then the PATCH re-cut with the move machinery it was the last caller
of (S3.8 — before R12, because the move tests open partitions at destinations nobody registered), then the two
memory-layer changes that hold on both sides of the flip (S3.9 R12, S3.10 known projects), then the flip itself
(S3.11), Reveal (S3.12) and the slice gate (S3.13). The flip cannot be cut smaller: `store_root`, both `put`s'
addresses, the memory partition path and the purge guard break together the moment `store_root` changes.

| Task | Crates touched | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| S3.1 migration 003 | storage, docs/api | — |
| S3.2 R17 | storage | S1 (`register` in its test) |
| S3.3 CLI `--file` header | CLI | — |
| S3.4 `repoint_rows` | storage | — |
| S3.5 `project_life` | storage, docs/api | S1, S2 (`resolve`), S3.4 |
| S3.6 boot recovery | daemon | S3.5 |
| S3.7 guard audit | storage, core, daemon (tests) | S1, S2 |
| S3.8 PATCH re-cut | daemon, storage, core | S3.5, S3.7 |
| S3.9 R12 in memory | storage, core, CLI | S3.7, S3.8 |
| S3.10 known projects | core, storage | S3.9 |
| S3.11 the flip | storage, core, daemon | S3.1–S3.10 |
| S3.12 Reveal | storage | S3.11 |
| S3.13 slice gate (no commit) | — | all |

### Rules every task carries

- One cargo process at a time; `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`, never `--workspace`. Never run the offline
  memory eval as a gate (`no-offline-harness-gate`); `cargo check -p openalpaca_core --features live-eval --tests`
  is compile only.
- A test that touches a store holds its crate's guard: `crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard` (storage),
  `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard` (core, daemon), `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox` (CLI). S1's `test-home-guard`
  feature makes `projects::register` panic in any test build whose home is unset or the real one — that panic
  is how a missed test announces itself. Never `~/.openalpaca`, never a real repository, never `localhost:11434`.
- No `&s[..n]`; `set_var` only inside the guards. Anchored edits (the `Edit` tool or `perl -pi -e` with an
  exactly-once assertion), never BSD `sed -i`.
- A migration or a new storage top-level module regenerates `docs/api` with `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py`
  in the same commit, and `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check` prints no drift after it.
- Commit messages: conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line, and the trailer
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

```rust
    let elsewhere = fx.put_in(&other_scope, "owner-1", "notes.txt", b"hello");

    assert!(!project.deduped, "a home row never answers a project's turn");
    assert!(!elsewhere.deduped, "one project's row never answers another's turn");
    assert_ne!(project.asset.id, home.asset.id);
    assert_ne!(elsewhere.asset.id, project.asset.id);
    assert_eq!(fx.address(&home.asset.id).0, None);
    assert_eq!(
        fx.address(&project.asset.id).0.as_deref(),
        fx.project_root().to_str()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        fx.address(&elsewhere.asset.id).0.as_deref(),
        other_root.to_str()
    );

    // Inside one store, dedup still holds — at home and in a project.
    let again_home = fx.put("owner-1", "other-name.txt", b"hello");
    assert!(again_home.deduped);
    assert_eq!(again_home.asset.id, home.asset.id);
    let again_project = fx.put_in(&fx.project_scope(), "owner-1", "x.txt", b"hello");
    assert!(again_project.deduped);
    assert_eq!(again_project.asset.id, project.asset.id);
}
```
