```rust
/// The dedup answer: this owner's own *upload* row for these bytes **in this
/// store**, if it has one.
///
/// Every predicate is in the SQL, because `idx_file_assets_sha256` is not
/// unique and `LIMIT 1` picks a row rather than *the* row. Filtering the owner
/// in Rust afterwards meant a second owner was handed the first owner's row,
/// failed the check, and wrote a new row and a new file every single time.
/// `origin` is here for the same reason: a produced artifact can be
/// byte-identical to an upload, and answering with it would hand the uploader a
/// row that is not an upload. `project_root` is here because dedup is scoped to
/// the turn's project (R17): matched across every store, one project's turn was
/// handed a row that belongs to another, and a delete of that project took the
/// file out of the other's transcript. `COALESCE(project_root, '')` is the
/// address baseline every writer shares (`store::project_root_of`).
fn load_by_sha256(
    conn: &Connection,
    sha256: &str,
    owner_id: &str,
    project_root: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Option<FileAsset>> {
    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&format!(
        "SELECT {FILE_ASSET_COLUMNS} FROM file_assets
         WHERE sha256 = ?1 AND owner_id = ?2 AND origin = 'upload'
           AND COALESCE(project_root, '') = ?3
         LIMIT 1"
    ))?;
    let mut rows = stmt.query(rusqlite::params![
        sha256,
        owner_id,
        project_root.unwrap_or("")
    ])?;
    match rows.next()? {
        Some(row) => Ok(Some(row_to_file_asset(row)?)),
        None => Ok(None),
    }
}
```

            // never the path.

```rust
    /// POST /v1/files/upload — Upload a file via multipart form, with the
    /// turn's per-request headers. `x-workspace-path` puts the upload in the
    /// same project as the turn it is attached to (design §4) — the same rule
    /// as [`Self::post_with_headers`]: per request, never a default header.
    pub async fn upload_file(
        &self,
        path: &std::path::Path,
        headers: &[(&str, String)],
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
        use reqwest::multipart;

        let filename = path
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "file".to_string());

        let data = tokio::fs::read(path)
            .await
            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read file: {}", path.display()))?;

        let mime = mime_guess::from_path(path)
            .first_or_octet_stream()
            .to_string();

        let part = multipart::Part::bytes(data)
            .file_name(filename)
            .mime_str(&mime)?;

        let form = multipart::Form::new().part("file", part);

        let url = format!("{}/v1/files/upload", self.base_url);
        let mut request = self.http.post(&url).multipart(form);
        for (name, value) in headers {
            request = request.header(*name, value);
        }
        let resp = check_response(request.send().await?).await?;
        Ok(resp.json().await?)
    }
```

/// headers the turn itself sends ([`ChatTarget::headers`]).
async fn upload_files(

    files: &[std::path::PathBuf],

) -> Result<Vec<serde_json::Value>> {

  Add, right after it:

```rust
    /// §6 step 2: one transaction moves every row naming `old_root` in the
    /// five path columns to `new_root`, and rewrites `storage_path` on the
    /// rows whose `project_root` is `old_root` — `old_dir` (the project's
    /// folder under `projects/`) becomes `new_dir`, and, for Stage 2's pointer
    /// rows, `old_root` becomes `new_root`. A prefix counts only when a `/` or
    /// a `\` follows it, compared with `substr`, never `LIKE` (whose `_` and
    /// `%` a path may hold). `rel_path` is the address and does not change.
    ///
    /// `missing_since` is cleared with the address it described: the mark
    /// says "nothing is at `storage_path`", and this rewrites `storage_path`.
    /// No stat pass inside the transaction (R32) — the read path re-stamps.
    ///
    /// `file_assets` goes **last**: `idx_file_assets_addr` is
    /// (`project_root`, `rel_path`), the one unique key a re-point can
    /// violate, and the failure that rolls the transaction back must have the
    /// other four to roll back. Path-scoped, not owner-scoped: `session` and
    /// `task` carry no `owner_id`; the route refuses a root holding another
    /// owner's rows ([`WorkspaceRows::other_owners`]) before calling this.
    /// Idempotent: run again after it committed, it matches nothing.
    pub fn repoint_rows(
        &self,
        old_root: &str,
        new_root: &str,
        old_dir: &str,
        new_dir: &str,
    ) -> Result<RebaseCounts> {
        self.db.with_connection(|conn| {
            let tx = conn.unchecked_transaction()?;
            let roots = rusqlite::params![old_root, new_root];
            let sessions = tx.execute(
                "UPDATE session SET workspace_id = ?2, updated_at = datetime('now')
                  WHERE workspace_id = ?1",
                roots,
            )?;
            let tasks = tx.execute(
                "UPDATE task SET workspace_id = ?2, updated_at = datetime('now')
                  WHERE workspace_id = ?1",
                roots,
            )?;
            let messages = tx.execute(
                "UPDATE conversation_messages SET workspace_root = ?2 WHERE workspace_root = ?1",
                roots,
            )?;
            let followups = tx.execute(
                "UPDATE lane_followups SET workspace_path = ?2, updated_at = datetime('now')
                  WHERE workspace_path = ?1",
                roots,
            )?;
            let file_assets = tx.execute(
                "UPDATE file_assets
                    SET project_root = ?2,
                        storage_path = CASE
                            WHEN substr(storage_path, 1, length(?3) + 1) IN (?3 || '/', ?3 || '\\')
                            THEN ?4 || substr(storage_path, length(?3) + 1)
                            WHEN substr(storage_path, 1, length(?1) + 1) IN (?1 || '/', ?1 || '\\')
                            THEN ?2 || substr(storage_path, length(?1) + 1)
                            ELSE storage_path END,
                        missing_since = NULL,
                        updated_at = datetime('now')
                  WHERE project_root = ?1",
                rusqlite::params![old_root, new_root, old_dir, new_dir],
            )?;
            tx.commit()?;
            Ok(RebaseCounts {
                file_assets,
                sessions,
                tasks,
                messages,
                followups,
            })
        })
    }

use super::*;
use crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard;
use tempfile::{TempDir, tempdir};

/// A temp home store (through the crate's guard), a sibling `work/` where the
/// projects live, and a temp database. Nothing here touches a real store.
struct World {
    _tmp: TempDir,
    _env: HomeStoreGuard,
    home: PathBuf,
    work: PathBuf,
    db: Database,
}

impl World {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let tmp = tempdir().unwrap();
        let root = tmp.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
        let home = root.join("home");
        let work = root.join("work");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&work).unwrap();
        let env = HomeStoreGuard::set(&home);
        let db = Database::open(&root.join("db").join("test.db")).unwrap();
        Self {
            _tmp: tmp,
            _env: env,
            home,
            work,
            db,
        }
    }

    fn dir(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = self.work.join(name);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        dir
    }

        projects::register(&self.dir(name)).unwrap()
    }

    fn rows_of(&self, p: &Project) {
        let root = p.root_string();
        let bytes = p.dir.join("artifacts").join("loose").join("01-notes.md");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(bytes.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&bytes, "notes\n").unwrap();
        self.db
            .with_connection(|conn| {

                     VALUES ('s-1', 'u:gui', 'gui', ?1)",

                )?;
                conn.execute(

                     VALUES ('t-1', 't', 'u', 'u:gui', ?1, 'completed')",

                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO conversation_messages
                         (lane_key, role, content, session_id, workspace_root)
                     VALUES ('u:gui', 'user', 'hi', 's-1', ?1)",

                conn.execute(

                         (lane_key, kind, content, principal_json, workspace_path)

#[test]
fn a_re_point_renames_the_folder_and_moves_every_row() {
    let w = World::new();
    let before = w.project("app");
    w.rows_of(&before);
    let new = w.dir("app-moved");

    let done = repoint(&w.db, &before.root, &new).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(done.before, before);
    assert_eq!(done.after.id, before.id, "the id is the project's for good (ST-13)");
    assert_eq!(done.after.root, new);
    assert_eq!(done.after.name, projects::folder_name(&new));
    assert_eq!(
        (done.after.previous_root.clone(), done.after.previous_name.clone()),
        (None, None),
        "step 4 cleared the marker"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        done.rows,
        RebaseCounts {
            file_assets: 1,
            sessions: 1,
            tasks: 1,
            messages: 1,
            followups: 1,
        }
    );
    assert!(!before.dir.exists(), "the old folder was renamed");
    assert_eq!(projects::lookup(&new).unwrap(), Some(done.after.clone()));
    assert_eq!(projects::lookup(&before.root).unwrap(), None);
    assert_eq!(w.named(&before.root), 0);
    assert_eq!(w.named(&new), 5);
    let moved = w.storage_path();
    assert!(
        moved.starts_with(done.after.dir.to_string_lossy().as_ref()),
        "{moved}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read_to_string(&moved).unwrap(),
        "notes\n",
        "the bytes are where the row says"
    );
}

/// R24: a re-point stopped after any of its four steps — a crash, here the
/// checkpoint — is finished by the next recovery, and a second recovery has
/// nothing to do. After step 4 there is nothing left to finish.
#[test]
fn a_re_point_stopped_after_any_step_is_finished_by_the_next_recovery() {
    for step in [
        RepointStep::Marked,
        RepointStep::RowsRewritten,
        RepointStep::Renamed,
        RepointStep::Cleared,
    ] {
        let w = World::new();
        let before = w.project("app");
        w.rows_of(&before);
        let new = w.dir("app-moved");

        let err = repoint_with(&w.db, &before.root, &new, &mut |at| at != step).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err.downcast_ref::<RepointInterrupted>(),
            Some(&RepointInterrupted(step))
        );

        let report = recover_repoints(&w.db);
        let finished = if step == RepointStep::Cleared {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            vec![new.clone()]
        };
        assert_eq!(
            report,
            RecoveryReport {
                finished,
                failed: Vec::new(),
            },
            "{step:?}"
        );

        let after = projects::lookup(&new)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{step:?}: the project is found at its new path"));
        assert_eq!(after.id, before.id);
        assert_eq!(after.name, projects::folder_name(&new));
        assert_eq!((after.previous_root.clone(), after.previous_name.clone()), (None, None));
        assert!(!before.dir.exists(), "{step:?}");
        assert_eq!(w.named(&new), 5, "{step:?}");
        assert!(w.storage_path().starts_with(after.dir.to_string_lossy().as_ref()));
        assert_eq!(
            recover_repoints(&w.db),
            RecoveryReport::default(),
            "{step:?}: a second boot finds nothing to do"
        );
    }
}

```rust
//! A project's life once it is registered (design §6): the re-point, and the
//! boot recovery of one that did not finish (R24). Stage 1 step (5) adds the
//! delete here.
//!
//! Database and files only. What storage cannot see stays with the caller:
//! the memory service's `quiesce` and the lane registry's live-run check are
//! the route's (`PATCH /v1/workspaces`).
//!
//! Lock order (interfaces §1.5): [`projects::lock`] first, then the database
//! mutex — the re-point holds the first across its one transaction, so
//! nothing here may take the projects lock inside a `with_connection`.

use std::fmt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};

use crate::Database;
use crate::artifacts::{ArtifactStore, RebaseCounts};
use crate::content_io::fsync_dir;
use crate::store::projects::{self, Project, ProjectError, ProjectFile, ProjectsLock};

/// §6's four steps, each named for what has just happened.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RepointStep {
    /// 1: `project.json` names the new root, with `previous_root` and
    /// `previous_name`.
    Marked,
    /// 2: the five path columns and both `storage_path` prefixes, in one
    /// transaction.
    RowsRewritten,
    /// 3: `projects/<previous_name>` renamed to the new name.
    Renamed,
    /// 4: `project.json` without the two keys.
    Cleared,
}

/// A finished re-point: the project as it was and as it is, and the rows
/// that moved.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Repointed {
    pub before: Project,
    pub after: Project,
    pub rows: RebaseCounts,
}

/// A re-point the test checkpoint stopped (R24's crash hook), returned inside
/// the `anyhow::Error`. The disk is exactly as that step left it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RepointInterrupted(pub RepointStep);

impl fmt::Display for RepointInterrupted {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "the re-point stopped after {:?}", self.0)
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for RepointInterrupted {}

/// What [`recover_repoints`] did.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecoveryReport {
    /// The new roots of the re-points finished.
    pub finished: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Re-points that failed again, by new root, with why. Tried again at the
    /// next boot.
    pub failed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,
}

/// §6 *Re-point*: the project `old_path` resolves to is now at `new_path`.
///
/// Under [`projects::lock`] for the whole call. `old_path` must resolve to a
/// registered project ([`ProjectError::NotRegistered`]). `new_path`,
/// canonicalized, must be a directory ([`ProjectError::NotADirectory`] — a
/// mistyped path is never created), must not overlap the home store
/// ([`ProjectError::IsHome`]), must differ from the project's root
/// ([`ProjectError::SamePath`]), and must be neither a registered project nor
/// named by any of the five path columns ([`ProjectError::Exists`], ST-20).
/// Then: 1 the file is marked; 2 one transaction moves the rows (a failure
/// clears the marker and returns the error); 3 the folder is renamed (its new
/// name is free or this project's own, R6); 4 the marker is cleared.
pub fn repoint(db: &Database, old_path: &Path, new_path: &Path) -> Result<Repointed> {
    repoint_with(db, old_path, new_path, &mut |_| true)
}

/// [`repoint`] with R24's crash hook: `checkpoint` runs after each step, and
/// `false` stops there with [`RepointInterrupted`] and the disk as that step
/// left it. Production passes `|_| true`.
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn repoint_with(
    db: &Database,
    old_path: &Path,
    new_path: &Path,
    checkpoint: &mut dyn FnMut(RepointStep) -> bool,
) -> Result<Repointed> {
    let held = projects::lock();
    let before = registered(old_path)?;
    let new_root = target_root(db, &before, new_path)?;

    let mut marked = before.file();
    marked.root = new_root.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    marked.previous_root = Some(before.root_string());
    marked.previous_name = Some(before.name.clone());
    projects::write_project_file(&before.dir, &marked)?;
    stop(checkpoint, RepointStep::Marked)?;

    let (after, rows) = finish(db, &before.dir, &marked, &held, checkpoint, OnRowsFailure::ClearMarker)?;
    Ok(Repointed {
        before,
        after,
        rows,
    })
}

/// R24, at boot, before anything resolves a project: every folder under
/// `projects/` whose `project.json` carries `previous_root` is a re-point
/// that did not finish, and steps 2–4 run again — each idempotent. A failure
/// is reported and left for the next boot.
pub fn recover_repoints(db: &Database) -> RecoveryReport {
    let held = projects::lock();
    let mut report = RecoveryReport::default();
    let entries = match projects::list() {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        Err(e) => {
            let dir = projects::projects_dir().unwrap_or_default();
            report.failed.push((dir, format!("{e:#}")));
            return report;
        }
    };
    for entry in entries.iter().filter(|p| p.previous_root.is_some()) {
        match finish(db, &entry.dir, &entry.file(), &held, &mut |_| true, OnRowsFailure::Leave) {
            Ok((after, _)) => report.finished.push(after.root),
            Err(e) => report.failed.push((entry.root.clone(), format!("{e:#}"))),
        }
    }
    report
}

/// What step 2's failure does to the marker: a re-point the caller asked for
/// clears it ("nothing else changed"); a recovery leaves it for the next boot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum OnRowsFailure {
    ClearMarker,
    Leave,
}

/// The project `old_path` resolves to, or [`ProjectError::NotRegistered`].
fn registered(old_path: &Path) -> Result<Project> {
    match projects::resolve(old_path)? {
        Some(projects::ResolvedProject {
            project: Some(project),
            ..
        }) => Ok(project),
        Some(resolved) => Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::NotRegistered {
            root: resolved.root_string(),
        })),
        None => Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::NotRegistered {
            root: old_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        })),
    }
}

/// The canonical new root, or the refusal §6 names for it.
fn target_root(db: &Database, before: &Project, new_path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let written = new_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let root = match new_path.is_absolute().then(|| std::fs::canonicalize(new_path)) {
        Some(Ok(root)) if root.is_dir() => root,
        _ => return Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::NotADirectory { path: written })),
    };
    let text = root.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    if projects::overlaps_home_store(&root) {
        return Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::IsHome { path: text }));
    }
    if root == before.root {
        return Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::SamePath { path: text }));
    }
    let named = !ArtifactStore::new(db)
        .workspace_rows(&text, None)?
        .counts
        .is_empty();
    if named || projects::lookup(&root)?.is_some() {
        return Err(anyhow::Error::new(ProjectError::Exists { path: text }));
    }
    Ok(root)
}

/// Steps 2–4 for the marked `project.json` in `dir` (the folder it is in
/// now). Each step is idempotent, so recovery runs this same function.
fn finish(
    db: &Database,
    dir: &Path,
    marked: &ProjectFile,
    held: &ProjectsLock,
    checkpoint: &mut dyn FnMut(RepointStep) -> bool,
    on_rows_failure: OnRowsFailure,
) -> Result<(Project, RebaseCounts)> {
    let (Some(old_root), Some(old_name)) = (
        marked.previous_root.as_deref(),
        marked.previous_name.as_deref(),
    ) else {
        bail!("{} carries no re-point to finish", dir.display());
    };
    let parent = dir
        .parent()
        .with_context(|| format!("{} has no parent", dir.display()))?;
    let current = dir
        .file_name()
        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
        .with_context(|| format!("{} has no folder name", dir.display()))?;
    let new_root = PathBuf::from(&marked.root);
    // After step 3 the folder already has its new name; before it, the name
    // is chosen now, under the lock — free, or this project's own (R6).
    let new_name = if current != old_name {
        current.to_string()
    } else {
        projects::name_for(&new_root, Some(&marked.id), held)?
    };
    let old_dir = parent.join(old_name);
    let new_dir = parent.join(&new_name);

    // Step 2.
    let rows = match ArtifactStore::new(db).repoint_rows(
        old_root,
        &marked.root,
        &old_dir.to_string_lossy(),
        &new_dir.to_string_lossy(),
    ) {
        Ok(rows) => rows,
        Err(e) => {
            let e = e.context(format!(
                "the rows of {old_root} could not be re-pointed onto {}",
                marked.root
            ));
            if on_rows_failure == OnRowsFailure::ClearMarker {
                let mut cleared = marked.clone();
                cleared.root = old_root.to_string();
                cleared.previous_root = None;
                cleared.previous_name = None;
                if let Err(undo) = projects::write_project_file(dir, &cleared) {
                    return Err(e.context(format!(
                        "and {} still names the new root ({undo:#}); the next start finishes the re-point",
                        dir.join(projects::PROJECT_FILE).display()
                    )));
                }
            }
            return Err(e);
        }
    };
    stop(checkpoint, RepointStep::RowsRewritten)?;

    // Step 3.
    if dir != new_dir {
        std::fs::rename(dir, &new_dir).with_context(|| {
            format!("could not rename {} to {}", dir.display(), new_dir.display())
        })?;
        fsync_dir(parent);
    }
    stop(checkpoint, RepointStep::Renamed)?;

    // Step 4.
    let mut cleared = marked.clone();
    cleared.previous_root = None;
    cleared.previous_name = None;
    projects::write_project_file(&new_dir, &cleared)?;
    stop(checkpoint, RepointStep::Cleared)?;

    let after = projects::read_project_dir(&new_dir)?.with_context(|| {
        format!("{} has no readable project.json after the re-point", new_dir.display())
    })?;
    Ok((after, rows))
}

fn stop(checkpoint: &mut dyn FnMut(RepointStep) -> bool, step: RepointStep) -> Result<()> {
    if checkpoint(step) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(anyhow::Error::new(RepointInterrupted(step)))
    }
}

```rust
//! R24: a project re-point the previous process did not finish is finished
//! at boot — after the database opens, before anything resolves a project
//! (design §6, *Re-point*).

use openalpaca_storage::Database;
use openalpaca_storage::project_life;
use tracing::{info, warn};

/// Runs [`project_life::recover_repoints`] and says what it did: one INFO per
/// re-point finished, one WARN per failure naming the project. A failure
/// never stops the boot — the next one tries again.
pub fn recover_repoints(db: &Database) {
    let report = project_life::recover_repoints(db);
    for root in &report.finished {
        info!(
            "Finished re-pointing the project now at {}",
            root.display()
        );
    }
    for (root, reason) in &report.failed {
        warn!(
            "Could not finish re-pointing the project now at {}: {reason}; it is tried again at the next boot",
            root.display()
        );
    }
}
```

    // finished here — after the database opens and before anything resolves
    // a project (the routes and every ingress start later).
    bootstrap::recover_repoints(&db);

### Task S3.7: Every test that writes under a project scope registers the project first (the guard audit)

This task changes tests only, so its test cycle is the audit: today's tests build `<project>/.openalpaca` paths
by hand and write under projects nobody registered. After it, every test that writes under
`StoreScope::Project(_)` — directly, or through the memory service with a hand-made `.git` root — registers the
project under its crate's guard, and every *positive* path it computes inside a project store goes through
`store::store_root`. Both hold before and after the flip (before it `store_root` is still
`<root>/.openalpaca`), so S3.9 (R12) and S3.11 (the flip) change no test's setup. Negative assertions such as

    /// A workspace directory under the temp root with an optional marker. A
    /// `.git` workspace is a project and is registered (design §3), as the
    /// daemon's turn there would have done — under this harness's home.
    pub(super) fn workspace(&self, name: &str, marker: Option<&str>) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = self.root.path().join("ws").join(name);
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        if let Some(m) = marker {
            fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(m)).unwrap();
        }
        let dir = dir.canonicalize().unwrap();
        if marker == Some(".git") {
            openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register(&dir).unwrap();
        }
        dir
    }

    /// A registered project's store directory — where its `memory/` is.
    pub(super) fn store_dir(&self, root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        openalpaca_storage::store::store_root(&StoreScope::Project(root.to_path_buf())).unwrap()
    }

```rust
/// A scratch project: a directory with a `.git` marker, canonical, and
/// registered under the scratch store as the daemon's first turn there would
/// register it (storage design §3), so its notes have a folder under the
/// store's `projects/`.
fn scratch_project(under: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let project = under.join("project");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(project.join(".git")).expect("scratch project marker");
    let project = project.canonicalize().expect("canonical scratch project");
    openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register(&project).expect("register the scratch project");
    project
}
```

```rust
/// What an earlier build's in-project `.layout` says, written by hand. The
/// GET still reads it until Stage 1 step (5) removes `store_present`,
/// `recorded_root` and `moved` (interfaces C8).
fn earlier_build_marker(root: &str, recorded: &str) {
    let dir = std::path::Path::new(root).join(store::STORE_DIR_NAME);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("store dir");
    std::fs::write(dir.join(".layout"), format!("1\nproject_root={recorded}\n")).expect("marker");
}

fn project_at(root: &str) -> projects::Project {
    projects::lookup(std::path::Path::new(root))
        .expect("lookup")
        .expect("a registered project")
}
```

/// The user moved the project's folder with `mv`: the re-point moves its rows
/// and renames its folder under `projects/`; the id stays (ST-13).
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_project_moved_by_hand_is_re_pointed_with_its_rows_and_its_folder() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let old = f.project("old-project");
    let before = project_at(&old);
    f.artifact(&old, "Notes");
    f.session("session-1", &old);
    f.task("task-1", &old, "completed");
    let new_dir = f.projects.path().join("new-project");
    std::fs::rename(&old, &new_dir).expect("the user's mv");
    let new = new_dir
        .canonicalize()
        .expect("canonicalize")
        .to_string_lossy()
        .into_owned();

    let (status, body) = f.patch(&old, &new).await;
    assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
    assert_eq!(body["old_path"], old);
    assert_eq!(body["new_path"], new);
    assert_eq!(body["moved"]["artifacts"], 1);
    assert_eq!(body["moved"]["sessions"], 1);
    assert_eq!(body["moved"]["tasks"], 1);
    assert_eq!(body["store_moved"], true, "the folder under projects/ was renamed");

    let after = project_at(&new);
    assert_eq!(after.id, before.id);
    assert!(!before.dir.exists());
    assert!(projects::lookup(std::path::Path::new(&old)).unwrap().is_none());
    let (_, at_new) = f.get(Some(&new)).await;
    assert_eq!(at_new["rows"]["artifacts"], 1);
    assert_eq!(at_new["rows"]["sessions"], 1);
    let (_, at_old) = f.get(Some(&old)).await;
    assert_eq!(at_old["rows"]["artifacts"], 0);
    let record = ArtifactStore::new(&f.db)
        .list(&openalpaca_storage::ArtifactQuery::new(OWNER))
        .expect("list")
        .0
        .remove(0);
    assert!(
        std::path::Path::new(&record.storage_path).exists(),
        "{} does not exist",
        record.storage_path
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_re_point_while_a_memory_write_is_pending_is_refused() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let old = f.project("old-project");
    let before = project_at(&old);
    let new = f.bare_dir("new-project");
    f.artifact(&old, "Notes");

    let pending = f
        .memory
        .quiesce(std::path::Path::new(&old))
        .expect("nothing is writing yet");
    let (status, body) = f.patch(&old, &new).await;
    assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::CONFLICT, "{body}");
    assert_eq!(error_code(&body), "WORKSPACE_BUSY");
    assert!(
        body["error"]["message"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().contains("memory"),
        "{body}"
    );
    assert_eq!(project_at(&old), before, "project.json was never marked");
    let (_, rows) = f.get(Some(&old)).await;
    assert_eq!(rows["rows"]["artifacts"], 1);

    drop(pending);
    let (status, body) = f.patch(&old, &new).await;
    assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
}

```rust
// ── PATCH /v1/workspaces ─────────────────────────────────────────

/// A [`ProjectError`] anywhere in `e`'s chain, as the route answers it, or
/// `None` for any other failure (interfaces §6.1): not registered `404`, the
/// home store `409`, not a directory `422`, already a project `409`, the
/// same path `400` — each with the error's own sentence.
pub(crate) fn project_error_response(e: &anyhow::Error) -> Option<Response> {
    let error = e
        .chain()
        .find_map(|cause| cause.downcast_ref::<ProjectError>())?;
    let status = match error {
        ProjectError::NotRegistered { .. } => StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
        ProjectError::IsHome { .. } | ProjectError::Exists { .. } => StatusCode::CONFLICT,
        ProjectError::NotADirectory { .. } => StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
        ProjectError::SamePath { .. } => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
    };
    Some(api_error(status, error.code(), error.to_string()))
}

/// Re-point a project onto the folder it is in now (design §6): the route's
/// half — the owner check, the in-flight check, the memory quiesce — then
/// [`project_life::repoint`], which refuses a new path that is not a
/// directory, overlaps the home store, is the same path, or is already a
/// project or named by rows (ST-20), and otherwise rewrites the five path
/// columns and both `storage_path` prefixes in one transaction and renames
/// the project's folder under `projects/`.
///
/// Owner-scoped like every injecting write (R40): a path no project owns and
/// a project holding another owner's rows answer the same `404`, in the same
/// words. Until Stage 1 step (4) keys memory by the project's id, a
/// re-pointed project's notes stay keyed by its old folder (unreleased
/// commits only).
pub(crate) fn rebase_workspace(
    db: &Database,
    memory: &MemoryService,
    owner_id: &str,
    request: RebaseRequest,
) -> Response {
    let old_path = match canonical_path(&request.old_path) {
        Ok(path) => path,
        Err(response) => return response,
    };
    let new_path = match canonical_path(&request.new_path) {
        Ok(path) => path,
        Err(response) => return response,
    };
    let project = match projects::resolve(Path::new(&old_path)) {
        Ok(Some(ResolvedProject {
            project: Some(project),
            ..
        })) => project,
        Ok(_) => {
            return api_error(
                StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
                "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND",
                format!("nothing of yours is recorded under {old_path}"),
            );
        }
        Err(e) => {
            return api_error(
                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                "WORKSPACE_MOVE_FAILED",
                format!("{e:#}"),
            );
        }
    };
    let old_root = project.root_string();

    let store = ArtifactStore::new(db);
    let rows = match store.workspace_rows(&old_root, Some(owner_id)) {
        Ok(rows) => rows,
        Err(e) => return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", e.to_string()),
    };
    if rows.other_owners > 0 {
        return owner_mismatch(&old_root, rows.other_owners);
    }
    if rows.active_tasks > 0 {
        return api_error(
            StatusCode::CONFLICT,
            "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
            format!(
                "{} run(s) under {old_root} are still in flight; a running or paused run \
                 resolved its store when it started, and re-pointing the row would not move it",
                rows.active_tasks
            ),
        );
    }

    // Held until this function returns: every memory write for the project
    // waits, and one already in flight refuses the re-point.
    let _quiesced = match memory.quiesce(Path::new(&old_root)) {
        Ok(guard) => guard,
        Err(e) => {
            return api_error(
                StatusCode::CONFLICT,
                "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
                format!(
                    "a memory write under {old_root} is still in flight ({e}); re-pointing now \
                     would move its folder out from under it. Try again in a moment"
                ),
            );
        }
    };

    match project_life::repoint(db, Path::new(&old_root), Path::new(&new_path)) {
        Ok(done) => Json(serde_json::json!({
            "old_path": done.before.root_string(),
            "new_path": done.after.root_string(),
            "moved": counts_json(&done.rows),
            "store_moved": done.before.name != done.after.name,
        }))
        .into_response(),
        Err(e) => project_error_response(&e).unwrap_or_else(|| {
            api_error(
                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                "WORKSPACE_MOVE_FAILED",
                format!("{old_root} was not re-pointed onto {new_path}: {e:#}"),
            )
        }),
    }
}
```

  - replace the module doc (lines `//! \`/v1/workspaces\` — §4.8's "Project moved", as a route.` through the
    paragraph ending "…a purge of the whole project for a path that named one file of it.") with:

```rust
//! `/v1/workspaces` — a project's life (design §6), as routes.
//!
//! ```text
//! GET   /v1/workspaces?path=<abs>          -> what is recorded at that root
//! PATCH /v1/workspaces {old_path,new_path} -> re-point a project onto its new folder
//! POST  /v1/workspaces/purge {path|all}    -> delete one project's history
//! ```
//!
//! A project's canonical path is its identity in five row columns
//! (`task.workspace_id`, `session.workspace_id`,
//! `conversation_messages.workspace_root`, `lane_followups.workspace_path`,
//! `file_assets.project_root`) and in `file_assets.storage_path`'s prefix, so a
//! folder moved by hand strands them until it is re-pointed. The re-point is
//! `project_life::repoint`: the project's `project.json` marked, one
//! transaction, the folder under `projects/` renamed, the marker cleared — and
//! a crash between two steps is finished at the next boot (R24). The route
//! owns the checks storage cannot see: the owner (R40), the runs in flight and
//! the memory service's quiesce.
//!
//! The `GET` and the purge keep their pre-design shapes until Stage 1 step
//! (5) (interfaces §6, C8): the `GET` still reads an earlier build's in-project
//! `.layout` for `recorded_root` and `moved`, and the purge still resolves its
//! path by rows and the marker walk (R72, R75). `dry_run` defaults to **true**
//! on the purge — the daemon fails closed.

/// R12: a root with no folder under `projects/` has no partition. Every way
/// in — the open, the read-only open, the key, the owner listing — answers
/// `NotRegistered` naming the root, and nothing is created anywhere.
#[test]
fn an_unregistered_project_root_has_no_partition_and_nothing_is_created() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let stray = sb.outside.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let scope = StoreScope::Project(stray.clone());

    let err = Partition::open(&scope, ALICE).err().expect("refused");
    assert!(
        matches!(&err, MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { root } if root == &stray),
        "{err:?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(err.class(), "fixture:not_registered");
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("is not registered"), "{err}");
    assert!(matches!(
        Partition::open_readonly(&scope, &owner_key(ALICE)),
        Err(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { .. })
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        partition_key_for(&scope, &owner_key(ALICE)),
        Err(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { .. })
    ));
    let listed = list_owner_keys(&scope).unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        matches!(
            listed.downcast_ref::<MemoryFilesError>(),
            Some(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { .. })
        ),
        "{listed:#}"
    );
    assert!(sb.outside_is_empty(), "nothing in the folder");
}

```rust
/// The store directory a partition of `scope` lives under, and the
/// components above its `memory/` that [`Partition::open`] checks before any
/// below (design §3 rule 1). The home root is the store's own and is not
/// checked. A project is R12's question first: a root with no folder under
/// `projects/` has no partition ([`MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered`]),
/// decided before a path is joined, so nothing is created.
fn scope_root(scope: &StoreScope) -> Result<(PathBuf, Vec<PathBuf>), MemoryFilesError> {
    match scope {
        StoreScope::Home => Ok((home_root()?, Vec::new())),
        StoreScope::Project(root) => {
            if !root.is_absolute() {
                return Err(MemoryFilesError::Io(anyhow::anyhow!(
                    "project store root must be an absolute path, got {}",
                    root.display()
                )));
            }
            if projects::lookup(root)?.is_none() {
                return Err(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { root: root.clone() });
            }
            let store = store_root(scope)?;
            Ok((store.clone(), vec![store]))
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// The registered projects in which `owner_id` has a partition directory
    /// (design §5: known projects come from `projects::list()`), sorted —
    /// what the purge's listing and the 30 s reconciliation iterate. Scoped
    /// to the owner like every workspace answer (R40): another owner's
    /// partition in a project of its own does not name that root to this one.
    /// A project whose folder under `projects/` is gone is no project; a
    /// listing failure is logged and lists nothing.
    pub fn known_project_roots(&self, owner_id: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        let owner_key = files::owner_key(owner_id);
        let projects = match openalpaca_storage::store::projects::list() {
            Ok(list) => list,
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    "memory: the projects under projects/ could not be listed, listing no project roots: {e:#}"
                );
                return Vec::new();
            }
        };
        let mut roots: Vec<PathBuf> = projects
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|p| {
                openalpaca_storage::store::store_root(&StoreScope::Project(p.root.clone()))
                    .map(|store| {
                        store
                            .join(ContentKind::Memory.dir_name())
                            .join(files::OWNERS_DIR)
                            .join(&owner_key)
                            .is_dir()
                    })
                    .unwrap_or(false)
            })
            .map(|p| p.root)
            .collect();
        roots.sort();
        roots.dedup();
        roots
    }

/// `projects/`, found by `projects::lookup`; `content_dir` keeps its shape
/// beneath it, and nothing is written into the project's own folder — no

#[test]
fn a_project_store_is_its_folder_under_projects() {

    let root = tmp.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let _guard = HomeStoreGuard::set(&root.join("home"));

    let scope = StoreScope::Project(project.clone());

/// R12: a root with no folder under `projects/` has no store. `store_root`,

#[test]
fn an_unregistered_project_root_has_no_store_and_nothing_is_created() {
    let tmp = tempdir().unwrap();

    let repo = root.join("work").join("repo");
    fs::create_dir_all(repo.join(".git")).unwrap();
    let scope = StoreScope::Project(repo.clone());

    for err in [
        store_root(&scope).unwrap_err(),
        ensure_store(&scope).unwrap_err(),
        content_dir(&scope, ContentKind::Artifacts).unwrap_err(),

        assert!(projects::is_not_registered(&err), "{err:#}");
        assert_eq!(
            err.downcast_ref::<projects::ProjectError>()

    assert_eq!(

        "the folder holds its .git and nothing else"

}

/// R15: a project artifact's bytes land in the project's folder under the
/// home store's `projects/`, and its row records the turn's project root —
/// never the directory the bytes reached. Nothing lands in the project.
#[test]
fn a_project_artifact_lands_under_projects_and_records_the_turns_root() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let mut new = NewArtifact::new(OWNER, &f.scope(), ArtifactKind::Markdown, "Notes", b"a\n");
    new.created = at(1);
    let (record, _) = f.store().put(new).unwrap();

    let folder = f
        .home_root()
        .join(crate::store::projects::PROJECTS_DIR)
        .join(crate::store::projects::folder_name(&f.project_root()));
    assert_eq!(
        PathBuf::from(&record.storage_path),
        folder
            .join("artifacts")
            .join("loose")
            .join("2026-09-01")
            .join("01-notes.md")
    );
    assert_eq!(record.project_root.as_deref(), f.project_root().to_str());
    assert!(!f.project_root().join(".openalpaca").exists(), "ST-1");
}

/// R15/R12: a row whose own columns do not name its store falls back to
/// its scope's store, and that fallback creates nothing — for a project no
/// folder under `projects/` records, nothing at all.
#[test]
fn resolving_a_row_whose_columns_do_not_name_its_store_creates_nothing() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let stray = tempdir().unwrap();
    let stray_root = stray.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    f.db.with_connection(|conn| {
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO file_assets (id, owner_id, sha256, filename, mime_type, size_bytes,
                 storage_path, status, origin, project_root, rel_path)
             VALUES ('stray-row', ?1, 'sha', 'notes.md', 'text/markdown', 1, '/nowhere/x.md',
                     'ready', 'produced', ?2, 'loose/2026-09-01/01-notes.md')",
            rusqlite::params![OWNER, stray_root.to_string_lossy()],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();

    assert!(f.store().resolve_content("stray-row", None).is_err());
    assert!(!stray_root.join(".openalpaca").exists(), "nothing in the folder");
    assert!(
        !f.home_root()
            .join(crate::store::projects::PROJECTS_DIR)
            .join(crate::store::projects::folder_name(&stray_root))
            .exists(),
        "and nothing under projects/"
    );
}

#[test]
fn project_partition_is_created_lazily_in_the_projects_folder_with_private_modes() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let folder = crate::store::projects::lookup(&sb.project_root())

    assert_eq!(p.health(), PartitionHealth::Absent);

    assert!(owner.join("notes").is_dir());
    assert!(owner.join(".history").is_dir());

        let file = p.notes_dir().join(&note_files(&p)[0]);
        assert_eq!(fsx::mode_of(&file), Some(0o600));
    }
    // The key is the same after the artifact path creates `artifacts/` beside it.
    crate::store::content_dir(&sb.project_scope(), crate::store::ContentKind::Artifacts).unwrap();
    let again = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();

#[cfg(unix)]
#[test]
fn a_link_or_file_at_any_component_refuses_the_project_partition() {
    let key = owner_key(ALICE);
    let components = [
        "memory".to_string(),
        "memory/owners".to_string(),
        format!("memory/owners/{key}"),
        format!("memory/owners/{key}/notes"),
        format!("memory/owners/{key}/.history"),
    ];
    for component in &components {
        let sb = Sandbox::new();
        let folder = crate::store::projects::lookup(&sb.project_root())
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .dir;
        let link = folder.join(component);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(link.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        symlink(sb.outside.path(), &link);
        let err = sb
            .open_project(ALICE)
            .err()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{component} must refuse"));
        match &err {
            MemoryFilesError::PathRefused {
                component: named,
                reason,
            } => {
                assert_eq!(named, &link, "names the component");
                assert!(reason.contains("symbolic link"), "{reason}");
            }
            other => panic!("{component}: expected PathRefused, got {other:?}"),
        }
        assert!(sb.outside_is_empty(), "{component}: nothing written through the link");
        assert!(!sb.home.join("memory").exists());
    }
    // A regular file where `memory` should be a directory.
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let folder = crate::store::projects::lookup(&sb.project_root())
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap()
        .dir;
    std::fs::write(folder.join("memory"), "not a directory\n").unwrap();
    let err = sb.open_project(ALICE).expect_err("a file refuses");
    assert!(
        matches!(&err, MemoryFilesError::PathRefused { reason, .. } if reason == "not a directory")
    );
    assert_eq!(read_file(&folder.join("memory")), b"not a directory\n");
    assert_eq!(err.class(), "fixture:path_refused");
}

/// The two levels above a project's `memory/` are the home store's own, and a
/// link at either refuses the partition with nothing written where it leads.
/// A link at `projects/` is followed by `projects::lookup` (S1 checks no
/// component above a project's folder), so the open's component check names
/// it; a link at the project's folder is a folder `lookup` never opens (S1's
/// `read_project_dir`, R11), so the root reads as not registered.
#[cfg(unix)]
#[test]
fn a_link_at_projects_or_at_the_projects_folder_refuses_the_partition() {
    for level in ["projects", "folder"] {
        let sb = Sandbox::new();
        let folder = crate::store::projects::lookup(&sb.project_root())
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .dir;
        let name = folder.file_name().unwrap().to_os_string();
        let link = match level {
            "projects" => folder.parent().unwrap().to_path_buf(),
            _ => folder.clone(),
        };
        // The real directory moves beside `outside`, so the link still leads to
        // the project's project.json; the link takes its place.
        let moved = sb.outside.path().join("moved");
        std::fs::rename(&link, &moved).unwrap();
        symlink(&moved, &link);

        let err = sb
            .open_project(ALICE)
            .err()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{level} must refuse"));
        match (level, &err) {
            ("projects", MemoryFilesError::PathRefused { component, reason }) => {
                assert_eq!(component, &link);
                assert!(reason.contains("symbolic link"), "{reason}");
            }
            ("folder", MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { root }) => {
                assert_eq!(root, &sb.project_root());
            }
            (level, other) => panic!("{level}: unexpected refusal {other:?}"),
        }
        let through_link = match level {
            "projects" => moved.join(&name).join("memory"),
            _ => moved.join("memory"),
        };
        assert!(!through_link.exists(), "{level}: nothing written through the link");
    }
}

```rust
//! The single source of truth for every OpenAlpaca path.
//!
//! There is one root — `~/.openalpaca` (`home_root()`, overridable with
//! `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE`). App state and content with no project live there,
//! and each project's content lives in its own folder under it,
//! `projects/<name>/` (owner decision ST-1; [`projects`] names and finds the
//! folders). Nothing is ever written inside a project's own folder. Both
//! stores have the same shape for content, so `content_dir(scope, kind)` is
//! `root/<kind>` in both cases.
//!
//! ```text
//! ~/.openalpaca/
//!   README.md          seeded once; explains every entry
//!   .layout            line 1: layout version; line 2: install_id=<uuid-v4>
//!   state/             MACHINE STATE — opaque, never user-edited, never committed
//!     openalpaca.db (+ -wal, -shm), discovery.json, openalpacad.lock, .master_key
//!     backups/         rotated copies of hand-edited config files
//!     logs/            daemon.log, gui.log
//!   config/            USER-EDITED runtime config (GUI/CLI-managed daemons)
//!   plugins/           user-dropped plugin dirs + .permissions.toml
//!   projects/<name>/   one folder per project: project.json, artifacts/, uploads/, memory/
//!   artifacts/ uploads/ sessions/ …   content store, home scope
//! ```
```

  (the rule paragraph after it unchanged). `StoreScope`:

```rust
pub enum StoreScope {
    /// A project, named by its canonical root (absolute) — what the resolver
    /// returns, never the store directory. Its content lives in its folder
    /// under `<home>/projects/` (ST-1), found by [`projects::lookup`].
    Project(PathBuf),
    /// `~/.openalpaca` — the no-project fallback.
    Home,
}
```

  `store_root`, `ensure_store`, `content_dir` and `project_root_of` (docs included) become:

```rust
/// The root directory of a store. Creates nothing.
///
/// Home: [`home_root`]. A project: its folder under `projects/` (ST-1) as
/// [`projects::lookup`] finds it — `<home>/projects/<name>`, canonical. A
/// root with no folder there is [`projects::ProjectError::NotRegistered`]
/// inside the error (R12): a reader asks [`projects::is_not_registered`] and
/// treats the project as empty, and nothing is created for it here.
pub fn store_root(scope: &StoreScope) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    match scope {
        StoreScope::Home => home_root(),
        StoreScope::Project(root) => {
            if !root.is_absolute() {
                bail!(
                    "project store root must be an absolute path, got {}",
                    root.display()
                );
            }
            match projects::lookup(root)? {
                Some(project) => Ok(project.dir),
                None => Err(anyhow::Error::new(projects::ProjectError::NotRegistered {
                    root: root.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
                })),
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Creates the home root and seeds its metadata: `README.md` and `.layout`
/// (line 2 `install_id=<uuid-v4>`). Idempotent — each file is written only
/// when absent, so user edits stick.
///
/// A project's folder holds `project.json` and content only (R3) and exists
/// from its registration, so for a project scope this is [`store_root`] and
/// nothing else.
pub fn ensure_store(scope: &StoreScope) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let root = store_root(scope)?;
    if matches!(scope, StoreScope::Project(_)) {
        return Ok(root);
    }
    fs::create_dir_all(&root)
        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to create store root: {}", root.display()))?;
    let readme = root.join(README_FILE);
    if !readme.exists() {
        write_new(&readme, HOME_README)?;
    }
    ensure_layout(&root)?;
    Ok(root)
}
```

```rust
/// `store_root(scope)/<kind>` — created on use (reserved names stay absent
/// until something needs them). A project's folder exists from its
/// registration, so nothing is seeded first; a root with no folder is
/// [`store_root`]'s typed error and nothing is created (R12).
pub fn content_dir(scope: &StoreScope, kind: ContentKind) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let dir = store_root(scope)?.join(kind.dir_name());
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir)
        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to create content directory: {}", dir.display()))?;
    Ok(dir)
}

/// The canonical-path string a content row records as its `project_root`;
/// `None` is the home store, which is the address baseline (§4.8).
///
/// The one place a [`StoreScope`] becomes a stored address, so
/// `COALESCE(project_root, '')` means the same thing to every writer. R15:
/// it is the turn's project, never the directory the bytes reached — under
/// ST-1 that is the project's folder under `projects/` for every project.
pub fn project_root_of(scope: &StoreScope) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    match scope {
        StoreScope::Home => Ok(None),
        StoreScope::Project(root) => {
            let canonical = root.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| root.clone());
            Ok(Some(canonical.to_string_lossy().to_string()))
        }
    }
}
```

  Delete `project_root_at` (doc included), `GITIGNORE_TEXT`, `PROJECT_README` and `readme_text`. `ensure_layout`

```rust
/// Writes the home root's `.layout` when absent — line 1 the layout version,
/// line 2 `install_id=<uuid>` — and repairs an unreadable version line.
/// Nothing is ever added to a marker that exists: it keeps whatever keys it
/// has, and any other line already there is carried through untouched.
fn ensure_layout(root: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let path = root.join(LAYOUT_FILE);
    let existing = match fs::read_to_string(&path) {
        Ok(t) => Some(t),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => None,
        Err(e) => return Err(e).with_context(|| format!("Failed to read {}", path.display())),
    };

    let Some(text) = existing else {
        let fresh = format!(
            "{LAYOUT_VERSION}\n{INSTALL_ID_KEY}={}\n",
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4()
        );
        return write_atomic(&path, &fresh);
    };
```

  `artifacts_root_for` becomes:

```rust
/// `<store>/artifacts` for a record, recovered from its own two address
/// columns so a changed `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` cannot silently re-point a
/// row. A row whose columns do not carry it falls back to its scope's store
/// through [`store_root`] — which creates nothing, and for a project no
/// folder under `projects/` records is R12's `NotRegistered`.
fn artifacts_root_for(record: &ArtifactRecord) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    if let Some(rel) = record.rel_path.as_deref()
        && let Some(prefix) = record.storage_path.strip_suffix(rel)
    {
        let trimmed = prefix.trim_end_matches('/');
        if !trimmed.is_empty() {
            return Ok(PathBuf::from(trimmed));
        }
    }
    let scope = match &record.project_root {
        Some(root) => StoreScope::Project(PathBuf::from(root)),
        None => StoreScope::Home,
    };
    Ok(store_root(&scope)?.join(ContentKind::Artifacts.dir_name()))
}
```

```rust
/// The canonical form of `path` when it may be shown in its folder: a
/// regular file whose canonical path is under the canonical home root
/// ([`home_root`], `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` honoured). Refused: a path that
/// does not resolve, anything that is not a regular file, and a file outside
/// the home root. The canonical path decides, so a symlink is judged by where
/// it leads.
pub fn revealable_path(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, RevealRefusal> {
    revealable_path_with_home(path, home_root().ok().as_deref())
}

/// [`revealable_path`] with the home root passed in, so the rule is testable
/// without reading the environment.
fn revealable_path_with_home(path: &Path, home: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PathBuf, RevealRefusal> {
    let canonical = path
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| RevealRefusal::Missing(path.to_path_buf()))?;
    let is_file = std::fs::metadata(&canonical).is_ok_and(|meta| meta.is_file());
    if !is_file {
        return Err(RevealRefusal::NotAFile(canonical));
    }
    let under_home = home.is_some_and(|home| {
        let home = home.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| home.to_path_buf());
        canonical.starts_with(home)
    });
    if under_home {
        Ok(canonical)
    } else {
        Err(RevealRefusal::OutsideStore(canonical))
    }
}
```

  goes through `Harness::workspace` (`tests.rs`, `tool_suggestion_tests.rs`, `episode_tests.rs`) or a learning

## Stage 1, slice S4 — memory by project id

Draft for the Stage 1 plan. Spec: `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8) §5, §6, §16 step (4); the shared names are
`interfaces.md` (§4, §7.1, §7.2, §7.3), which this draft follows. Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`);
every `file:line` is from that HEAD and is located by content in each step, because S1–S3 land before S4 and move
lines.

### What this slice does

A project's memory partition stops being named by the folder it lies in. Its key becomes
`proj-<owner-key>-<16 hex of sha256(project id)>` (R18), its control snapshot gains an optional `project_id`
written only when set (R19), and a project partition opens only when the id in the `project.json` beside its
`memory/` equals the id in its snapshot — the snapshot's `root` is still recorded but never compared. Because a
re-point renames `projects/<name>/` and rewrites rows but never touches a snapshot or an index row, a project's
notes, origins, tombstones and index rows survive S3's re-point and its boot recovery unchanged; S4 adds the
tests that prove it. The memory index's schema goes to 6 (R21), so every old cache is rebuilt once. Every reader
that still found a project by its snapshot's `root` finds it by id — the index rebuild and the doctor through
`projects::list()`, `adopt` through `projects::by_id` (R20). A `proj-…` snapshot an earlier build wrote carries no id: it is never opened,
never adopted, never deleted, and the doctor lists it (R22). The doctor's stale / abandoned / orphaned move
states, which nothing can produce since S3, go with their CLI code. `MemoryService::quiesce` and every write slot
of a project are keyed by the project id, so one hold covers the old path and the new. Learning and task
extraction drop a chunk only when its root is no longer a registered project; a missing project's turns are
still learned into its notes at home (ST-21). Fixture 17 is rewritten for the re-point. S4 adds no route, no
migration, no CLI verb or flag, no config key and no event; it changes the doctor's wire answer
(`move_snapshots` → `idless_project_snapshots`), which no generated document describes.

**What S4 does not do, and who does** (interfaces.md C1, C6, §6.1, §7.1, §7.3): the re-point core
(`project_life::repoint`, `repoint_with`, `recover_repoints`, `repoint_rows`), R24's boot recovery, the crash
hook's four steps, and the removal of `store/project_move.rs`, `begin_project_move`, `finish_project_move`,
`SnapshotMove`, `project_of_partition_root`, `MemoryService::begin_project_move` / `finish_project_move` /
`known_project_roots`, `MoveStep` and `rebase_workspace_with` are **S3**. `memory/.gitignore`,
`PROJECT_GITIGNORE_TEXT`, `assert_gitignore` and fixtures 03 and 04 are **S3**. The quiesce retry (100 ms for
3 s before `WORKSPACE_BUSY`) is **S5a**'s route helper `quiesce_project`. Fixture 17's step 12 is **S5a**'s.
Manuals, `API_MAP.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the records are **S6**.

```rust
/// R19: a snapshot exactly as today's build writes it — every one carries
/// `"moved_from": null`, none a `project_id` — still loads under
/// `deny_unknown_fields`, binds, and is written back with no `project_id`
/// key, so a home snapshot this build saves stays readable to an earlier
/// one. The schema number is still 1.
#[test]
fn a_snapshot_as_todays_build_writes_it_loads_and_binds() {
    let home_example = SNAPSHOT_EXAMPLE
        .replace(
            "proj-3f9a1c2d4e5b6a7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7-0a1b2c3d4e5f6071",
            "home-3f9a1c2d4e5b6a7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
        )
        .replace("\"scope\": \"project\"", "\"scope\": \"home\"")
        .replace(
            "/Users/x/dev/app/.openalpaca/memory",
            "/Users/x/.openalpaca/memory",
        );
    assert!(home_example.contains("\"moved_from\": null"));
    assert!(!home_example.contains("project_id"));
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = dir.path().join("home-3f9a1c2d4e5b6a7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7.json");
    std::fs::write(&path, &home_example).unwrap();
    let loaded = ControlSnapshot::load(&path).unwrap().expect("the file is there");
    assert_eq!(SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA, 1);
    assert_eq!(loaded.schema, SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA);
    assert_eq!(loaded.project_id, None);
    assert_eq!(loaded.moved_from, None);
    assert!(
        loaded
            .check_binding(&loaded.partition_key, &loaded.owner_key, &loaded.root)
            .is_ok()
    );
    let written = loaded.to_json();
    assert!(!written.contains("project_id"), "{written}");
    assert!(written.contains("\"moved_from\": null"), "{written}");
}

/// R19: `project_id` is written right after `root`, and only when set; it
/// reads back as the same id; an explicit `null` reads as absent; a
/// spelling that is not the canonical one is refused, so the partition it
/// guards is quarantined rather than bound to a guess.
#[test]
fn a_project_id_is_written_after_root_only_when_set() {
    let id = ProjectId::parse("7d1c2b3a-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d").unwrap();
    let plain: ControlSnapshot = serde_json::from_str(SNAPSHOT_EXAMPLE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(plain.project_id, None);
    assert!(!plain.to_json().contains("project_id"));

    let stamped = plain.clone().with_project_id(id);
    let json = stamped.to_json();
    let keys: Vec<&str> = json
        .lines()
        .filter(|l| l.starts_with("  \""))
        .map(|l| l.trim().split('"').nth(1).unwrap())
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        keys,
        [
            "schema",
            "partition_key",
            "scope",
            "owner_key",
            "owner_id",
            "root",
            "project_id",
            "created_at",
            "updated_at",
            "moved_from",
            "repaired_at",
            "pending",
            "notes",
            "tombstones"
        ]
    );
    assert!(json.contains("\"project_id\": \"7d1c2b3a-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d\""));
    let again: ControlSnapshot = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(again.project_id, Some(id));
    assert_eq!(again, stamped);

    let with_null = SNAPSHOT_EXAMPLE.replace(
        "\"moved_from\": null,",
        "\"project_id\": null,\n  \"moved_from\": null,",
    );
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::from_str::<ControlSnapshot>(&with_null)
            .unwrap()
            .project_id,
        None
    );
    let upper = SNAPSHOT_EXAMPLE.replace(
        "\"moved_from\": null,",
        "\"project_id\": \"7D1C2B3A-4E5F-4A6B-8C7D-9E0F1A2B3C4D\",\n  \"moved_from\": null,",
    );
    assert!(serde_json::from_str::<ControlSnapshot>(&upper).is_err());
}
```

    let mut home = earlier.clone();
    home.scope = SnapshotScope::Home;
    assert!(home.check_binding(&key, &owner, &home.root, None).is_ok());
    assert!(home.check_binding(&key, &owner, "/elsewhere", None).is_err());
    assert!(
        project.check_binding(&key, &owner, &project.root, None).is_err(),
        "a snapshot carrying an id is no home snapshot"
    );

    assert!(project.check_binding("home-x", &owner, &project.root, Some(&id)).is_err());
    assert!(home.check_binding(&key, "x", &home.root, None).is_err());
}

/// R18: a project partition is keyed by its project id, carries the id in
/// its snapshot from the first write, and says which project it belongs to;
/// the home partition carries none, and its snapshot file has no
/// `project_id` key.
#[test]
fn a_project_partition_is_keyed_and_stamped_by_its_project_id() {

    let want = project_partition_key(&owner_key(ALICE), &project.id);

        partition_key_for(&sb.project_scope(), &owner_key(ALICE)).unwrap(),
        want
    );

    assert_eq!(p.partition_key(), want);
    assert_eq!(p.project_id(), Some(&project.id));

    )
    .unwrap();
    let snapshot = p.snapshot().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(snapshot.partition_key, want);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.project_id, Some(project.id));
    let on_disk = std::fs::read_to_string(p.snapshot_path()).unwrap();
    assert!(
        on_disk.contains(&format!("\"project_id\": \"{}\"", project.id)),
        "{on_disk}"
    );

    let home = sb.open_home(ALICE);
    home.create(

        Actor::UserSurface,
    )
    .unwrap();

/// R18, R22: a project snapshot that names another project, or none (an
/// earlier build's), quarantines the partition with a reason naming which;
/// `doctor --repair` rebuilds it stamped with the project's own id, and the
/// partition serves its note again.
#[test]
fn a_project_snapshot_bound_elsewhere_is_quarantined_and_repair_stamps_the_id() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let project = crate::store::projects::register(&sb.project_root()).unwrap();
    let p = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
    let created = p
        .create(
            new_note("Release", "# Release\n\nTag first.\n", NoteKind::Procedure),
            Actor::UserSurface,
        )
        .unwrap();
    let path = p.snapshot_path().to_path_buf();
    drop(p);
    for (stamp, needle) in [
        (Some(ProjectId::new()), "bound to project"),
        (None, "earlier build"),
    ] {
        let mut s = ControlSnapshot::load(&path).unwrap().unwrap();
        s.project_id = stamp;
        s.save(&path, ts(2026, 9, 24, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap();
        let reopened = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
        match reopened.health() {
            PartitionHealth::Quarantined(reason) => {
                assert!(reason.contains(needle), "{needle}: {reason}")
            }
            other => panic!("{needle}: {other:?}"),
        }
        let report = reopened.repair(&owner_key(ALICE)).unwrap();
        assert!(report.rebuilt, "{needle}");
        assert_eq!(reopened.snapshot().unwrap().project_id, Some(project.id));
        assert_eq!(reopened.health(), PartitionHealth::Ready);
        assert!(reopened.read(&created.id).is_ok(), "{needle}");
    }
}

/// R18 with S3's re-point: the project's folder under `projects/` is
/// renamed and no snapshot is touched — the partition keeps its key, its
/// snapshot file byte for byte, and its note, read at the new path. The old
/// path is no project any more.
#[test]
fn a_repointed_project_partition_keeps_its_key_snapshot_and_notes() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let project = crate::store::projects::register(&sb.project_root()).unwrap();
    let p = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
    let note = p
        .create(
            new_note("Release", "# Release\n\nTag first.\n", NoteKind::Procedure),
            Actor::UserSurface,
        )
        .unwrap();
    let key = p.partition_key().to_string();
    let snapshot_file = p.snapshot_path().to_path_buf();
    let before = std::fs::read(&snapshot_file).unwrap();
    drop(p);

    let db = crate::Database::open(&sb.outside.path().join("db.sqlite")).unwrap();
    let moved = sb.outside.path().join("moved");
    std::fs::create_dir(&moved).unwrap();
    let moved = moved.canonicalize().unwrap();
    crate::project_life::repoint(&db, &sb.project_root(), &moved).unwrap();

    let at_new = Partition::open(&StoreScope::Project(moved.clone()), ALICE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(at_new.partition_key(), key);
    assert_eq!(at_new.project_id(), Some(&project.id));
    assert_eq!(at_new.health(), PartitionHealth::Ready);
    let read = at_new.read(&note.id).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read.revision, note.revision);
    assert!(read.derived.recorded);
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(&snapshot_file).unwrap(),
        before,
        "a re-point touches no snapshot"
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(
            Partition::open(&sb.project_scope(), ALICE),
            Err(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { .. })
        ),
        "the old path is no project any more"
    );
}

/// R24 with R18: a re-point stopped after any of its first three steps is
/// finished by the next boot's recovery, and the partition comes through
/// under the same key, Ready, serving its note at the same revision.
#[test]
fn a_repoint_interrupted_after_any_step_keeps_the_partition_once_recovered() {
    use crate::project_life::{RepointStep, recover_repoints, repoint_with};
    for stop in [
        RepointStep::Marked,
        RepointStep::RowsRewritten,
        RepointStep::Renamed,
    ] {
        let sb = Sandbox::new();
        crate::store::projects::register(&sb.project_root()).unwrap();
        let p = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
        let note = p
            .create(
                new_note("Release", "# Release\n\nTag first.\n", NoteKind::Procedure),
                Actor::UserSurface,
            )
            .unwrap();
        let key = p.partition_key().to_string();
        drop(p);
        let db = crate::Database::open(&sb.outside.path().join("db.sqlite")).unwrap();
        let moved = sb.outside.path().join("moved");
        std::fs::create_dir(&moved).unwrap();
        let moved = moved.canonicalize().unwrap();

        let stopped = repoint_with(&db, &sb.project_root(), &moved, &mut |step| step != stop);
        assert!(stopped.is_err(), "{stop:?}: the hook stopped it");
        let report = recover_repoints(&db);
        assert_eq!(report.finished, [moved.clone()], "{stop:?}: {report:?}");
        assert!(report.failed.is_empty(), "{stop:?}: {report:?}");

        let at_new = Partition::open(&StoreScope::Project(moved.clone()), ALICE).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(at_new.partition_key(), key, "{stop:?}");
        assert_eq!(at_new.health(), PartitionHealth::Ready, "{stop:?}");
        assert_eq!(
            at_new.read(&note.id).unwrap().revision,
            note.revision,
            "{stop:?}"
        );
    }
}

/// R22: a project snapshot an earlier build wrote — keyed by its directory,
/// no project id — is left where it is: `adopt` neither renames it nor
/// refuses because of it, and adopts everything else.
#[test]
fn adopt_leaves_an_earlier_builds_idless_project_snapshot_in_place() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    crate::store::projects::register(&sb.project_root()).unwrap();
    let home = sb.open_home(ALICE);
    home.create(
        new_note("Home note", "# H\n", NoteKind::Preference),
        Actor::UserSurface,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let project = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
    project
        .create(
            new_note("Project note", "# P\n", NoteKind::Fact),
            Actor::UserSurface,
        )
        .unwrap();
    drop((home, project));
    let earlier_key = format!("proj-{}-0123456789abcdef", owner_key(ALICE));
    let earlier_path = snapshot_path_for(&earlier_key).unwrap();
    let earlier_root = sb
        .project_root()
        .join(".openalpaca/memory/owners")
        .join(owner_key(ALICE));
    ControlSnapshot::new(
        &earlier_key,
        SnapshotScope::Project,
        owner_key(ALICE),
        ALICE,
        earlier_root.to_string_lossy(),
        ts(2026, 9, 20, 0, 0, 0),
    )
    .save(&earlier_path, ts(2026, 9, 20, 0, 0, 0))
    .unwrap();
    let before = std::fs::read(&earlier_path).unwrap();

    let reborn = "u_example_alice_reborn";
    let adopted = adopt(&owner_key(ALICE), reborn, ts(2026, 9, 24, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(adopted.len(), 2, "{adopted:?}");
    assert!(adopted.contains(&format!("home-{}", owner_key(reborn))));
    assert!(
        adopted.iter().all(|k| !k.ends_with("-0123456789abcdef")),
        "{adopted:?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(&earlier_path).unwrap(),
        before,
        "left byte for byte"
    );
}

/// R21 (storage design): every project partition's key changed from its
/// directory's hash to its project id's, so a cache written at schema 5 —

#[test]

/// The project key of a project partition (storage design R18): the first
/// [`DIR_KEY_HEX`] characters of `sha256_hex` over the project's id in its
/// canonical form — the id in `projects/<name>/project.json`, which a
/// re-point never changes, so a partition keeps its key, its snapshot and
/// its index rows when its project moves.
pub fn project_key(project_id: &ProjectId) -> String {
    let mut key = sha256_hex(project_id.to_string().as_bytes());
    key.truncate(DIR_KEY_HEX);
    key
}

/// `home-<owner-key>`.

pub fn project_partition_key(owner_key: &str, project_id: &ProjectId) -> String {
    format!("proj-{owner_key}-{}", project_key(project_id))
}

  **(2) `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/memory_files/snapshot.rs`.** Replace the whole method `check_binding`
  (its doc comment through its closing brace) with:

```rust
    /// Whether this snapshot is the one for the partition with
    /// `partition_key` and `owner_key` (design §7a). A home snapshot is
    /// bound to its directory: `root` must be the directory it was read for,
    /// and it carries no project id. A project snapshot is bound to its
    /// project (storage design R18): `project_id` must be the id in the
    /// `project.json` beside the partition's `memory/`, and `root` is not
    /// compared — a re-point renames the folder and touches no snapshot. A
    /// project snapshot with no id is an earlier build's (R22) and binds
    /// nothing.
    pub fn check_binding(
        &self,
        partition_key: &str,
        owner_key: &str,
        root: &str,
        project_id: Option<&ProjectId>,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        match (project_id, self.project_id.as_ref()) {
            (None, None) => {
                if self.root != root {
                    return Err(format!("bound to `{}`, read for `{root}`", self.root));
                }
            }
            (None, Some(theirs)) => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "a home partition's snapshot names project {theirs}"
                ));
            }
            (Some(ours), None) => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "the snapshot carries no project id (an earlier build's), read for project {ours}"
                ));
            }
            (Some(ours), Some(theirs)) => {
                if ours != theirs {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "bound to project {theirs}, read for project {ours}"
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        if self.partition_key != partition_key {
            return Err(format!(
                "partition_key is `{}`, expected `{partition_key}`",
                self.partition_key
            ));
        }
        if self.owner_key != owner_key {
            return Err(format!(
                "owner_key is `{}`, expected `{owner_key}`",
                self.owner_key
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

  Leave S3's `fn scope_root` exactly as S3 wrote it — it decides R12 and, in S3's version, the components the open
  checks for links. Replace the whole `pub fn partition_key_for` (its doc comment through its closing brace, as
  S3 left it) with the block below, which puts the new private `project_id_of` right above it:

```rust
/// The project a scope's partition belongs to (storage design R18): `None`
/// at home; for a project, the id in the `project.json` that records its
/// root, or `NotRegistered` (R12) when no folder under `projects/` does. A
/// relative root is refused by `lookup` (it has no existing ancestor).
fn project_id_of(scope: &StoreScope) -> Result<Option<ProjectId>, MemoryFilesError> {
    match scope {
        StoreScope::Home => Ok(None),
        StoreScope::Project(root) => match crate::store::projects::lookup(root)? {
            Some(project) => Ok(Some(project.id)),
            None => Err(MemoryFilesError::NotRegistered { root: root.clone() }),
        },
    }
}

/// The partition key of `owner_key`'s partition in `scope` — what
/// [`Partition::open`] derives — without opening or creating anything. For
/// a log line that must name a partition it has not opened. A project
/// partition's key is its project id's (R18): `NotRegistered` for a root no
/// folder under `projects/` records.
pub fn partition_key_for(scope: &StoreScope, owner_key: &str) -> Result<String, MemoryFilesError> {
    Ok(match project_id_of(scope)? {
        None => home_partition_key(owner_key),
        Some(id) => project_partition_key(owner_key, &id),
    })
}

feat(storage): a project partition is keyed and bound by its project id (R18, R21)

A project partition's key is proj-<owner-key>-<16 hex of sha256(project
id)>, and its control snapshot binds by the id in the project.json beside
its memory/ — the recorded root is no longer compared. The first write and
`repair` stamp the id (one `fresh_snapshot` helper, which `derive_view`'s
in-memory placeholder shares); `adopt` carries it. A project snapshot with
no id (an earlier build's) binds nothing and `adopt` leaves it in place
(R22). `dir_key` is gone. Because a re-point renames the folder and never
writes a snapshot, a project's partition keeps its key, snapshot and notes
through S3's re-point and its boot recovery. The memory index goes to
schema 6: every old project row sits under a key nothing reads, so an old
cache is rebuilt from the notes.

Verified: cargo test -p openalpaca_storage memory_files / memory_index; -p openalpaca_core memory::service; -p openalpacad routes::workspaces; -p openalpaca commands::memory; cargo check -p openalpaca_core --features live-eval --tests

// ============================================================================
// A re-point and the memory partition (storage design R18; fixture 17)

/// R18 after S3's re-point: a whole rebuild finds a project partition by
/// the id in its control snapshot, not by the folder its recorded `root`
/// names — after a re-point that folder is gone — so the partition is
/// re-indexed under the same key, at its new folder, before any read
/// touches it.
#[test]
fn a_rebuild_finds_a_repointed_project_partition_by_its_id() {
    let h = Harness::new();
    let old = h.workspace("old", Some(".git"));
    openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register(&old).unwrap();
    let note = h.store(
        &h.user(ALICE, Some(&old)),
        "Release step",
        "# Release step\n\nTag, then run the release script.\n",
        NoteKind::Procedure,
    );
    let key = h
        .snapshot(&StoreScope::Project(old.clone()), ALICE)
        .unwrap()
        .partition_key;
    let new = h.root.path().join("ws").join("new");
    fs::create_dir_all(&new).unwrap();
    let new = new.canonicalize().unwrap();
    openalpaca_storage::project_life::repoint(&h.db, &old, &new).unwrap();

    h.service.rebuild_index().unwrap();

    assert!(
        h.service
            .index()
            .get(&key, &note.id.to_string())
            .unwrap()
            .is_some(),
        "the rebuild re-indexed the partition under its key"
    );
    let found = search(&h, &h.user(ALICE, Some(&new)), "release script");
    assert_eq!(search_ids(&found), [note.id]);
    assert_eq!(found.results[0].revision, note.revision);
}
