/// R20: `adopt` finds a project partition's folder by the project id in its
/// snapshot. After a re-point the snapshot's recorded `root` names a folder
/// that is gone; the partition is adopted where its project now is, under
/// the key its id gives, and serves its note with its record.
#[test]
fn adopt_after_a_repoint_finds_the_partition_by_its_project_id() {
    let sb = Sandbox::new();
    let project = crate::store::projects::register(&sb.project_root()).unwrap();
    let p = sb.open_project(ALICE).unwrap();
    let pn = p
        .create(
            new_note("Project note", "# P\n", NoteKind::Fact),
            Actor::UserSurface,
        )
        .unwrap();
    drop(p);
    let db = crate::Database::open(&sb.outside.path().join("db.sqlite")).unwrap();
    let moved = sb.outside.path().join("moved");
    std::fs::create_dir(&moved).unwrap();
    let moved = moved.canonicalize().unwrap();
    crate::project_life::repoint(&db, &sb.project_root(), &moved).unwrap();

    let reborn = "u_example_alice_reborn";
    let adopted = adopt(&owner_key(ALICE), reborn, ts(2026, 9, 24, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap();
    let want = project_partition_key(&owner_key(reborn), &project.id);
    assert_eq!(adopted, [want.clone()]);
    let moved_scope = StoreScope::Project(moved.clone());
    assert_eq!(
        list_owner_keys(&moved_scope).unwrap(),
        [owner_key(reborn)]
    );
    let p = Partition::open(&moved_scope, reborn).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.partition_key(), want);
    assert_eq!(p.health(), PartitionHealth::Ready);
    assert!(p.read(&pn.id).unwrap().derived.recorded);
    assert_eq!(p.snapshot().unwrap().project_id, Some(project.id));
}

fix(storage): adopt finds a project partition's folder by its project id (R20)

`adopt` took a project partition's owners directory from the root its
snapshot recorded; after a re-point that folder is gone, and adopt renamed
nothing while writing a snapshot for the new owner. It now finds the
folder by the project id the snapshot carries, through `projects::by_id`,
and builds the new key from that id. A snapshot whose id no folder records
is left alone with a WARN; one with no id was already left alone (R22).

                        body: "# Release step\n\nTag first.\n".into(),
                        kind: Some(NoteKind::Procedure),
                        ..Default::default()
                    },
                )
                .unwrap();
            tx.send(()).unwrap();
        });
        assert!(
            rx.recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(150))
                .is_err(),
            "a write at the new path waits while the hold stands"
        );
        drop(held);
        rx.recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .expect("the write lands once the hold is released");
    });

    let other = h.workspace("other", Some(".git"));
    assert_ne!(
        MemoryService::slot_key(&StoreScope::Project(other), ALICE_KEY),
        slot,
        "another root never shares this project's slot"
    );
}
```

```rust
    fn slot_key(scope: &StoreScope, owner_key: &str) -> String {
        match scope {
            StoreScope::Home => format!("home:{owner_key}"),
            StoreScope::Project(root) => {
                match openalpaca_storage::store::projects::lookup(root) {
                    Ok(Some(project)) => Self::project_slot_key(&project.id),
                    // Not a registered project (R12): its writes are refused
                    // where the partition opens; this slot only keeps two of
                    // them apart, and never meets a project's.
                    Ok(None) | Err(_) => format!("unregistered:{}", canonical_lenient(root)),
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The write slot of a project (storage design R18): one per project,
    /// shared by every owner's partition of it, whatever path names it.
    fn project_slot_key(project_id: &openalpaca_storage::store::projects::ProjectId) -> String {
        format!("proj:{project_id}")
    }

    /// The hold a re-point and a delete take on a project's memory (storage
    /// design §6): refused while a memory write of the project is in
    /// flight, otherwise every new write of it waits until the guard drops.
    /// Named by the project's id (R18), so it holds under the old path and
    /// the new. It refuses rather than waits; the route retries (S5a).
    pub fn quiesce(
        &self,
        project_id: &openalpaca_storage::store::projects::ProjectId,
    ) -> Result<QuiesceGuard, MemoryError> {
        let key = Self::project_slot_key(project_id);
        self.slots
            .quiesce(&key)
            .map_err(|()| MemoryError::WritePending { key })
    }
```

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(memory): quiesce and every project write slot are keyed by the project id

`MemoryService::quiesce` takes the project's id, and every write slot of
a project partition — writes, the index rebuild, the 30 s reconciliation —
is `proj:<project id>`, looked up from the root its scope names. One hold
therefore covers a project under its old path and its new one, and a
write at the new path waits for a re-point or a delete in progress. An
unregistered root's slot (its write is refused at open anyway) never
meets a project's. The interim PATCH looks the id up before it quiesces.

Verified: cargo test -p openalpaca_core memory::service; cargo test -p openalpacad routes::workspaces

/// Whether a chunk's project is gone (owner decision ST-21, superseding
/// LQ5): its root is no longer a registered project — its data was deleted.
/// A missing project, whose folder is gone but whose record under
/// `projects/` stands, is not gone: its turns are learned into its notes,
/// which live in the home store and re-create nothing in the user's
/// folder. A lookup that fails is not "gone" either: the chunk goes on,
/// and the write's own error holds the cursor. The check before the model
/// call (`queue.rs`, task extraction) and the one right before the first
/// write ask the same question.
pub(crate) fn root_gone(root: Option<&Path>) -> bool {
    root.is_some_and(|r| matches!(projects::lookup(r), Ok(None)))
}
```

  (a) In `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/memory_files/fixtures.rs`, after `every_file_level_fixture_is_satisfied`:

```rust
/// Fixture 17 is a specification no loader runs — its ops are the
/// service's, the route's and the CLI's, and `memory_files::tests`,
/// `memory::service::tests` and `routes::workspaces::tests` pin it — so
/// this keeps it honest: every op it uses and every expectation it checks
/// is one the README defines.
#[test]
fn fixture_17_uses_only_the_ops_and_expectations_the_readme_defines() {
    let path = fixtures_dir().join("17-move-purge-factory-reset-config-reset.json");
    let fixture: Value = serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let readme = std::fs::read_to_string(fixtures_dir().join("README.md")).unwrap();
    let defined: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = readme
        .lines()
        .filter(|l| l.starts_with("| `"))
        .filter_map(|l| l.split('|').nth(1))
        .flat_map(|cell| {
            cell.split('`')
                .skip(1)
                .step_by(2)
                .map(str::to_string)
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        })
        .collect();
    for step in arr(&fixture["operations"]) {
        let op = s(&step["op"]);
        assert!(
            defined.contains(op),
            "step {}: op `{op}` is not in the README",
            step["step"]
        );
        for (key, _) in step["expect"].as_object().into_iter().flatten() {
            assert!(
                defined.contains(key.as_str()),
                "step {}: expectation `{key}` is not in the README",
                step["step"]
            );
        }
    }
}
```

### Spec conflicts

1. **The brief puts §6's re-point core in S4; interfaces.md C1 puts it in S3.** The brief asks S4 for the
   re-point's refusals, its four steps, R24's boot recovery, the crash hook, and the removal of
   `store/project_move.rs`, `begin_project_move` / `finish_project_move`, the service's move functions and
   `known_project_roots`, `MoveStep` and `rebase_workspace_with`. interfaces.md §0, §5.1, §7.1 and C1 give all of
   it to S3, because the flip (S3) breaks today's PATCH, whose store and memory moves join `.openalpaca` onto the
   project (`store/project_move.rs:35-37`, `partition.rs:2749`). Followed interfaces.md: S4 consumes
   `project_life::{repoint, repoint_with, recover_repoints, RepointStep}` and adds the tests that a project's
   memory survives a re-point and a recovered crash (S4.2, S4.3, S4.6).
2. **`memory/.gitignore` and fixtures 03 and 04.** The brief lists them under S4; interfaces.md C6 and §7.3 give
   them to S3 (fixture 03 asserts the file, and the flip rewrites both). Followed interfaces.md.
3. **The quiesce retry.** The brief says `quiesce` "tries for a few seconds before `WORKSPACE_BUSY`"; interfaces.md
   §6.1 and §8 put the retry (100 ms for 3 s) in S5a's route helper `quiesce_project`, and spec §5 itself says
   `quiesce` "refuses rather than waits … so the two routes try". S4 changes only the key; `quiesce` still
   refuses at once.
4. **Accepted (R-S14).** **ST-21's task-extraction site.** Spec §5 and interfaces.md §4.5 cite `task_extraction/mod.rs:398-404` and say
   "before its model call". At HEAD those lines are the store loop *after* the call. Placed the check where the
   words put it: right after the context is built (HEAD :134-155), before the cost-cap read and the call.
5. **Accepted (R-S14).** **Fixture 17's steps.** interfaces.md §7.3 gives S4 "steps 1–11 and 13–16" and S5a "step 12", which implies
   16 steps. Today's fixture has 25, and its collision, adopt and config-reset steps stay, so the rewrite has 24.
   Step 12 stays the purge step, now of a project (`project_d`) no later step names, so S5a's delete changes no
   other step.
6. **Accepted (R-S14).** **"Three places build a fresh snapshot" (R18).** There is a fourth `ControlSnapshot::new`, in `derive_view`
   (HEAD `partition.rs:1386`), an in-memory placeholder; S4.2 routes it through the same `fresh_snapshot` helper.
   And `adopt`'s `ControlSnapshot::new` arm (HEAD :2974) runs only for a home candidate with no snapshot: a
   project candidate always carries its old snapshot, whose id `adopt` keeps (and restates with
   `snapshot.project_id = c.project_id`). "adopt stamps the id" holds by carrying it, not by building a snapshot.
7. **The `nth(4)` sites.** Spec §5 lists five lines; `partition.rs:2788` is the helper's call, not a site
   (`panel/fact-check-rev03.json` B6), and S3 deletes three of the four. S4 converts the two left (the rebuild,
   the doctor) and `adopt`'s parent read.

   themselves, which is idempotent. S4 calls S3's `scope_root` only where S3 already does and never rewrites it.
2. `known_project_roots`: interfaces.md §7.1 removes it in S3, naming the PATCH and the purge as its last callers;

## Stage 1, slice S5a — a project's life: delete its data, the routes and the CLI (draft)

Drafted at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`) from `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8: §6 *Delete its data*, §9, §16
step 5) and `interfaces.md` (§5.2, §6.1, §6.2, §7.1). Every `file:line` is HEAD's; code is located by content.

### What this slice does

S5a builds the daemon and CLI half of §16 step 5 on top of S1–S4. In storage it adds ST-19's delete core to
`project_life`: a read-only plan (`delete_plan`) and a delete (`delete_project_data`) that share one predicate for
which rows die — every row naming the project in the five path columns, and the rows hanging off its sessions and
runs, `learning_cursor` included — and which files are kept (those a message the transaction leaves still links).
A kept file is copied into the root store under `kept/<project folder>-<project id>/`, re-addressed with no project
(a kept by-product as its newest version only), and the copy is taken back if the transaction fails. The project's
folder under `projects/` goes as one directory (`remove_project_folder`), never by iterating `storage_path`. In core,
`MemoryService::remove_project` drops every owner's partition of the project from the index and removes its control
snapshots. In the daemon, `/v1/workspaces` becomes §9's wire: `GET` lists projects, `GET ?path=` answers
`{path, root, id, name, missing, rows, active_tasks, queued_tasks}`, `POST` chooses a folder, `PATCH` answers the
re-pointed project, and `POST …/purge` is the delete — of a project named by its root exactly (a path inside one is
refused, naming the root: the lead's R-S8), refused while a run is in flight, a plan unless `dry_run: false`, and
under `quiesce` for the rest; the old purge (its `all` form, its upload-unlink loop, the
`.layout` reading, the marker-walk refusals) goes with its last callers. The CLI gets `store list`,
`store rebase` and `store purge <project>` on the new shapes and `chat --project <dir>`; fixture 17's purge step
becomes the delete. The factory-reset preview is not this slice's: `interfaces.md` §0 gives it to S6 (SC-2).

### Rules every task below carries

- One cargo process at a time. Every test command is `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`, never the workspace.
- A test that touches a store holds its crate's guard: `crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard` (storage),
  `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard` (core and daemon), `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox` (CLI). Every project is a
  git repository made under the test's own tempdir and registered through `store::projects::register` (or a
  folder under that tempdir which a `POST /v1/workspaces` test chooses); no test
  names `~/.openalpaca` or a real repository, and none reaches `localhost:11434` (the CLI tests use
  `test_util::serve` on a random loopback port).
- No `&s[..n]` string cut appears in this slice's code. No `std::env::set_var` is added (the guards own it).
- Edits are anchored: each "replace" names the item to replace by its signature or a unique line. No `sed -i`.
- A task that changes a route request struct, a CLI subcommand or flag, or a `lib.rs` re-export runs
  `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py` and commits `docs/api/` in the same commit; every task ends with
  `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check` printing `API documentation is up to date.`
- This slice adds no `.md` file and changes no memory-index row (`memory_index::SCHEMA_VERSION` stays where S4 put it).
- Commit messages use a conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line, and end with
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Names from S1–S4 are used exactly as `interfaces.md` declares them; each task's **Consumes** lists them and
  cites the sheet's section for every name S1–S4 add (they are not at HEAD). Everything else a task names was
  checked against HEAD `32292608`.

Order: S5a.1 → S5a.2 → S5a.3 (storage) → S5a.4 (core) → S5a.5 → S5a.6 → S5a.7 → S5a.8 → S5a.9 → S5a.10 (daemon)
→ S5a.11 → S5a.12 (CLI).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test.**

  ```rust
  //! ST-19's delete core: the plan, the rows, the folder (design §6, *Delete
  //! its data*). DB and files only — the live-run guard, the memory slot and
  //! the partitions are the route's (`apps/openalpacad/src/routes/workspaces.rs`).

  In `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life.rs`, after S3's last item, add:

  Create `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life/delete/tests.rs`:

  ```rust
  //! The delete core against a scenario with a bystander on every leg: a second
  //! project, a home conversation, a surviving conversation that also holds a
  //! message naming the doomed project, and files linked from inside and from
  //! outside. The home store is a tempdir behind the crate's one guard; both
  //! projects are git repositories made for the test.

  use super::*;
  use crate::memory_files::{
      ControlSnapshot, NOTES_DIR, OWNERS_DIR, SnapshotScope, home_partition_key, owner_key,
      project_partition_key, snapshot_path_for,
  };
  use crate::repository::{ARTIFACT_ROLE, ATTACHMENT_ROLE};
  use crate::store::StoreScope;
  use crate::store::projects::{self, Project};
  use crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard;
  use crate::{
      ArtifactKind, ArtifactStore, Database, FileAssetRepository, NewArtifact, NewUpload,
      PurgeCounts, PurgeSession, UploadStore,
  };
  use chrono::{DateTime, TimeZone, Utc};
  use std::path::PathBuf;
  use tempfile::{TempDir, tempdir};

  const OWNER: &str = "owner-1";

  /// One date for every write, so a second put of a title is its next version.
  fn at() -> DateTime<Utc> {
      Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 10, 1, 9, 0, 0).unwrap()
  }

  pub(super) struct World {
      tmp: TempDir,
      _env: HomeStoreGuard,
      pub(super) home: PathBuf,
      pub(super) db: Database,
  }

  impl World {
      pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
          let tmp = tempdir().unwrap();
          let home = tmp.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join("home");
          std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();
          let env = HomeStoreGuard::set(&home);
          let db = Database::open(&tmp.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
          Self { tmp, _env: env, home, db }
      }

      /// A git repository under the test's tempdir, registered as a project.
      pub(super) fn project(&self, name: &str) -> Project {
          let root = self.tmp.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join("repos").join(name);
          std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join(".git")).unwrap();
          projects::register(&root).unwrap()
      }

      pub(super) fn exec(&self, sql: &str, params: &[&dyn rusqlite::ToSql]) {
          self.db
              .with_connection(|conn| {
                  conn.execute(sql, params)?;
                  Ok(())
              })
              .unwrap();
      }

      pub(super) fn count(&self, sql: &str) -> i64 {
          self.db
              .with_connection(|conn| Ok(conn.query_row(sql, [], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))?))
              .unwrap()
      }

      /// A user row in `session`, naming `root` in `workspace_root` (or none).
      pub(super) fn message(&self, session: &str, root: Option<&str>) -> i64 {
          self.db
              .with_connection(|conn| {
                  conn.execute(
                      "INSERT INTO conversation_messages
                           (lane_key, role, content, session_id, workspace_root)
                       VALUES (?1, 'user', 'hi', ?1, ?2)",
                      rusqlite::params![session, root],
                  )?;
                  Ok(conn.last_insert_rowid())
              })
              .unwrap()
      }

      /// An upload in `project`'s store whose bytes are its own name.
      pub(super) fn upload(&self, project: &Project, name: &str) -> String {
          let scope = StoreScope::Project(project.root.clone());
          UploadStore::new(&self.db)
              .put(NewUpload {
                  owner_id: OWNER,
                  filename: name,
                  mime_type: "text/plain",
                  data: name.as_bytes(),
                  scope: &scope,
                  created: at(),
              })
              .unwrap()
              .asset
              .id
      }

      /// A by-product in `project`'s store; the same title again is its next version.
      pub(super) fn by_product(&self, project: &Project, title: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
          let scope = StoreScope::Project(project.root.clone());
          let mut new = NewArtifact::new(OWNER, &scope, ArtifactKind::Markdown, title, bytes);
          new.created = at();
          ArtifactStore::new(&self.db).put(new).unwrap().0.id
      }

      pub(super) fn link(&self, message: i64, file: &str, role: &str) {
          FileAssetRepository::new(&self.db)
              .link_to_message_with_role(message, file, 0, None, role)
              .unwrap();
      }

      /// A control snapshot written by hand: `project` names a project
      /// partition stamped with its id, `None` the home partition.
      pub(super) fn snapshot(&self, owner: &str, project: Option<&Project>) {
          let okey = owner_key(owner);
          let now = Utc::now();
          let (key, scope, dir, id) = match project {
              Some(p) => (
                  project_partition_key(&okey, &p.id),
                  SnapshotScope::Project,
                  p.dir.join("memory").join(OWNERS_DIR).join(&okey),
                  Some(p.id),
              ),
              None => (
                  home_partition_key(&okey),
                  SnapshotScope::Home,
                  self.home.join("memory").join(OWNERS_DIR).join(&okey),
                  None,
              ),
          };
          let mut snapshot =
              ControlSnapshot::new(&key, scope, &okey, owner, dir.to_string_lossy(), now);
          if let Some(id) = id {
              snapshot = snapshot.with_project_id(id);
          }
          snapshot.save(&snapshot_path_for(&key).unwrap(), now).unwrap();
      }

      /// A file under a project partition's `notes/` — counted by name only.
      pub(super) fn note_file(&self, project: &Project, owner: &str, name: &str) {
          let dir = project
              .dir
              .join("memory")
              .join(OWNERS_DIR)
              .join(owner_key(owner))
              .join(NOTES_DIR);
          std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
          std::fs::write(dir.join(name), b"---\nschema: 1\n---\n").unwrap();
      }
  }

  /// What [`seed`] made, by name.
  pub(super) struct Seed {
      pub(super) p: Project,
      pub(super) q: Project,
      pub(super) m_p: i64,
      pub(super) m_q_leg: i64,
      pub(super) m_q: i64,
      pub(super) m_h: i64,
      pub(super) u_alone: String,
      pub(super) u_shared: String,
      pub(super) u_leg: String,
      pub(super) u_q: String,
      pub(super) a_alone: String,
      pub(super) a_shared: String,
  }

  /// `p` is deleted; `q` and the home scope are bystanders.
  ///
  /// | Row | Names `p` by | Fate |
  /// |---|---|---|
  /// | session `s-p` | `workspace_id` | goes |
  /// | message `m_p` | its session | goes |
  /// | message `m_q_leg` (session `s-q`) | `workspace_root` | goes; `s-q` stays |
  /// | `t-p`, its span, event, decision, LLM call | `workspace_id` / the run | go |
  /// | follow-ups `f-sp` (session `s-p`), `f-path` (session `s-q`, `workspace_path = p`) | session / path | go |
  /// | `learning_cursor` of `s-p` | its session | goes |
  /// | `u_alone` (linked by `m_p`), `u_leg` (linked by `m_q_leg`), `a_alone` (unlinked) | `project_root` | go |
  /// | `u_shared` (linked by `m_p` and the home message `m_h`) | `project_root` | kept |
  /// | `a_shared`, two versions (linked as an artifact by `m_q`) | `project_root` | kept, newest version |
  pub(super) fn seed(w: &World) -> Seed {
      let p = w.project("doomed");
      let q = w.project("bystander");
      let (pr, qr) = (p.root_string(), q.root_string());
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO session (id, lane_key, source, workspace_id) VALUES ('s-p', 's-p', 'gui', ?1)",
          &[&pr],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO session (id, lane_key, source, workspace_id, message_count)
           VALUES ('s-q', 's-q', 'gui', ?1, 2)",
          &[&qr],
      );
      w.exec("INSERT INTO session (id, lane_key, source) VALUES ('s-h', 's-h', 'gui')", &[]);
      let m_p = w.message("s-p", Some(pr.as_str()));
      let m_q_leg = w.message("s-q", Some(pr.as_str()));
      let m_q = w.message("s-q", Some(qr.as_str()));
      let m_h = w.message("s-h", None);
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO message_feedback (message_id, feedback) VALUES (?1, 'positive')",
          &[&m_p],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO task (id, title, created_by, source_lane, workspace_id, session_id, status)
           VALUES ('t-p', 't', 'test', 'test', ?1, 's-p', 'completed')",
          &[&pr],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO task (id, title, created_by, source_lane, workspace_id, session_id, status)
           VALUES ('t-q', 't', 'test', 'test', ?1, 's-q', 'completed')",
          &[&qr],
      );
      // A home turn that started p's run: the run goes, the turn stays readable.
      w.exec("UPDATE conversation_messages SET task_id = 't-p' WHERE id = ?1", &[&m_h]);
      for (session, task) in [(Some("s-p"), None), (None, Some("t-p")), (Some("s-q"), None)] {
          w.exec(
              "INSERT INTO tool_execution_log (agent_id, tool_name, success, duration_ms, session_id, task_id)
               VALUES ('a', 'read', 1, 3, ?1, ?2)",
              &[&session, &task],
          );
      }
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO lane_followups (lane_key, kind, content, principal_json, session_id)
           VALUES ('s-p', 'followup', 'later', '{}', 's-p')",
          &[],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO lane_followups (lane_key, kind, content, principal_json, session_id, workspace_path)
           VALUES ('s-q', 'followup', 'later', '{}', 's-q', ?1)",
          &[&pr],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO lane_followups (lane_key, kind, content, principal_json, session_id, workspace_path)
           VALUES ('s-q', 'followup', 'later', '{}', 's-q', ?1)",
          &[&qr],
      );
      w.exec("INSERT INTO learning_cursor (session_id) VALUES ('s-p'), ('s-q')", &[]);
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO subagent_span (id, task_id, template_id, agent_instance_id, label, started_at)
           VALUES ('span-1', 't-p', 't', 'i', 'review', '2026-10-01T09:00:00Z')",
          &[],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO event_log (event_type, task_id) VALUES ('started', 't-p'), ('started', 't-q')",
          &[],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO dispatch_decisions (request_id, task_id, mode, reason)
           VALUES ('r-1', 't-p', 'lead', 'because')",
          &[],
      );
      w.exec(
          "INSERT INTO llm_call_log (task_id, provider, model) VALUES ('t-p', 'anthropic', 'sonnet')",
          &[],
      );

      let u_alone = w.upload(&p, "alone.txt");
      let u_shared = w.upload(&p, "shared.txt");
      let u_leg = w.upload(&p, "leg.txt");
      let u_q = w.upload(&q, "theirs.txt");
      let a_alone = w.by_product(&p, "Alone", b"alone\n");
      let a_shared = w.by_product(&p, "Shared", b"v1\n");
      assert_eq!(w.by_product(&p, "Shared", b"v2\n"), a_shared, "the second put is version 2");
      w.link(m_p, &u_alone, ATTACHMENT_ROLE);
      w.link(m_p, &u_shared, ATTACHMENT_ROLE);
      w.link(m_h, &u_shared, ATTACHMENT_ROLE);
      w.link(m_q_leg, &u_leg, ATTACHMENT_ROLE);
      w.link(m_q, &a_shared, ARTIFACT_ROLE);
      w.link(m_q, &u_q, ATTACHMENT_ROLE);

      Seed { p, q, m_p, m_q_leg, m_q, m_h, u_alone, u_shared, u_leg, u_q, a_alone, a_shared }
  }

  Replace the whole of `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life/delete.rs` with:

  ```rust
  //! ST-19's delete core: the plan, the rows, the folder (design §6, *Delete
  //! its data*). DB and files only — the live-run guard, the memory slot and
  //! the partitions are the route's (`apps/openalpacad/src/routes/workspaces.rs`).
  //!
  //! One rule decides every statement: a row belongs to the project when one of
  //! the five path columns names its root, or it hangs off a session or a run
  //! that does. A message dies with its session **or** with its own
  //! `workspace_root`, and a file is kept exactly when a message the delete
  //! leaves still links it — so the plan, the kept set and the transaction
  //! read one predicate ([`DOOMED_MESSAGE`], [`kept_ids`]), and a dry run and
  //! the real call cannot disagree.

  use std::fs;
  use std::path::Path;

  use anyhow::Result;

  use crate::Database;
  use crate::artifacts::{PurgeCounts, PurgeSession};
  use crate::memory_files::{NOTES_DIR, OWNERS_DIR, SnapshotScope, list_snapshots};
  use crate::store::ContentKind;
  use crate::store::projects::{Project, ProjectId};

  /// The project's conversations.
  const DOOMED_SESSIONS: &str = "SELECT id FROM session WHERE workspace_id = ?1";
  /// The project's runs.
  const DOOMED_TASKS: &str = "SELECT id FROM task WHERE workspace_id = ?1";
  /// A message the delete takes: one of the project's conversations, or one
  /// naming the project itself — a turn in another conversation that ran in it.
  const DOOMED_MESSAGE: &str =
      "workspace_root = ?1 OR session_id IN (SELECT id FROM session WHERE workspace_id = ?1)";

  /// Every file a message the delete leaves still links, by attachment or as
  /// a run's artifact.
  fn kept_ids() -> String {
      format!(
          "SELECT a.file_id FROM conversation_message_attachments a
            WHERE a.message_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM conversation_messages WHERE {DOOMED_MESSAGE})"
      )
  }

  /// Files of the project another conversation still links (step 1).
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct KeptFiles {
      pub uploads: usize,
      pub artifacts: usize,
  }

  /// What deleting a project's data would do, read without changing anything.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  pub struct DeletePlan {
      pub project: Project,
      /// What goes. Uploads and by-products here are the ones **not** kept.
      pub counts: PurgeCounts,
      pub kept: KeptFiles,
      /// The project's conversations, for the route's live-run guard.
      pub sessions: Vec<PurgeSession>,
      /// Control snapshots carrying this project's id: one per owner.
      pub memory_partitions: usize,
      /// Note files under `<dir>/memory/owners/*/notes/`.
      pub memory_notes: usize,
  }

  /// The plan of [`delete_project_data`] for `project` — reads only, and never
  /// iterates `storage_path`.
  pub fn delete_plan(db: &Database, project: &Project) -> Result<DeletePlan> {
      let root = project.root_string();
      let (counts, kept, sessions) = db.with_connection(|conn| {
          let count = |sql: &str| -> Result<usize> {
              Ok(conn.query_row(sql, rusqlite::params![root], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as usize)
          };
          let sessions = {
              let mut stmt = conn.prepare(
                  "SELECT id, lane_key FROM session WHERE workspace_id = ?1 ORDER BY id",
              )?;
              let rows = stmt
                  .query_map(rusqlite::params![root], |row| {
                      Ok(PurgeSession {
                          id: row.get(0)?,
                          lane_key: row.get(1)?,
                      })
                  })?
                  .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<PurgeSession>>>()?;
              rows
          };
          let linked = kept_ids();
          let kept = KeptFiles {
              uploads: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file_assets
                    WHERE project_root = ?1 AND origin = 'upload' AND id IN ({linked})"
              ))?,
              artifacts: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file_assets
                    WHERE project_root = ?1 AND origin <> 'upload' AND id IN ({linked})"
              ))?,
          };
          let counts = PurgeCounts {
              sessions: sessions.len(),
              messages: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversation_messages WHERE {DOOMED_MESSAGE}"
              ))?,
              tool_calls: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tool_execution_log
                    WHERE session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS}) OR task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"
              ))?,
              followups: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lane_followups
                    WHERE workspace_path = ?1 OR session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS})"
              ))?,
              tasks: count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task WHERE workspace_id = ?1")?,
              spans: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subagent_span WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"
              ))?,
              run_events: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event_log WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"
              ))?,
              uploads: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file_assets
                    WHERE project_root = ?1 AND origin = 'upload' AND id NOT IN ({linked})"
              ))?,
              artifacts: count(&format!(
                  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file_assets
                    WHERE project_root = ?1 AND origin <> 'upload' AND id NOT IN ({linked})"
              ))?,
          };
          Ok((counts, kept, sessions))
      })?;
      Ok(DeletePlan {
          project: project.clone(),
          counts,
          kept,
          sessions,
          memory_partitions: project_partitions(&project.id)?,
          memory_notes: note_files(&project.dir),
      })
  }

  /// Control snapshots of `id`'s partitions, every owner (R18, R19).
  fn project_partitions(id: &ProjectId) -> Result<usize> {
      Ok(list_snapshots()?
          .into_iter()
          .filter_map(|(_, parsed)| parsed.ok())
          .filter(|s| s.scope == SnapshotScope::Project && s.project_id.as_ref() == Some(id))
          .count())
  }

  /// Note files under `dir/memory/owners/*/notes/`: regular `*.md` files, not
  /// dot-prefixed, reached through no link (`DirEntry::file_type` does not
  /// follow one).
  fn note_files(dir: &Path) -> usize {
      let owners = dir.join(ContentKind::Memory.dir_name()).join(OWNERS_DIR);
      let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(&owners) else {
          return 0;
      };
      entries
          .flatten()
          .filter(|owner| owner.file_type().is_ok_and(|t| t.is_dir()))
          .filter_map(|owner| fs::read_dir(owner.path().join(NOTES_DIR)).ok())
          .flat_map(|notes| notes.flatten())
          .filter(|note| {
              let name = note.file_name();
              let name = name.to_string_lossy();
              !name.starts_with('.')
                  && name.ends_with(".md")
                  && note.file_type().is_ok_and(|t| t.is_file())
          })
          .count()
  }

  #[cfg(test)]
  mod tests;
  ```

### Task S5a.2: Delete the rows in one transaction, keeping linked files in the root store

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life/delete.rs` — new items `KEPT_DIR`, `DeleteOutcome`, `delete_project_data`, private `KeptRow`, `Placed`, `kept_rows`, `place_one`, `copy_fresh`, `unplace`, `strings`, `delete_within`; the `use` block grows.
- Modify: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life.rs` — the `pub use delete::{…}` line.
- Test: `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/project_life/delete/tests.rs`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: S5a.1's `delete_plan`, `KeptFiles`, `DOOMED_*`, `kept_ids`; `store::{content_dir, confine_to_root, ContentKind, StoreScope}`; `crate::content_io::{fsync_dir(&Path), remove_best_effort(&Path)}` (both `pub(crate)` at HEAD); `ArtifactStore::{versions, resolve_content}`.
- Produces:
  ```rust
  /// `<kind>/kept/<project folder>-<project id>/<old rel_path>` in the root store.
  pub const KEPT_DIR: &str = "kept";
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  pub struct DeleteOutcome { pub counts: PurgeCounts, pub kept: KeptFiles, pub session_ids: Vec<String>, pub message_ids: Vec<i64> }
  pub fn delete_project_data(db: &Database, project: &Project) -> anyhow::Result<DeleteOutcome>;
  ```
  Choice: a kept file is **copied**, then the transaction re-addresses it; the source goes with `projects/<name>/` in step 3. Why: if the transaction fails the project is untouched and the copies are removed, so "one transaction" stays true. The address `kept/<name>-<id>/` is one no grammar produces (uploads are `<date>/…`, artifacts `<date>-<title>-<task8>/…` or `loose/<date>/…`); the id makes it fresh for every project ever deleted, the old `rel_path` was unique within the project (`idx_file_assets_addr`), and the folder name tells a person browsing `~/.openalpaca/uploads/` where it came from (≤ 209 + 1 + 36 = 246 bytes, under a 255-byte component).

  /// Every regular file under `dir`, recursively.
  fn files_under(dir: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
      let mut out = Vec::new();
      let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
          return out;
      };
      for entry in entries.flatten() {
          let path = entry.path();
          if entry.file_type().unwrap().is_dir() {
              out.extend(files_under(&path));
          } else {
              out.push(path);
          }
      }
      out
  }

      assert_eq!(versions[0].version, 2);
      let rel: String = w
          .db

      assert!(store.resolve_content(&s.a_shared, Some(1)).is_err(), "version 1 is gone");

  use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
  use rusqlite::Connection;

  use crate::Database;
  use crate::artifacts::{PurgeCounts, PurgeSession};
  use crate::content_io::{fsync_dir, remove_best_effort};
  use crate::memory_files::{NOTES_DIR, OWNERS_DIR, SnapshotScope, list_snapshots};

  Add after `KeptFiles`:

  ```rust
  /// Where a kept file lands in the root store:
  /// `<uploads|artifacts>/kept/<project folder>-<project id>/<its old rel_path>`.
  /// No grammar path starts with it, the id makes it fresh for every project
  /// ever deleted, and the old `rel_path` was unique within the project.
  pub const KEPT_DIR: &str = "kept";

  /// What [`delete_project_data`] did — read inside its transaction.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  pub struct DeleteOutcome {
      pub counts: PurgeCounts,
      pub kept: KeptFiles,
      /// The sessions whose `sessions/<id>/` directory is now rowless.
      pub session_ids: Vec<String>,
      /// Every message the transaction deleted, in id order — the route forgets
      /// those conversations' summaries by them (design 09 §13.3).
      pub message_ids: Vec<i64>,
  }

  /// A file step 1 keeps, as its row names it.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  struct KeptRow {
      id: String,
      upload: bool,
      rel_path: Option<String>,
  }

  /// Where step 1 put it.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  struct Placed {
      id: String,
      upload: bool,
      rel_path: String,
      storage_path: String,
      /// The copy this call wrote; `None` when the project held no bytes for it.
      written: Option<PathBuf>,
  }

  fn kept_rows(conn: &Connection, root: &str) -> Result<Vec<KeptRow>> {
      let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&format!(
          "SELECT id, origin, rel_path FROM file_assets
            WHERE project_root = ?1 AND id IN ({}) ORDER BY id",
          kept_ids()
      ))?;
      let rows = stmt
          .query_map(rusqlite::params![root], |row| {
              let origin: String = row.get(1)?;
              Ok(KeptRow {
                  id: row.get(0)?,
                  upload: origin == "upload",
                  rel_path: row.get(2)?,
              })
          })?
          .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<KeptRow>>>()?;
      Ok(rows)
  }

  /// Copies one kept file into the root store. The source is read from
  /// `projects/<name>/<kind>/<rel_path>` confined to that directory — never from
  /// `storage_path` — and a link out of it reads as no bytes.
  fn place_one(project: &Project, row: &KeptRow) -> Result<Placed> {
      let kind = if row.upload {
          ContentKind::Uploads
      } else {
          ContentKind::Artifacts
      };
      let home_dir = content_dir(&StoreScope::Home, kind)?;
      let home_dir = home_dir
          .canonicalize()
          .with_context(|| format!("failed to canonicalize {}", home_dir.display()))?;
      let tail = row.rel_path.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| row.id.clone());
      let rel_path = format!("{KEPT_DIR}/{}-{}/{tail}", project.name, project.id);
      let target = confine_to_root(&home_dir, &home_dir.join(&rel_path))?;
      let source_root = project.dir.join(kind.dir_name());
      let source = match row.rel_path.as_deref() {
          Some(rel) if source_root.is_dir() => confine_to_root(&source_root, &source_root.join(rel))
              .ok()
              .filter(|path| path.is_file()),
          _ => None,
      };
      let written = match source {
          Some(source) => {
              copy_fresh(&source, &target)?;
              Some(target.clone())
          }
          None => None,
      };
      Ok(Placed {
          id: row.id.clone(),
          upload: row.upload,
          rel_path,
          storage_path: target.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
          written,
      })
  }

  /// `source` to a `target` that must not exist yet, synced.
  fn copy_fresh(source: &Path, target: &Path) -> Result<()> {
      let dir = target
          .parent()
          .with_context(|| format!("{} has no parent", target.display()))?;
      fs::create_dir_all(dir).with_context(|| format!("failed to create {}", dir.display()))?;
      let mut from = fs::File::open(source)
          .with_context(|| format!("failed to open {}", source.display()))?;
      let mut to = fs::OpenOptions::new()
          .write(true)
          .create_new(true)
          .open(target)
          .with_context(|| format!("failed to create {}", target.display()))?;
      let copied = std::io::copy(&mut from, &mut to).and_then(|_| to.sync_all());
      if let Err(e) = copied {
          drop(to);
          remove_best_effort(target);
          return Err(e).with_context(|| {
              format!("failed to copy {} to {}", source.display(), target.display())
          });
      }
      fsync_dir(dir);
      Ok(())
  }

  fn unplace(placed: &[Placed]) {
      for p in placed {
          if let Some(path) = &p.written {
              remove_best_effort(path);
          }
      }
  }

  fn strings(conn: &Connection, sql: &str, root: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
      let mut stmt = conn.prepare(sql)?;
      let out = stmt
          .query_map(rusqlite::params![root], |row| row.get::<_, String>(0))?
          .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<String>>>()?;
      Ok(out)
  }

  /// §6 *Delete its data*, steps 1 and 2: the files a surviving message links
  /// are copied into the root store, then one transaction re-addresses them
  /// with no project (a by-product as its newest version only) and deletes
  /// every row naming the project in the five path columns and the rows that
  /// hang off its sessions and runs, `learning_cursor` included. A failure
  /// anywhere deletes nothing and takes the copies back. Never iterates
  /// `storage_path`; removes no file of the project (step 3 is the route's).
  pub fn delete_project_data(db: &Database, project: &Project) -> Result<DeleteOutcome> {
      let root = project.root_string();
      let rows = db.with_connection(|conn| kept_rows(conn, &root))?;
      let mut placed: Vec<Placed> = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());
      for row in &rows {
          match place_one(project, row) {
              Ok(p) => placed.push(p),
              Err(e) => {
                  unplace(&placed);
                  return Err(e.context(format!(
                      "keeping file {} of {root}; nothing was deleted",
                      row.id
                  )));
              }
          }
      }
      let result = db.with_connection(|conn| {
          let tx = conn.unchecked_transaction()?;
          let outcome = delete_within(&tx, &root, &placed)?;
          tx.commit()?;
          Ok(outcome)
      });
      if result.is_err() {
          unplace(&placed);
      }
      result
  }

  fn delete_within(tx: &Connection, root: &str, placed: &[Placed]) -> Result<DeleteOutcome> {
      let bind = rusqlite::params![root];
      // A file linked from a surviving message after the copies were made would
      // lose that link with the project's rows: refuse. The other direction — a
      // copied file whose surviving link went meanwhile — is still re-addressed
      // into the root store; the orphan-upload sweep takes an unlinked upload
      // once its grace period has passed.
      if let Some(row) = kept_rows(tx, root)?
          .iter()
          .find(|row| !placed.iter().any(|p| p.id == row.id))
      {
          bail!(
              "file {} of {root} was attached to another conversation while its data was being \
               deleted; nothing was deleted — try again",
              row.id
          );
      }
      let session_ids = strings(tx, &format!("{DOOMED_SESSIONS} ORDER BY id"), root)?;
      let message_ids: Vec<i64> = {
          let mut stmt = tx.prepare(&format!(
              "SELECT id FROM conversation_messages WHERE {DOOMED_MESSAGE} ORDER BY id"
          ))?;
          let ids = stmt
              .query_map(bind, |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))?
              .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<i64>>>()?;
          ids
      };
      // Conversations that stay but lose a message naming the project.
      let touched = strings(
          tx,
          &format!(
              "SELECT DISTINCT session_id FROM conversation_messages
                WHERE workspace_root = ?1 AND session_id IS NOT NULL
                  AND session_id NOT IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS})"
          ),
          root,
      )?;

      // Step 1's rows, re-addressed before anything they hang off goes.
      for p in placed {
          tx.execute(
              "UPDATE file_assets
                  SET project_root = NULL, rel_path = ?2, storage_path = ?3,
                      missing_since = CASE WHEN ?4 THEN NULL ELSE datetime('now') END,
                      updated_at = datetime('now')
                WHERE id = ?1 AND project_root = ?5",
              rusqlite::params![p.id, p.rel_path, p.storage_path, p.written.is_some(), root],
          )?;
          if !p.upload {
              tx.execute(
                  "DELETE FROM artifact_versions
                    WHERE artifact_id = ?1
                      AND version <> (SELECT version FROM file_assets WHERE id = ?1)",
                  rusqlite::params![p.id],
              )?;
              tx.execute(
                  "UPDATE artifact_versions SET rel_path = ?2 WHERE artifact_id = ?1",
                  rusqlite::params![p.id, p.rel_path],
              )?;
              tx.execute(
                  "UPDATE file_assets SET version_count = 1 WHERE id = ?1",
                  rusqlite::params![p.id],
              )?;
          }
      }

      // Messages first (their feedback and attachment links cascade), then
      // what hangs off the sessions, then the sessions.
      let messages = tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM conversation_messages WHERE {DOOMED_MESSAGE}"),
          bind,
      )?;
      for id in &touched {
          tx.execute(
              "UPDATE session
                  SET message_count = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversation_messages WHERE session_id = ?1),
                      updated_at = datetime('now')
                WHERE id = ?1",
              rusqlite::params![id],
          )?;
      }
      let tool_calls = tx.execute(
          &format!(
              "DELETE FROM tool_execution_log
                WHERE session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS}) OR task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"
          ),
          bind,
      )?;
      // A queued follow-up naming the project goes even when its session is
      // another project's: left, it would start later in a deleted project.
      let followups = tx.execute(
          &format!(
              "DELETE FROM lane_followups
                WHERE workspace_path = ?1 OR session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS})"
          ),
          bind,
      )?;
      tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM learning_cursor WHERE session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS})"),
          bind,
      )?;
      // A run of another project started from one of these conversations
      // keeps its row and loses the link, as `delete_session` does it.
      tx.execute(
          &format!(
              "UPDATE task SET session_id = NULL, updated_at = datetime('now')
                WHERE session_id IN ({DOOMED_SESSIONS})"
          ),
          bind,
      )?;
      let sessions = tx.execute("DELETE FROM session WHERE workspace_id = ?1", bind)?;

      let spans = tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM subagent_span WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"),
          bind,
      )?;
      let run_events = tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM event_log WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"),
          bind,
      )?;
      tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM dispatch_decisions WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"),
          bind,
      )?;
      tx.execute(
          &format!("DELETE FROM llm_call_log WHERE task_id IN ({DOOMED_TASKS})"),
          bind,
      )?;
      let tasks = tx.execute("DELETE FROM task WHERE workspace_id = ?1", bind)?;

      // The project's files the kept set did not take (their versions cascade).
      let uploads = tx.execute(
          "DELETE FROM file_assets WHERE project_root = ?1 AND origin = 'upload'",
          bind,
      )?;
      let artifacts = tx.execute("DELETE FROM file_assets WHERE project_root = ?1", bind)?;

      Ok(DeleteOutcome {
          counts: PurgeCounts {
              sessions,
              messages,
              tool_calls,
              followups,
              tasks,
              spans,
              run_events,
              uploads,
              artifacts,
          },
          kept: KeptFiles {
              uploads: placed.iter().filter(|p| p.upload).count(),
              artifacts: placed.iter().filter(|p| !p.upload).count(),
          },
          session_ids,
          message_ids,
      })
  }
  ```

  (`tool_execution_log` rows are deleted, as today's purge does, not de-indexed as `delete_session` does under R51:
  a whole project's run history is what the person asked to delete.)

  ```rust
  /// §6 step 3's last part: `projects/<name>/` removed as one directory, under
  /// [`projects::lock`] so no `register` races it. The folder is reached by
  /// name under `projects_dir()`, never through `project.dir` (canonical, so
  /// through a link it would be the link's target): `projects/` and the
  /// folder must both be real directories, and the folder must still record
  /// this project's id. `Ok(false)` when it is already gone.
  pub fn remove_project_folder(project: &Project) -> Result<bool> {
      let _held = projects::lock();
      let projects_dir = projects::projects_dir()?;
      for path in [projects_dir.clone(), projects_dir.join(&project.name)] {
          match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
              Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_dir() => {}
              Ok(_) => bail!(
                  "{} is not a real directory (a link or a file); it was left in place",
                  path.display()
              ),
              Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),
              Err(e) => {
                  return Err(e).with_context(|| format!("failed to stat {}", path.display()));
              }
          }
      }
      let folder = projects_dir.join(&project.name);
      match projects::read_project_dir(&folder)? {
          Some(found) if found.id == project.id => {}
          _ => bail!(
              "{} no longer records project {}; it was left in place",
              folder.display(),
              project.id
          ),
      }
      fs::remove_dir_all(&folder)
          .with_context(|| format!("failed to remove {}", folder.display()))?;
      fsync_dir(&projects_dir);
      Ok(true)
  }
  ```

      assert_eq!(h.service.remove_project(&p.id).unwrap(), 2);

      let indexed = |key: &str, id: &NoteId| {
          h.service.index.get(key, &id.to_string()).unwrap().is_some()
      };
      assert!(!indexed(&alice_p_key, &alice_p.id));
      assert!(!indexed(&bob_p_key, &bob_p.id));
      assert!(indexed(&alice_q_key, &alice_q.id));
      assert!(indexed(&home_key, &home.id));

      let keys: Vec<String> = files::list_snapshots()
          .unwrap()
          .into_iter()
          .filter_map(|(_, parsed)| parsed.ok())
          .map(|s| s.partition_key)
          .collect();
      assert!(!keys.contains(&alice_p_key));
      assert!(!keys.contains(&bob_p_key));
      assert!(keys.contains(&alice_q_key));
      assert!(keys.contains(&home_key));

      // The note files go with the folder, not with this call.
      assert!(p.dir.join("memory").join(files::OWNERS_DIR).is_dir());
      assert_eq!(h.service.remove_project(&p.id).unwrap(), 0, "nothing left to drop");
  }

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** In `management.rs` add `use openalpaca_storage::store::projects::ProjectId;` after `use openalpaca_storage::store::StoreScope;`, and in the `impl MemoryService` block, after `doctor`:

  ```rust
      /// ST-19 step 3 (design §6, *Delete its data*): every owner's partition
      /// of the project — a control snapshot carrying its id — is dropped from
      /// the index, forgotten by this process's fingerprints, scans and parse
      /// cache, and its snapshot removed from `state/memory-control/`. The note
      /// files go with `projects/<name>/` (`project_life::remove_project_folder`).
      ///
      /// The caller holds [`MemoryService::quiesce`] for the project; this
      /// takes no write slot, so it never waits on that hold. Answers how many
      /// partitions were dropped. An unreadable snapshot is skipped: it cannot
      /// be told to be this project's.
      pub fn remove_project(&self, project_id: &ProjectId) -> Result<usize, MemoryError> {
          let snapshots = files::list_snapshots()?;
          let mut fingerprints = self.fingerprints.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
          let mut last_scans = self.last_scans.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
          let mut removed = 0;
          for (path, parsed) in snapshots {
              let Ok(snapshot) = parsed else {
                  continue;
              };
              if snapshot.scope != files::SnapshotScope::Project
                  || snapshot.project_id.as_ref() != Some(project_id)
              {
                  continue;
              }
              let key = snapshot.partition_key;
              self.indexed(self.index.remove_partition(&key))?;
              fingerprints.remove(&key);
              last_scans.remove(&key);
              self.parse_cache.evict_partition(&key);
              match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
                  Ok(()) => {}
                  Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
                  Err(e) => {
                      return Err(MemoryError::Internal(anyhow::Error::new(e).context(
                          format!("could not remove the control snapshot {}", path.display()),
                      )));
                  }
              }
              removed += 1;
          }
          Ok(removed)
      }
  ```

  Replace `get_workspace` (and delete `workspace_json`, its only helper) with:

  ```rust
  // ── GET /v1/workspaces ───────────────────────────────────────────

  /// With no `path`: every project OpenAlpaca knows, as its folder under
  /// `projects/` records it, sorted by folder name — a bare array (§9).
  /// Creates nothing.
  pub(crate) fn list_workspaces() -> Response {
      match projects::list() {
          Ok(list) => Json(list.iter().map(ProjectView::from).collect::<Vec<_>>()).into_response(),
          Err(e) => api_error(
              StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
              "IO_ERROR",
              format!("the projects folder could not be read: {e:#}"),
          ),
      }
  }

  /// What a path resolves to — the way a turn's `x-workspace-path` is
  /// resolved, registering nothing (§3) — and the rows recorded under that
  /// root, so a caller sees what a re-point would move and what the delete
  /// would refuse on.
  pub(crate) fn get_workspace(db: &Database, query: WorkspaceQuery) -> Response {
      let Some(raw) = query.path else {
          return list_workspaces();
      };
      let path = match canonical_path(&raw) {
          Ok(path) => path,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let resolved = match projects::resolve(Path::new(&path)) {
          Ok(resolved) => resolved,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(
                  StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                  "IO_ERROR",
                  format!("{path} could not be resolved: {e:#}"),
              );
          }
      };
      let Some(resolved) = resolved else {
          return Json(WorkspaceView {
              path,
              root: None,
              id: None,
              name: None,
              missing: false,
              rows: RowCountsView::default(),
              active_tasks: 0,
              queued_tasks: 0,
          })
          .into_response();
      };
      let root = resolved.root_string();
      let rows = match ArtifactStore::new(db).workspace_rows(&root, None) {
          Ok(rows) => rows,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", e.to_string());
          }
      };
      let project = resolved.project.as_ref();
      Json(WorkspaceView {
          path,
          root: Some(root),
          id: project.map(|p| p.id.to_string()),
          name: project.map(|p| p.name.clone()),
          missing: project.is_some_and(|p| p.missing),
          rows: RowCountsView::from(&rows.counts),
          active_tasks: rows.active_tasks,
          queued_tasks: rows.queued_tasks,
      })
      .into_response()
  }
  ```

  /// Choose a folder: register the project it resolves to — the git repository
  /// it lies in, else the folder itself (R10, ST-6) — and answer it. A choice
  /// already registered answers the same project. The fifth registration site
  /// of §2.2: the daemon registers, a read never does.
  pub(crate) fn choose_workspace(request: ChooseWorkspaceRequest) -> Response {
      let path = match canonical_path(&request.path) {

      match projects::choose(Path::new(&path)) {

  }

  ```rust
  /// The registered project a client path resolves to, or the answer that
  /// refuses it: `404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` for a root no folder under
  /// `projects/` records (R12's words) or a path in no project.
  #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
  fn registered_project(path: &str) -> Result<Project, Response> {
      match projects::resolve(Path::new(path)) {
          Ok(Some(ResolvedProject {
              project: Some(project),
              ..
          })) => Ok(project),
          Ok(Some(resolved)) => Err(api_error(
              StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
              "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND",
              ProjectError::NotRegistered {
                  root: resolved.root_string(),
              }
              .to_string(),
          )),
          Ok(None) => Err(api_error(
              StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
              "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND",
              format!(
                  "{path} is in no project: no folder under projects/ records it and no git \
                   repository holds it"
              ),
          )),
          Err(e) => Err(api_error(
              StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
              "IO_ERROR",
              format!("{path} could not be resolved: {e:#}"),
          )),
      }
  }

  /// How often, and for how long, the re-point and the delete try for the
  /// project's memory slot. `quiesce` refuses rather than waits, and the 30 s
  /// reconciliation and an index rebuild hold the same slot for moments, so
  /// three seconds outlasts them in practice and is short enough for a dialog.
  pub(crate) const QUIESCE_RETRY_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);
  pub(crate) const QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

  /// `MemoryService::quiesce`, tried every [`QUIESCE_RETRY_EVERY`] until
  /// [`QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR`] has passed; the last refusal is returned.
  async fn quiesce_project(
      memory: &MemoryService,
      id: &ProjectId,
  ) -> Result<QuiesceGuard, MemoryError> {
      let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR;
      loop {
          match memory.quiesce(id) {
              Ok(guard) => return Ok(guard),
              Err(e) if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= deadline => return Err(e),
              Err(_) => tokio::time::sleep(QUIESCE_RETRY_EVERY).await,
          }
      }
  }
  ```

  Replace `rebase_workspace` (the whole function and its doc) with:

  ```rust
  // ── PATCH /v1/workspaces ─────────────────────────────────────────

  /// Re-point a project onto its new path (§6): the rows of the five path
  /// columns and both `storage_path` prefixes in one transaction, and the
  /// project's folder under `projects/` renamed — `project_life::repoint`.
  ///
  /// Owner-scoped (R40): a project holding another owner's rows is the same
  /// `404` an unknown one is. Refused while a run is `running` or `paused`
  /// there, and while the project's memory slot stays held for
  /// [`QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR`]. The target's refusals are `repoint`'s: not a
  /// directory (422), the home store (409), already a project or named by the
  /// rows (409, ST-20), the same path (400).
  pub(crate) async fn rebase_workspace(
      db: &Database,
      memory: &MemoryService,
      owner_id: &str,
      request: RebaseRequest,
  ) -> Response {
      let old = match canonical_path(&request.old_path) {
          Ok(path) => path,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let new = match canonical_path(&request.new_path) {
          Ok(path) => path,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let project = match registered_project(&old) {
          Ok(project) => project,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let root = project.root_string();
      let rows = match ArtifactStore::new(db).workspace_rows(&root, Some(owner_id)) {
          Ok(rows) => rows,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", e.to_string());
          }
      };
      if rows.other_owners > 0 {
          return owner_mismatch(&root, rows.other_owners);
      }
      if rows.active_tasks > 0 {
          return api_error(
              StatusCode::CONFLICT,
              "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
              format!(
                  "{} run(s) under {root} are still in flight; re-point it once they finish",
                  rows.active_tasks
              ),
          );
      }
      let _quiesced = match quiesce_project(memory, &project.id).await {
          Ok(guard) => guard,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(
                  StatusCode::CONFLICT,
                  "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
                  format!(
                      "a memory write under {root} is still in flight ({e}); re-pointing now \
                       would rename its folder out from under it. Try again in a moment"
                  ),
              );
          }
      };
      match project_life::repoint(db, &project.root, Path::new(&new)) {
          Ok(done) => Json(RepointView {
              old_path: done.before.root_string(),
              new_path: done.after.root_string(),
              moved: RowCountsView::from(&done.rows),
              project: ProjectView::from(&done.after),
          })
          .into_response(),
          Err(e) => project_error_response(&e).unwrap_or_else(|| {
              api_error(
                  StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                  "WORKSPACE_MOVE_FAILED",
                  format!("{root} could not be re-pointed onto {new}: {e:#}"),
              )
          }),
      }
  }
  ```

  Refusals: `400 INVALID_PATH`, `404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (no registered project there, or another owner's rows — R40), `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` (the lead's R-S8: the path lies inside a registered project rather than being its root; the answer names the root, and nothing is counted), `409 WORKSPACE_BUSY` (a `queued`/`running`/`paused` run under the root, a live run of one of its conversations, or the memory slot held past `QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR`). No new code (`interfaces.md` §8): a delete whose copies or transaction fail answers `500 DB_ERROR`, today's purge code for its transaction, with a message saying nothing was deleted; a resolution that cannot be read is `500 IO_ERROR` (S5a.7's `registered_project`). Choice: the delete also calls `LearningQueue::forget_session` for each deleted conversation, as `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` does (`routes/sessions.rs:815`) — the old purge never did (fact check, claim 2/5).           self.session("s-q", &qr);

          self.home_session("s-h");
          let m_h = self.home_message("s-h");
          let u_alone = self.upload(&p, "alone.txt");
          let u_shared = self.upload(&p, "shared.txt");
          self.by_product(&p, "Report", OWNER);
          self.link(m_p, &u_alone);
          self.link(m_p, &u_shared);
          self.link(m_h, &u_shared);
          self.note(OWNER, Some(p.root.as_path()), "Release on Fridays");
          self.note(OTHER, Some(p.root.as_path()), "Staging is blue");
          self.note(OWNER, Some(q.root.as_path()), "Bystander note");
          self.note(OWNER, None, "Kept at home");
          std::fs::write(p.root.join("README.md"), b"the user's own file").expect("own file");
          Scene { p, q, u_shared, session_dir }
      }
  }

  async fn a_real_delete_removes_rows_logs_every_owners_notes_and_the_folder_and_nothing_else() {
      let w = World::new();
      let s = w.scene();
      let bystander_snapshots = project_snapshots(&s.q.id);

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&s.p.root, false).await;

      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
      assert_eq!(body["applied"], true);
      assert_eq!(
          body["removed"],
          serde_json::json!({"session_dirs": 1, "memory_partitions": 2, "project_folder": true})
      );
      assert_eq!(body["counts"]["messages"], 1);
      assert_eq!(body["counts"]["memory_notes"], 2);
      assert_eq!(body["kept"], serde_json::json!({"uploads": 1, "artifacts": 0}));

      // The project's rows, log, partitions and folder are gone.
      assert_eq!(w.count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session"), 2);
      assert_eq!(w.count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task"), 0);
      assert!(!s.session_dir.exists());
      assert!(!s.p.dir.exists());
      assert_eq!(projects::lookup(&s.p.root).expect("lookup"), None);
      assert_eq!(project_snapshots(&s.p.id), 0);
      // Every owner's notes: a read from the deleted root is an empty project (R12).
      assert_eq!(
          crate::test_util::note_titles(&w.memory, OWNER, Some(s.p.root.as_path())),
          vec!["Kept at home".to_string()]
      );
      assert!(crate::test_util::note_titles(&w.memory, OTHER, Some(s.p.root.as_path())).is_empty());
      // The upload a home conversation still shows reads from the root store.
      let shared = FileAssetRepository::new(&w.db)
          .get_by_id(&s.u_shared)
          .expect("read")
          .expect("kept");
      assert!(
          std::path::Path::new(&shared.storage_path)
              .starts_with(w.home.join("uploads").join(project_life::KEPT_DIR)),
          "{}",
          shared.storage_path
      );
      assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&shared.storage_path).expect("bytes"), b"shared.txt");

      // Nothing else: the bystander, the home notes, the project's own folder.
      assert!(s.q.dir.is_dir());
      assert_eq!(project_snapshots(&s.q.id), bystander_snapshots);
      assert_eq!(
          crate::test_util::note_titles(&w.memory, OWNER, Some(s.q.root.as_path())),
          vec!["Bystander note".to_string(), "Kept at home".to_string()]
      );
      assert_eq!(std::fs::read(s.p.root.join("README.md")).expect("own file"), b"the user's own file");
      assert!(s.p.root.join(".git").is_dir());
  }

  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_queued_run_or_a_live_lane_refuses_the_delete_before_anything_moves() {
      let w = World::new();
      let s = w.scene();
      w.task("t-queued", &text(&s.p.root), "queued");

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&s.p.root, false).await;
      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::CONFLICT, "{body}");
      assert_eq!(error_code(&body), "WORKSPACE_BUSY");

      // A run dispatched with no workspace of its own, from one of p's
      // conversations: only the lane registry knows it is live.
      w.db
          .with_connection(|conn| {
              conn.execute("DELETE FROM task WHERE id = 't-queued'", [])?;
              conn.execute(
                  "INSERT INTO task (id, title, created_by, source_lane, session_id, status)
                   VALUES ('t-live', 't', 'test', 'test', 's-p', 'running')",
                  [],
              )?;
              Ok(())
          })
          .expect("a live run");
      w.ctx.register_workflow_for_lane("s-p", "t-live");

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&s.p.root, false).await;
      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::CONFLICT, "{body}");
      assert_eq!(error_code(&body), "WORKSPACE_BUSY");
      assert!(body["error"]["message"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().contains("s-p"), "{body}");
      assert!(s.p.dir.is_dir());
      assert_eq!(w.count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session WHERE id = 's-p'"), 1);
  }

  /// Waits out the real `QUIESCE_RETRY_FOR` (3 s), as the re-point's twin does.
  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_held_memory_slot_answers_busy_and_deletes_nothing() {
      let w = World::new();
      let s = w.scene();
      let _held = w.memory.quiesce(&s.p.id).expect("the slot is idle");

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&s.p.root, false).await;

      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::CONFLICT, "{body}");
      assert_eq!(error_code(&body), "WORKSPACE_BUSY");
      assert_eq!(w.count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session"), 3);
      assert!(s.p.dir.is_dir());
  }

  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_project_holding_another_owners_rows_is_a_404() {
      let w = World::new();

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&p.root, true).await;

  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_path_no_project_records_is_a_404_and_registers_nothing() {
      let w = World::new();

      let plain = w.dir("plain");
      for (path, says) in [(&repo, "is not a project OpenAlpaca knows"), (&plain, "is in no project")] {
          let (status, body) = w.delete(path, false).await;

  /// The lead's R-S8: deleting a project's data takes the project exactly —
  /// its root as registered. A path inside it is refused before anything is
  /// counted, the answer naming the root, on a dry run and a real one alike;
  /// the root itself is then deleted.
  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_path_inside_a_project_is_refused_naming_its_root_and_nothing_is_deleted() {
      let w = World::new();
      let s = w.scene();
      let root = text(&s.p.root);
      let inside = s.p.root.join("src");
      std::fs::create_dir_all(&inside).expect("a folder inside the project");

      for dry_run in [true, false] {
          let (status, body) = w.delete(&inside, dry_run).await;
          assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, "{body}");
          assert_eq!(error_code(&body), "WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT");
          let message = body["error"]["message"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
          assert!(
              message.contains(&format!("inside the project rooted at {root}")),
              "{message}"
          );
          assert!(
              message.contains(&format!("Delete the data of {root}")),
              "{message}"
          );
      }
      assert!(s.p.dir.is_dir());
      assert!(s.session_dir.exists());
      assert_eq!(w.count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session"), 3);

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&s.p.root, false).await;
      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
      assert!(!s.p.dir.exists());
  }

  /// The delete removes `projects/<name>/` as one directory; a row whose
  /// `storage_path` points anywhere else is never followed.
  #[tokio::test]
  async fn the_delete_never_follows_a_storage_path_out_of_the_project_folder() {
      let w = World::new();
      let p = w.project("tampered");
      let file = w.by_product(&p, "Report", OWNER);
      let decoy = w.dir("elsewhere").join("decoy.md");
      std::fs::write(&decoy, b"not OpenAlpaca's").expect("decoy");
      w.db
          .with_connection(|conn| {
              conn.execute(
                  "UPDATE file_assets SET storage_path = ?1 WHERE id = ?2",
                  [text(&decoy).as_str(), file.as_str()],
              )?;
              Ok(())
          })
          .expect("tamper");

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&p.root, false).await;

      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
      assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&decoy).expect("decoy"), b"not OpenAlpaca's");
      assert!(!p.dir.exists());
  }

  #[tokio::test]
  async fn a_delete_stands_the_writers_down_and_announces_every_conversation() {
      use openalpaca_core::session_log::{Record, RecordType, session_dir_name};

      let w = World::new();
      let p = w.project("narrated");
      let root = text(&p.root);
      w.session("s-a", &root);
      w.session("s-b", &root);
      let handle = w.log.open("s-a", Some("owner-1:gui"), Some("gui"), None);
      assert!(handle.emit(Record::new(RecordType::UserMsg)));
      assert!(handle.flush().await);
      let dir = w.sessions_root.join(session_dir_name("s-a"));
      assert!(dir.is_dir(), "the writer created {}", dir.display());
      let mut rx = w.bus.subscribe();

      let (status, _) = w.delete(&p.root, true).await;
      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK);
      assert!(rx.try_recv().is_err(), "a dry run announced a deletion");

      let (status, body) = w.delete(&p.root, false).await;
      assert_eq!(status, StatusCode::OK, "{body}");
      assert!(!dir.exists());
      assert!(handle.is_closed(), "the writer was not stood down");
      handle.emit(Record::new(RecordType::AssistantMsg));
      handle.flush().await;
      assert!(!dir.exists(), "a late record re-created {}", dir.display());

      let mut deleted = Vec::new();
      while let Ok(event) = rx.try_recv() {
          if let openalpaca_core::events::SystemEvent::SessionChanged {
              session_id,
              lane_key,
              status,
              ..
          } = event
          {
              assert_eq!(status, "deleted");
              assert_eq!(lane_key, session_id, "the fixture's lane key is the id");
              deleted.push(session_id);
          }
      }
      deleted.sort();
      assert_eq!(deleted, vec!["s-a".to_string(), "s-b".to_string()]);
  }

  ```rust
  //! `/v1/workspaces` — a project's life (design §6, §9).
  //!
  //! ```text
  //! GET   /v1/workspaces                      -> every project: [{id, root, name, missing}]
  //! GET   /v1/workspaces?path=<abs>           -> what the path resolves to, and the rows there
  //! POST  /v1/workspaces {path}               -> choose a folder: register its project (R10)
  //! PATCH /v1/workspaces {old_path,new_path}  -> re-point a project onto its new path
  //! POST  /v1/workspaces/purge {path,dry_run} -> delete everything OpenAlpaca holds for it (ST-19)
  //! ```
  //!
  //! A project is a folder under `~/.openalpaca/projects/` whose `project.json`
  //! records its id and root (`store::projects`); rows name it by that root in
  //! five columns. These routes resolve a client's path the one way a turn's is
  //! resolved (`projects::resolve`), answer the resolved root, and refuse rather
  //! than guess: `404` when no project is registered there or a row there is
  //! another owner's (R40), `409` while a run is in flight or the project's
  //! memory slot stays held, `409`/`422` for a target that is the home store,
  //! already a project, or not a directory.
  //!
  //! The delete answers a plan, one line per entry in the seeded README's
  //! retention terms, `delete` or `keep`; `dry_run` defaults to **true**, so a
  //! caller that forgets the field gets the plan and not the deletion. Under the
  //! project's memory slot it deletes the rows — keeping, in the root store,
  //! every file another conversation still links — the conversations' logs, the
  //! memory partitions of every owner and `projects/<name>/`. It never touches
  //! the project's own folder and never iterates `storage_path`. It takes the
  //! project exactly, by its root as registered: a path inside a project is
  //! `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT`, naming the root, rather than a deletion of
  //! the whole project for a path that named one folder of it.
