  // ── POST /v1/workspaces/purge ────────────────────────────────────

  /// What the delete needs from `AppState`, named so its refusals and its order
  /// can be tested without a gateway.
  pub(crate) struct PurgeDeps<'a> {
      pub db: &'a Database,
      /// The live lane registry — half of the in-flight guard.
      pub ctx: &'a SharedContext,
      /// Where `session_changed{status:"deleted"}` goes, one per conversation.
      pub bus: &'a openalpaca_core::bus::EventBus,
      /// The local user; the delete is owner-scoped (R40).
      pub owner: &'a str,
      pub memory: &'a Arc<MemoryService>,
      /// The home store's `sessions/`. `None` when it could not be resolved at
      /// boot: the rows still go, the directories are left and logged.
      pub sessions_root: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
      /// The live writers: each is stood down before its directory goes, or its
      /// next record re-creates it.
      pub session_log: Option<Arc<openalpaca_core::session_log::SessionLogService>>,
      /// The learning queue: a deleted conversation's pending turns are
      /// forgotten, as `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` does.
      pub learning: Option<Arc<openalpaca_core::memory::learning::LearningQueue>>,
  }

  /// The plan, in the README's retention terms; every entry named, zeroes included.
  fn plan_entries(plan: &DeletePlan) -> Vec<DeletePlanEntry> {
      let c = &plan.counts;
      let folder = format!("{}/{}/", projects::PROJECTS_DIR, plan.project.name);
      let line = |entry: String, holds: String, retention: &str, action: &'static str| {
          DeletePlanEntry {
              entry,
              holds,
              retention: retention.to_string(),
              action,
          }
      };
      vec![
          line(
              "sessions/".to_string(),
              format!(
                  "{} conversations, {} messages, {} tool calls, {} follow-ups — their logs live \
                   in the home store's sessions/",
                  c.sessions, c.messages, c.tool_calls, c.followups
              ),
              "size-capped, optional age sweep",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              "runs (database)".to_string(),
              format!("{} runs, {} subagent spans, {} run events", c.tasks, c.spans, c.run_events),
              "never swept — removed only when you ask",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              format!("{folder}uploads/"),
              format!("{} uploads handed to this project's conversations", c.uploads),
              "swept: an upload attached to no message is deleted once past the grace period",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              format!("{folder}artifacts/"),
              format!("{} by-products of this project's runs, with every version", c.artifacts),
              "never garbage-collected — removed only when you ask",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              format!("{folder}memory/"),
              format!(
                  "{} memory notes of every owner, in {} partitions, with their history",
                  plan.memory_notes, plan.memory_partitions
              ),
              "yours — never swept",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              folder.clone(),
              "project.json — the project's id and path; OpenAlpaca forgets the project".to_string(),
              "store metadata",
              "delete",
          ),
          line(
              "uploads/ (root store)".to_string(),
              format!(
                  "{} uploads another conversation still shows, moved here under {}/",
                  plan.kept.uploads,
                  project_life::KEPT_DIR
              ),
              "swept: an upload attached to no message is deleted once past the grace period",
              "keep",
          ),
          line(
              "artifacts/ (root store)".to_string(),
              format!(
                  "{} by-products another conversation still shows, moved here under {}/ as \
                   their newest version",
                  plan.kept.artifacts,
                  project_life::KEPT_DIR
              ),
              "never garbage-collected",
              "keep",
          ),
          line(
              plan.project.root_string(),
              "the project's own folder — OpenAlpaca never touches it".to_string(),
              "yours",
              "keep",
          ),
      ]
  }

  fn delete_view(
      plan: &DeletePlan,
      counts: &PurgeCounts,
      kept: KeptFiles,
      removed: Option<RemovedView>,
  ) -> DeleteDataView {
      let dry_run = removed.is_none();
      DeleteDataView {
          dry_run,
          applied: !dry_run,
          project: ProjectView::from(&plan.project),
          entries: plan_entries(plan),
          counts: DeleteCountsView {
              sessions: counts.sessions,
              messages: counts.messages,
              tool_calls: counts.tool_calls,
              followups: counts.followups,
              tasks: counts.tasks,
              spans: counts.spans,
              run_events: counts.run_events,
              uploads: counts.uploads,
              artifacts: counts.artifacts,
              memory_notes: plan.memory_notes,
          },
          kept: KeptView {
              uploads: kept.uploads,
              artifacts: kept.artifacts,
          },
          removed,
      }
  }

  /// The deleted conversations' log directories, each writer stood down first.
  async fn remove_session_dirs(deps: &PurgeDeps<'_>, session_ids: &[String]) -> usize {
      let Some(sessions_root) = deps.sessions_root.as_deref() else {
          if !session_ids.is_empty() {
              tracing::warn!(
                  "Deleted {} conversation(s) with no sessions root resolved; their logs stay on disk",
                  session_ids.len()
              );
          }
          return 0;
      };
      let mut removed = 0;
      for id in session_ids {
          if let Some(service) = deps.session_log.as_deref() {
              service.forget(id).await;
          }
          let dir = sessions_root.join(openalpaca_core::session_log::session_dir_name(id));
          if !dir.exists() {
              continue;
          }
          match std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir) {
              Ok(()) => removed += 1,
              Err(e) => tracing::warn!("The delete could not remove {}: {e}", dir.display()),
          }
      }
      removed
  }

  /// `session_changed{status:"deleted"}` for every conversation the
  /// transaction deleted — what `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` publishes.
  fn announce_deleted_sessions(deps: &PurgeDeps<'_>, plan: &DeletePlan, outcome: &DeleteOutcome) {
      for id in &outcome.session_ids {
          let lane_key = plan
              .sessions
              .iter()
              .find(|session| &session.id == id)
              .map(|session| session.lane_key.clone())
              .unwrap_or_default();
          let _ = deps
              .bus
              .publish(openalpaca_core::events::SystemEvent::SessionChanged {
                  session_id: id.clone(),
                  lane_key,
                  status: "deleted".to_string(),
                  task_id: None,
                  timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),
              });
      }
  }

  /// Delete everything OpenAlpaca holds for one project (ST-19), or answer the
  /// plan — which is what happens unless the caller says `dry_run: false`.
  ///
  /// The project is taken exactly: a path that resolves to a registered
  /// project but is not its root is `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT`, naming the
  /// root, before anything is counted — the one verb that deletes
  /// conversations and notes never walks a subfolder up to its project.
  ///
  /// Refused, before anything moves, while a run is in flight: a `queued`,
  /// `running` or `paused` run whose `workspace_id` is the root
  /// (`busy_tasks`), or a live run of one of its conversations that was
  /// dispatched with no workspace of its own (`session_has_live_run`). Then,
  /// holding the project's memory slot: the rows (`delete_project_data`,
  /// files another conversation links kept in the root store), the
  /// conversations' log directories, every owner's partitions
  /// (`MemoryService::remove_project`) and `projects/<name>/`. A failure
  /// after the rows went is logged and reported in `removed`, never a `500`:
  /// the deletion the caller asked for has happened.
  pub(crate) async fn delete_workspace_data(deps: &PurgeDeps<'_>, request: PurgeRequest) -> Response {
      let path = match canonical_path(&request.path) {
          Ok(path) => path,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let project = match registered_project(&path) {
          Ok(project) => project,
          Err(response) => return response,
      };
      let root = project.root_string();
      // The root as `register` recorded it: canonical, a missing tail as
      // written (ST-7), so a missing project's root also compares equal.
      let exact = projects::canonical_root(Path::new(&path)).is_ok_and(|p| p == project.root);
      if !exact {
          return api_error(
              StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
              "WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT",
              format!(
                  "{path} is inside the project rooted at {root}; deleting a project's data takes \
                   its root itself. Delete the data of {root} if that is what you meant"
              ),
          );
      }
      let store = ArtifactStore::new(deps.db);
      let rows = match store.workspace_rows(&root, Some(deps.owner)) {
          Ok(rows) => rows,
          Err(e) => return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", e.to_string()),
      };
      if rows.other_owners > 0 {
          return owner_mismatch(&root, rows.other_owners);
      }
      let busy = match store.busy_tasks(&root) {
          Ok(busy) => busy,
          Err(e) => return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", e.to_string()),
      };
      if busy > 0 {
          return api_error(
              StatusCode::CONFLICT,
              "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
              format!(
                  "{busy} run(s) under {root} are queued, running or paused; delete its data once \
                   they finish"
              ),
          );
      }
      let plan = match project_life::delete_plan(deps.db, &project) {
          Ok(plan) => plan,
          Err(e) => return api_error(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "DB_ERROR", format!("{e:#}")),
      };
      for session in &plan.sessions {
          if crate::routes::sessions::session_has_live_run(
              deps.db,
              deps.ctx,
              &session.id,
              &session.lane_key,
          ) {
              return api_error(
                  StatusCode::CONFLICT,
                  "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
                  format!(
                      "conversation {} of {root} has a run in flight; cancel it before deleting \
                       the project's data",
                      session.id
                  ),
              );
          }
      }
      if request.dry_run {
          return Json(delete_view(&plan, &plan.counts, plan.kept, None)).into_response();
      }

      let _quiesced = match quiesce_project(deps.memory, &project.id).await {
          Ok(guard) => guard,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(
                  StatusCode::CONFLICT,
                  "WORKSPACE_BUSY",
                  format!(
                      "a memory write under {root} is still in flight ({e}); nothing was \
                       deleted. Try again in a moment"
                  ),
              );
          }
      };
      let outcome = match project_life::delete_project_data(deps.db, &project) {
          Ok(outcome) => outcome,
          Err(e) => {
              return api_error(
                  StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                  "DB_ERROR",
                  format!("deleting the data of {root} failed, and nothing was deleted: {e:#}"),
              );
          }
      };
      let session_dirs = remove_session_dirs(deps, &outcome.session_ids).await;
      if let Some(queue) = deps.learning.as_deref() {
          for id in &outcome.session_ids {
              queue.forget_session(id);
          }
      }
      let memory_partitions = match deps.memory.remove_project(&project.id) {
          Ok(dropped) => dropped,
          Err(e) => {
              tracing::warn!(
                  "Deleted the data of {root}, but its memory partitions could not be dropped: \
                   {e}; `openalpaca memory doctor` names what is left"
              );
              0
          }
      };
      let project_folder = match project_life::remove_project_folder(&project) {
          Ok(removed) => removed,
          Err(e) => {
              tracing::warn!("Deleted the data of {root}, but its folder was left in place: {e:#}");
              false
          }
      };
      announce_deleted_sessions(deps, &plan, &outcome);
      Json(delete_view(
          &plan,
          &outcome.counts,
          outcome.kept,
          Some(RemovedView {
              session_dirs,
              memory_partitions,
              project_folder,
          }),
      ))
      .into_response()
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  /// Delete a project's data, or answer the plan. A real run flushes every live
  /// writer first — the barrier `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` awaits — so a writer
  /// holding records for a transcript about to go cannot re-create it after.
  pub async fn purge_workspace_handler(
      State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
      Json(request): Json<PurgeRequest>,
  ) -> Response {
      if !request.dry_run {
          crate::routes::sessions::flush_session_logs(&state).await;
      }
      let session_log = state.gateway.shared_context.session_log().cloned();
      delete_workspace_data(
          &PurgeDeps {
              db: &state.db,
              ctx: &state.gateway.shared_context,
              bus: &state.gateway.bus,
              owner: &state.local_user_id,
              memory: &state.memory_service,
              sessions_root: session_log
                  .as_ref()
                  .map(|service| service.root().to_path_buf()),
              session_log,
              learning: state.gateway.learning().cloned(),
          },
          request,
      )
      .await
  }

### Task S5a.9: The deleted conversations' summaries are forgotten in the home partition, never under the held slot

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/workspaces.rs` — `delete_workspace_data`, between `remove_session_dirs` and `remove_project`.
- Test: `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/workspaces/life_tests.rs`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `routes::sessions::forget_conversation_summaries(memory: Option<Arc<MemoryService>>, owner: &str, root: Option<&str>, message_ids: Vec<i64>)` (`routes/sessions.rs:841`); `test_util::{extracted_note, note_titles}` (`apps/openalpacad/src/test_util.rs:216`, `:269`).
- Produces: no new item. The call passes `root: None` — the home partition only. Why (SC-1): `MemoryService::forget` takes `begin_write` on each target's partition slot (`service/mutations.rs:396-398`), and `begin_write` waits while a `quiesce` holds that slot (`service/write_slot.rs:56-66`); the delete holds the project's slot, so a summary in the project's own partition would block the route for ever. Those summaries go whole with the partition in the next statement.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test.** Append to `life_tests.rs`:

  ```rust
  /// The delete on a thread of its own with its own runtime, so a hang fails
  /// the test instead of hanging the suite (a stuck thread is left behind when
  /// the process exits). No session writer: the test's runtime is blocked
  /// while it waits.
  fn delete_on_its_own_thread(
      w: &World,
      path: &std::path::Path,
  ) -> std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<(StatusCode, serde_json::Value)> {
      let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
      let db = w.db.clone();
      let memory = w.memory.clone();
      let bus = w.bus.clone();
      let sessions_root = w.sessions_root.clone();
      let path = text(path);
      std::thread::spawn(move || {
          let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
              .enable_all()
              .build()
              .expect("a runtime");
          let answer = runtime.block_on(async {
              let ctx = SharedContext::new();
              let deps = PurgeDeps {
                  db: &db,
                  ctx: &ctx,
                  bus: &bus,
                  owner: OWNER,
                  memory: &memory,
                  sessions_root: Some(sessions_root),
                  session_log: None,
                  learning: None,
              };
              split(delete_workspace_data(&deps, PurgeRequest { path, dry_run: false }).await).await
          });
          let _ = tx.send(answer);
      });
      rx
  }

  async fn a_delete_forgets_its_conversations_home_summaries_without_waiting_on_its_own_slot() {

      w.note(OWNER, None, "Kept at home");

          .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))

      );

  /// Every file under `dir`, with its bytes, sorted.
  fn tree(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<(PathBuf, Vec<u8>)> {

          return out;
      };

          if entry.file_type().expect("type").is_dir() {
              out.extend(tree(&path));

          }
      }

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** Replace everything in `apps/openalpaca/src/commands/store.rs` above `#[cfg(test)]` with:

  ```rust
  //! `openalpaca store` — the projects OpenAlpaca keeps a folder for (design §6).
  //!
  //! ```text
  //! openalpaca store list
  //! openalpaca store rebase <old> <new> [--dry-run]
  //! openalpaca store purge  <project> [--dry-run] [-y]
  //! ```
  //!
  //! A project's content lives at home, in `~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/`, and
  //! its path is recorded in five columns of the database. `list` shows every
  //! project and marks one whose folder is gone. `rebase` re-points a moved
  //! project — its rows and its folder's name under `projects/` — and its
  //! `--dry-run` reads what is recorded at both paths and names what the daemon
  //! would refuse. `purge` deletes everything OpenAlpaca holds for a project
  //! (ST-19) — conversations, runs, by-products, uploads, every owner's notes and
  //! its folder under `projects/` — and never the project's own folder; a file
  //! another conversation still uses is kept, moved to the root store. It prints
  //! the plan and deletes nothing unless you pass `-y`. It takes a project
  //! exactly: its root, or its folder as `store list` prints it
  //! (`projects/<name>`); the daemon refuses a path inside a project, naming
  //! the root.
  //!
  //! Everything here is `GET|PATCH /v1/workspaces` and
  //! `POST /v1/workspaces/purge`: the daemon owns the database, the memory and
  //! the session writers, and it owns the refusals; this prints them. A relative
  //! path is made absolute against this shell's directory before it is sent.

  use std::fmt::Write as _;
  use std::path::Path;

  use anyhow::{Context, Result};
  use clap::{Args, Subcommand};
  use colored::Colorize;
  use openalpaca_storage::store::projects::overlaps_home_store;
  use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

  use crate::client::DaemonClient;

  #[derive(Args)]
  pub struct StoreArgs {
      #[command(subcommand)]
      pub command: StoreCommands,
  }

  #[derive(Subcommand)]
  pub enum StoreCommands {
      /// List the projects OpenAlpaca keeps a folder for, and mark a missing one
      List,
      /// Re-point a moved project onto its new path
      Rebase {
          /// The path the project had
          old: String,
          /// The path it has now
          new: String,
          /// Report what would move and what would be refused; change nothing
          #[arg(long)]
          dry_run: bool,
      },
      /// Delete everything OpenAlpaca holds for a project (never its own folder)
      Purge {
          /// The project: its root as `store list` prints it, or its folder there
          /// (projects/<name>)
          project: String,
          /// Print the plan and change nothing — what happens anyway without -y
          #[arg(long)]
          dry_run: bool,
          /// Carry the plan out
          #[arg(short = 'y', long = "yes", conflicts_with = "dry_run")]
          yes: bool,
      },
  }

  /// One project, as the daemon answers it.
  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  struct ProjectView {
      id: String,
      root: String,
      name: String,
      #[serde(default)]
      missing: bool,
  }

  /// The rows the five path columns hold under one root.
  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
  struct RowCounts {
      #[serde(default)]
      artifacts: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      sessions: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      tasks: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      messages: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      followups: usize,
  }

  impl RowCounts {
      fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
          self.artifacts == 0
              && self.sessions == 0
              && self.tasks == 0
              && self.messages == 0
              && self.followups == 0
      }

      /// Every member named, zeroes included: "nothing else moved" is the part a
      /// reader is checking for.
      fn describe(&self) -> String {
          format!(
              "{} artifacts, {} conversations, {} runs, {} messages, {} follow-ups",
              self.artifacts, self.sessions, self.tasks, self.messages, self.followups
          )
      }
  }

  /// One path, as `GET /v1/workspaces?path=` describes it.
  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  struct WorkspaceView {
      path: String,
      #[serde(default)]
      root: Option<String>,
      #[serde(default)]
      id: Option<String>,
      #[serde(default)]
      name: Option<String>,
      #[serde(default)]
      missing: bool,
      #[serde(default)]
      rows: RowCounts,
      #[serde(default)]
      active_tasks: usize,
      /// `queued` runs: they do not stop a re-point, they do stop a delete.
      #[serde(default)]
      queued_tasks: usize,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  struct RepointResult {
      old_path: String,
      new_path: String,
      moved: RowCounts,
      project: ProjectView,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
  struct RebaseRequest<'a> {
      old_path: &'a str,
      new_path: &'a str,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
  struct PurgeRequest<'a> {
      path: &'a str,
      dry_run: bool,
  }

  /// One line of the daemon's plan: an entry, what it holds for this project,
  /// the retention class the README gives it, and `delete` or `keep`.
  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  struct PlanEntry {
      entry: String,
      holds: String,
      retention: String,
      action: String,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
  struct PurgeCounts {
      #[serde(default)]
      sessions: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      messages: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      tool_calls: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      followups: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      tasks: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      spans: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      run_events: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      uploads: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      artifacts: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      memory_notes: usize,
  }

  impl PurgeCounts {
      /// Every member named, zeroes included.
      fn describe(&self) -> String {
          format!(
              "{} conversations, {} messages, {} tool calls, {} follow-ups, {} runs, {} spans, \
               {} run events, {} uploads, {} by-products, {} memory notes",
              self.sessions,
              self.messages,
              self.tool_calls,
              self.followups,
              self.tasks,
              self.spans,
              self.run_events,
              self.uploads,
              self.artifacts,
              self.memory_notes
          )
      }
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
  struct Kept {
      #[serde(default)]
      uploads: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      artifacts: usize,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
  struct Removed {
      #[serde(default)]
      session_dirs: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      memory_partitions: usize,
      #[serde(default)]
      project_folder: bool,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  struct DeleteResult {
      #[serde(default)]
      applied: bool,
      project: ProjectView,
      #[serde(default)]
      entries: Vec<PlanEntry>,
      #[serde(default)]
      counts: PurgeCounts,
      #[serde(default)]
      kept: Kept,
      /// Present only on a real run: what the daemon actually removed.
      #[serde(default)]
      removed: Option<Removed>,
  }

  pub async fn run(args: StoreArgs) -> Result<()> {
      let client = DaemonClient::connect()?;
      let text = match args.command {
          StoreCommands::List => list(&client).await?,
          StoreCommands::Rebase { old, new, dry_run } => {
              rebase(&client, &absolute(&old)?, &absolute(&new)?, dry_run).await?
          }
          StoreCommands::Purge {
              project,
              dry_run,
              yes,
          } => {
              let root = purge_target(&client, &project).await?;
              purge(&client, &root, purge_is_dry(dry_run, yes)).await?
          }
      };
      print!("{text}");
      Ok(())
  }

  /// `--dry-run` is the default until `-y`: the two flags conflict in the
  /// parser, and the absence of both means the safe one.
  fn purge_is_dry(dry_run: bool, yes: bool) -> bool {
      dry_run || !yes
  }

  /// A path made absolute against this shell's directory: the daemon refuses a
  /// relative one rather than read it against its own (R22).
  fn absolute(path: &str) -> Result<String> {
      let trimmed = path.trim();
      let absolute = std::path::absolute(trimmed)
          .with_context(|| format!("cannot make {trimmed:?} an absolute path"))?;
      Ok(absolute.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
  }

  fn workspace_query(path: &str) -> String {
      format!("/v1/workspaces?path={}", urlencoding::encode(path))
  }

  // ── list ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  async fn list(client: &DaemonClient) -> Result<String> {
      let projects: Vec<ProjectView> = client.get("/v1/workspaces").await?;
      Ok(render_list(&projects))
  }

  fn render_list(projects: &[ProjectView]) -> String {
      let mut out = String::new();
      if projects.is_empty() {
          let _ = writeln!(
              out,
              "{}",
              "No projects yet. A chat turn in a git repository, or `openalpaca chat --project \
               <dir>`, makes one."
                  .yellow()
          );
          return out;
      }
      for project in projects {
          let missing = match project.missing {
              true => format!(
                  "  {}",
                  "missing — its folder is gone: re-point it, or delete its data".yellow()
              ),
              false => String::new(),
          };
          let _ = writeln!(out, "{}{missing}", project.root.bold());
          let _ = writeln!(
              out,
              "  {}",
              format!("projects/{} · id {}", project.name, project.id).dimmed()
          );
      }
      out
  }

  // ── rebase ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  async fn rebase(client: &DaemonClient, old: &str, new: &str, dry_run: bool) -> Result<String> {
      if dry_run {
          let from: WorkspaceView = client.get(&workspace_query(old)).await?;
          let to: WorkspaceView = client.get(&workspace_query(new)).await?;
          return Ok(render_plan(&from, &to));
      }
      let result: RepointResult = client
          .patch(
              "/v1/workspaces",
              &RebaseRequest {
                  old_path: old,
                  new_path: new,
              },
          )
          .await?;
      let mut out = String::new();
      let _ = writeln!(
          out,
          "{} {} → {}",
          "Re-pointed".green().bold(),
          result.old_path.dimmed(),
          result.new_path
      );
      let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}", result.moved.describe());
      let _ = writeln!(out, "  its folder is now projects/{}", result.project.name);
      Ok(out)
  }

  fn flag(out: &mut String, text: String) {
      let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}", text.yellow());
  }

  /// The `--dry-run` body: what is recorded at the old path and what the
  /// re-point would refuse. It reports rather than refuses. The home-store and
  /// not-a-directory lines read this machine's filesystem — the daemon's, on the
  /// machine they share; the daemon is what decides.
  fn render_plan(from: &WorkspaceView, to: &WorkspaceView) -> String {
      let mut out = String::new();
      let source = from.root.as_deref().unwrap_or(&from.path);
      let _ = writeln!(out, "{} {} → {}", "Would re-point".bold(), source.dimmed(), to.path);
      let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}", from.rows.describe());
      if from.id.is_none() {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!("{source} is not a project OpenAlpaca knows; the re-point would be refused"),
          );
      }
      if overlaps_home_store(Path::new(&to.path)) {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!(
                  "{} is, contains or lies inside the OpenAlpaca home store; the re-point would \
                   be refused",
                  to.path
              ),
          );
      } else if !Path::new(&to.path).is_dir() {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!(
                  "{} is not a directory; the re-point would be refused — create it first",
                  to.path
              ),
          );
      }
      if to.root.as_deref() == Some(to.path.as_str()) && (to.id.is_some() || !to.rows.is_empty()) {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!(
                  "{} is already a project of its own, or OpenAlpaca's records already name it; \
                   the re-point would be refused — delete that project's data first, or re-point \
                   onto another path",
                  to.path
              ),
          );
      }
      if from.active_tasks > 0 {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!(
                  "{} run(s) there are still in flight; the re-point would be refused until they \
                   finish",
                  from.active_tasks
              ),
          );
      }
      if from.queued_tasks > 0 {
          flag(
              &mut out,
              format!(
                  "{} run(s) there are queued; the re-point takes their rows with it, but \
                   deleting that project's data would be refused until they finish",
                  from.queued_tasks
              ),
          );
      }
      if from.missing {
          let _ = writeln!(out, "  its folder is gone; re-pointing is what re-attaches its data");
      }
      if let Some(name) = &from.name {
          let _ = writeln!(out, "  its folder projects/{name} would be renamed for the new path");
      }
      out
  }

  // ── purge ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  /// What `purge` sends (the lead's R-S8): a delete takes a project exactly.
  /// `projects/<name>`, a folder as `store list` prints it, is looked up in
  /// the daemon's list and sent as that project's root; anything else is a
  /// path, made absolute against this shell's directory and sent as written —
  /// the daemon refuses one inside a project, naming the project's root
  /// (`422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT`), and one in no project (`404`). A folder of
  /// this shell's directory that is itself called `projects` is
  /// `./projects/…`.
  async fn purge_target(client: &DaemonClient, project: &str) -> Result<String> {
      let trimmed = project.trim();
      let Some(name) = trimmed.strip_prefix("projects/") else {
          return absolute(trimmed);
      };
      let name = name.trim_end_matches('/');
      let projects: Vec<ProjectView> = client.get("/v1/workspaces").await?;
      projects
          .into_iter()
          .find(|listed| listed.name == name)
          .map(|listed| listed.root)
          .with_context(|| {
              format!(
                  "no project's folder is projects/{name}: `openalpaca store list` names each \
                   project's root and folder"
              )
          })
  }

  async fn purge(client: &DaemonClient, project: &str, dry_run: bool) -> Result<String> {
      let result: DeleteResult = client
          .post(
              "/v1/workspaces/purge",
              &PurgeRequest {
                  path: project,
                  dry_run,
              },
          )
          .await?;
      Ok(render_delete(&result))
  }

  fn render_delete(result: &DeleteResult) -> String {
      let mut out = String::new();
      let heading = match result.applied {
          true => format!("{} {}", "Deleted the data of".green().bold(), result.project.root),
          false => format!("{} {}", "Would delete the data of".bold(), result.project.root),
      };
      let _ = writeln!(out, "{heading}");
      let _ = writeln!(
          out,
          "  {}",
          format!("projects/{} · id {}", result.project.name, result.project.id).dimmed()
      );
      out.push_str(&render_entries(&result.entries));
      // Present only on a real run: filled from what the daemon actually removed.
      if let Some(removed) = &result.removed {
          let _ = writeln!(out, "  {} {}", "deleted:".bold(), result.counts.describe());
          let folder = match removed.project_folder {
              true => format!("the folder projects/{}", result.project.name),
              false => format!(
                  "not the folder projects/{} (the daemon log says why)",
                  result.project.name
              ),
          };
          let _ = writeln!(
              out,
              "  {} {} session log directories, {} memory partitions, {folder}",
              "removed:".bold(),
              removed.session_dirs,
              removed.memory_partitions
          );
      }
      if result.kept.uploads + result.kept.artifacts > 0 {
          let _ = writeln!(
              out,
              "  {} {} uploads and {} by-products another conversation still uses, moved to the \
               root store",
              "kept:".bold(),
              result.kept.uploads,
              result.kept.artifacts
          );
      }
      if !result.applied {
          let _ = writeln!(out);
          let _ = writeln!(
              out,
              "{}",
              "Nothing was deleted. Re-run with -y to carry this out.".dimmed()
          );
      }
      out
  }
  ```

  then, unchanged from HEAD, `enum Verdict` with its `impl`, `fn paint_verdict`, `fn render_entries`, `fn render_entries_with` (their docs referring to `print_entries` now say "the plan's body"). `print_entries`, `print_plan`, `destination_ancestor` and the old `view`/queued-run tests are gone (`destination_ancestor`'s `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` no longer exists).   /// A project as `POST /v1/workspaces` answers it — the two fields this
  /// command prints and sends.
  #[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
  struct ChosenProject {
      root: String,
      name: String,
  }

  /// `chat --project <dir>` (R10): the daemon resolves the folder — the git
  /// repository it lies in, else the folder itself — and remembers it; every
  /// turn then carries the answered root, never the typed text.
  async fn choose_project(client: &DaemonClient, dir: &std::path::Path) -> Result<ChosenProject> {
      let path = std::path::absolute(dir)
          .with_context(|| format!("Cannot make {} an absolute path", dir.display()))?;
      client
          .post(
              "/v1/workspaces",
              &serde_json::json!({ "path": path.to_string_lossy() }),
          )
          .await
          .with_context(|| format!("Could not use {} as this chat's project", path.display()))
  }

### Spec conflicts

- **SC-1 — §5.2's route order hangs.** **Accepted (R-S14).** `interfaces.md` §5.2 orders, under `quiesce(&project.id)`, `forget_conversation_summaries(..)` "before the partitions go" with no root stated; today's purge passes the project root (`workspaces.rs:1095-1101`). `MemoryService::forget` takes `begin_write` on each target's partition slot (`service/mutations.rs:396-398`), and `begin_write` waits while the slot is `Held` (`service/write_slot.rs:56-66`, `:71-80`); after S4 every slot of the project is `proj:{id}`, the slot the delete holds. A summary in the project's own partition therefore blocks the route for ever. **Correction:** call it with `root: None` — the home partition only; the project's own summaries go whole with `MemoryService::remove_project` (S5a.9, with a test that fails instead of hanging). `remove_project` takes no slot (S5a.4).
- **SC-2 — the factory-reset preview is listed twice.** This slice's brief puts it in S5a; `interfaces.md` §0 (S6's row) puts "the factory-reset preview" in S6. **Followed the sheet:** S5a does not touch `commands/config_factory_reset.rs`; spec §8's preview line (`projects/` left in place, project ids surviving) is S6's.
- **SC-3 — `unknown_entries` goes whole, not its "project form".** **Accepted (R-S14).** `interfaces.md` §7.1 and spec §7 remove "`unknown_entries` for a project store". At HEAD its only non-test caller is the purge plan (`workspaces.rs:791`); the home form has no caller. **Correction:** S5a.8 deletes the function and its four tests (`store/tests.rs:409`, `:432`, `:462`, `:491`).

Copy-then-commit is what lets a failed transaction leave the project whole and take its copies back (one transaction stays true); the source goes with `projects/<name>/` in step 3.

A file linked by another conversation after the copies were made would lose its link with the project's rows; the transaction refuses instead (`a_file_linked_after_the_copies_were_made_refuses_the_transaction`).

## Stage 1 — slice S5b: the app's half of a project's life cycle

Draft for the Stage 1 plan. Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Spec: `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8)
§3, §6, §7, §9 *App*, §16 step (5); shared names: `interfaces.md` §6.3 and §7.1. Line numbers below are from that
HEAD; every edit is located by the text it replaces.

### What this slice does

Settings → Connection stops treating a project as a string kept in `localStorage` and starts treating it as what the
daemon records under `~/.openalpaca/projects/`. `Use` asks `POST /v1/workspaces`, which answers the git repository
the folder is in or, when there is none, registers the folder itself (R10); the window keeps the **root** it was
answered, and the Project card names the root `GET /v1/status` resolves the window's path to, never the typed text.
Under the card, a **Projects** list (`GET /v1/workspaces`) shows every project with a `missing` tag for one whose
folder is gone (ST-7) and two actions: `Re-point…` (counts from `GET /v1/workspaces?path=`, then `PATCH`) and
`Delete data…` (a dry run's plan first, then the delete — ST-19). The window follows its own project through both: to
the new root after a re-point, to no project after a delete. The moved-project offer (`useMovedProject`,
`MovedProjectOffer`, `rebaseWorkspace`) goes with the in-project store that let it detect a move, and the Memory view
stops naming `.git or .openalpaca`. `API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` are S6's (`interfaces.md` §0): the rows they
need are handed over in *Hand-off to S6*, after the last task, and S5b edits neither.

**Depends on:** S5a landed (the routes and wire shapes of `interfaces.md` §6.1) and S2 (`GET /v1/status.project_root`
comes from the new resolver). Every test here mocks the client or the hooks, so no gate needs a daemon, and S5b runs
**no cargo command**. It touches no Rust, no route and no migration; its only generated doc is
`docs/api/apps/openalpaca-gui.md`, which `scripts/gen_api_docs.py` builds from `apps/openalpaca-gui/src/lib/api/*.ts`.

### Rules every task follows

- Work only under `apps/openalpaca-gui/` and, for the generated doc, `docs/api/apps/openalpaca-gui.md`. Never read,
  list or touch `~/.openalpaca`; start no daemon, no CLI and no `bun run tauri dev`.
- Edits are anchored: the Edit tool with the exact old text shown. Never BSD `sed -i`.
- **The four GUI gates**, all four, in this order, after every task (CLAUDE.md: `bun run check` is not `bun run build`):

  ```bash
  cd /Users/tangyunpei/dev/OpenAlpaca/apps/openalpaca-gui
  bun run check          # expected: no output, exit 0
  bun run test           # expected: "Test Files  <n> passed (<n>)" and "Tests  <m> passed (<m>)", 0 failed
  bun run format:check   # expected: "All matched files use Prettier code style!"
  bun run build          # expected: tsc -b, then vite's "✓ built in …"; exit 0
  ```

  Before `format:check`, run `bunx prettier --write` on exactly the files the task touched (listed in its Step 5). The
  code below is written to Prettier's shape, but Prettier (with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`) owns line breaks and
  class order; it does not sort imports. (`.prettierignore` excludes only `dist`, `node_modules`, `src-tauri/target`,
  `src-tauri/gen`, `static`.)
- A task that changes the exports of `src/lib/api/workspaces.ts` (S5b.1, S5b.2) regenerates the doc in the same commit:
  `cd /Users/tangyunpei/dev/OpenAlpaca && python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py`, then `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py
  --check` → `API documentation is up to date.` The generator reads the endpoint from the **first** `METHOD /v1/…` in
  each exported function's JSDoc (`gui_first_endpoint`), so every wrapper's JSDoc starts with its endpoint in

```ts
/**
 * `/v1/workspaces` — the projects the daemon knows, and their life cycle
 * (storage design §6, §9; owner decisions ST-6, ST-7, ST-19, ST-20).
 *
 * A project is a folder under `<home>/projects/` whose `project.json` records
 * its permanent id and its root (ST-13). Only the daemon can resolve a path
 * to one — canonicalize it, walk up to a registered root or a git
 * repository — so this window never guesses: it asks, and keeps the root
 * the daemon answered.
 *
 * Nothing is written inside a project folder (ST-1), so nothing travels with
 * a moved folder: a project whose root is gone is `missing` (ST-7) until its
 * owner re-points it or deletes its data. Every refusal below is an
 * `ApiError` carrying the daemon's code and a sentence written for the
 * owner, which the caller shows as written.
 */

import { apiFetch } from "../http";

/** What is recorded under one root, by the five path columns (R14). */
export interface WorkspaceCounts {
  /** `file_assets` rows: uploads and by-products. */
  artifacts: number;
  sessions: number;
  tasks: number;
  /** `conversation_messages` rows. */
  messages: number;
  /** Queued `lane_followups`. */
  followups: number;
}

/** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=` — what one path is. */
export interface Workspace {
  /** The path asked about, canonicalized (as written when it is gone). */
  path: string;
  /** The project root it resolves to; `null` when it is in no project. */
  root: string | null;
  /** The project's id; `null` for a root nobody has used yet, or no project. */
  id: string | null;
  /** The project's folder under `projects/`; `null` as `id` is. */
  name: string | null;
  /** The root is not a directory (ST-7); `false` when `root` is `null`. */
  missing: boolean;
  /** What is recorded under `root`; zeros when `root` is `null`. */
  rows: WorkspaceCounts;
  /** Runs under `root` that are `running` or `paused`. */
  active_tasks: number;
  /** Runs under `root` waiting to start. */
  queued_tasks: number;
}

/** Every row a re-point rewrites, summed. */
export function totalRows(counts: WorkspaceCounts): number {
  return (
    counts.artifacts +
    counts.sessions +
    counts.tasks +
    counts.messages +
    counts.followups
  );
}

/** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=` — `400 INVALID_PATH` for a relative or empty path. */
export async function getWorkspace(
  path: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<Workspace> {
  return await apiFetch<Workspace>("/v1/workspaces", {
    signal,
    query: { path },
  });
}
```

Replace the whole of `apps/openalpaca-gui/src/hooks/useWorkspaces.ts` with:

```ts
/**
 * `GET /v1/workspaces?path=` as a query (storage design §9): what the daemon
 * resolves one path to — its project root, the project's id and folder when
 * it is registered, whether its folder is missing, and what is recorded
 * under it.
 */

import { useQuery, type UseQueryResult } from "@tanstack/react-query";

import { getWorkspace, type Workspace } from "@/lib/api/workspaces";
import { qk } from "@/lib/query-keys";

/** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=`. Disabled until there is a path to ask about. */
export function useWorkspace(
  path: string | null,
): UseQueryResult<Workspace | null> {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.workspaces.detail(path ?? ""),
    queryFn: ({ signal }) =>
      path === null ? null : getWorkspace(path, signal),
    enabled: path !== null,
    // What is recorded under a root changes only when work is filed there,
    // and a failed lookup should not retry against a path the owner mistyped.
    staleTime: 30_000,
    retry: false,
  });
}
```

export interface ProjectRepoint {
  old_path: string;
  new_path: string;
  /** What the one transaction rewrote. */
  moved: WorkspaceCounts;
  /** The project now: its new root and its folder's new name. */
  project: Project;

export interface DeletePlanEntry {
  entry: string;
  holds: string;
  retention: string;
  action: "delete" | "keep";

/** What the delete removes (the plan) or removed. */

  tool_calls: number;

  tasks: number;

  artifacts: number;

export interface ProjectDataDeletion {
  dry_run: boolean;
  applied: boolean;
  project: Project;
  entries: DeletePlanEntry[];
  counts: DeleteCounts;
  /** Files another conversation still links, moved to the root store (ST-19). */

  removed: {

    memory_partitions: number;

}

```ts
/** `GET /v1/workspaces` — every project the home store records, by folder name. */
export async function listProjects(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Project[]> {
  return await apiFetch<Project[]>("/v1/workspaces", { signal });
}

/** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=` — `400 INVALID_PATH` for a relative or empty path. */
export async function getWorkspace(
  path: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<Workspace> {
  return await apiFetch<Workspace>("/v1/workspaces", {
    signal,
    query: { path },
  });
}

/**
 * `POST /v1/workspaces` — `Use`: the project a folder is in, made one when it
 * is in none (R10). Inside a git repository the answer is the repository;
 * otherwise the folder itself is registered. Refusals: `WORKSPACE_IS_HOME`
 * (409), `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY` (422), `INVALID_PATH` (400),
 * `WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED` (500).
 */
export async function chooseProject(path: string): Promise<Project> {
  return await apiFetch<Project>("/v1/workspaces", {
    method: "POST",
    body: { path },
  });
}

/**
 * `PATCH /v1/workspaces` — re-point a project at the folder it is in now
 * (§6). Refusals: `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404); `WORKSPACE_BUSY`,
 * `WORKSPACE_EXISTS` and `WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` (409);
 * `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY` (422); `INVALID_PATH` (400).
 */
export async function repointProject(
  oldPath: string,
  newPath: string,
): Promise<ProjectRepoint> {
  return await apiFetch<ProjectRepoint>("/v1/workspaces", {
    method: "PATCH",
    body: { old_path: oldPath, new_path: newPath },
  });
}

/**
 * `POST /v1/workspaces/purge` — everything OpenAlpaca holds for a project
 * (ST-19). `dryRun` answers the plan and deletes nothing. The daemon defaults
 * to a dry run; the flag is sent either way, so a missing argument can never
 * be the deletion. Refusals: `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404), `WORKSPACE_BUSY`
 * (409), `INVALID_PATH` (400), and `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` (422) for a path
 * inside a project rather than its root — the app sends a listed project's
 * root, so it never meets that one.
 */
export async function deleteProjectData(
  path: string,
  dryRun: boolean,
): Promise<ProjectDataDeletion> {
  return await apiFetch<ProjectDataDeletion>("/v1/workspaces/purge", {
    method: "POST",
    body: { path, dry_run: dryRun },
  });
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * A project's life-cycle writes (storage design §6) and what each one makes
 * stale. A re-point re-addresses a project's conversations, runs, files and
 * notes under its new root, and a delete removes them, so the surfaces that
 * read them must re-ask; a dry run changes nothing and must not make them.
 *
 * The hooks run for real against a mocked client and a client holding one
 * answered entry per domain, and the test reads which entries the write
 * invalidated — the shape of `useSettings.test.tsx`.
 */

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { renderHook, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import {
  useChooseProject,
  useDeleteProjectData,
  useProjects,
  useRepointProject,
} from "@/hooks/useWorkspaces";
import type { Project } from "@/lib/api/workspaces";
import { qk } from "@/lib/query-keys";

const PROJECT = vi.hoisted<Project>(() => ({
  id: "0b5c1d2e-3f40-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d",
  root: "/Users/me/repo",
  name: "-Users-me-repo",
  missing: false,
}));

vi.mock("@/lib/api/workspaces", async (importOriginal) => ({
  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import("@/lib/api/workspaces")>()),
  listProjects: vi.fn(async () => [PROJECT]),
  chooseProject: vi.fn(async () => PROJECT),
  repointProject: vi.fn(async (oldPath: string, newPath: string) => ({
    old_path: oldPath,
    new_path: newPath,
    moved: { artifacts: 0, sessions: 1, tasks: 0, messages: 2, followups: 0 },
    project: { ...PROJECT, root: newPath },
  })),
  deleteProjectData: vi.fn(async (_path: string, dryRun: boolean) => ({
    dry_run: dryRun,
    applied: !dryRun,
    project: PROJECT,
    entries: [],
    counts: {
      sessions: 0,
      messages: 0,
      tool_calls: 0,
      followups: 0,
      tasks: 0,
      spans: 0,
      run_events: 0,
      uploads: 0,
      artifacts: 0,
      memory_notes: 0,
    },
    kept: { uploads: 0, artifacts: 0 },
    removed: dryRun
      ? null
      : { session_dirs: 0, memory_partitions: 0, project_folder: true },
  })),
}));

/** Every domain a life-cycle write may touch, plus one it must not. */
const PROJECTS = qk.workspaces.list();
const STATUS = qk.status("/Users/me/repo");
const CONTENT = [
  qk.artifacts.all(),
  qk.sessions.all(),
  qk.tasks.all(),
  qk.memory.all(),
] as const;
const UNTOUCHED = qk.followups.all();

/**
 * `staleTime: Infinity` so a cached entry is fresh, as the app's 30 s default
 * makes it: only `refetchOnMount: "always"` can then re-read the list.
 */
function seeded(): QueryClient {
  const client = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: { retry: false, gcTime: Infinity, staleTime: Infinity },
      mutations: { retry: false },
    },
  });
  for (const key of [PROJECTS, STATUS, ...CONTENT, UNTOUCHED]) {
    client.setQueryData(key, []);
  }
  return client;
}

function wrapper(client: QueryClient) {
  return function Wrapper({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
    return (
      <QueryClientProvider client={client}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>
    );
  };
}

function stale(client: QueryClient, key: readonly unknown[]): boolean {
  return client.getQueryState(key)?.isInvalidated === true;
}

describe("useProjects", () => {
  it("re-reads the list on mount even when one is cached, since no event names a new project", async () => {
    const client = seeded();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useProjects(), {
      wrapper: wrapper(client),
    });

    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.data).toEqual([PROJECT]));
  });
});

describe("what each life-cycle write makes stale", () => {
  it("Use refreshes the project list and every window's status, and no content", async () => {
    const client = seeded();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useChooseProject(), {
      wrapper: wrapper(client),
    });

    result.current.mutate("/Users/me/repo/src");

    await waitFor(() => expect(stale(client, PROJECTS)).toBe(true));
    expect(stale(client, STATUS)).toBe(true);
    for (const key of CONTENT) expect(stale(client, key)).toBe(false);
    expect(stale(client, UNTOUCHED)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("a re-point refreshes everything the project's root addresses", async () => {
    const client = seeded();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useRepointProject(), {
      wrapper: wrapper(client),
    });

    result.current.mutate({ from: "/Users/me/repo", to: "/Users/me/work/repo" });

    await waitFor(() => expect(stale(client, PROJECTS)).toBe(true));
    expect(stale(client, STATUS)).toBe(true);
    for (const key of CONTENT) expect(stale(client, key)).toBe(true);
    expect(stale(client, UNTOUCHED)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("a dry run deletes nothing, so it refreshes nothing", async () => {
    const client = seeded();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useDeleteProjectData(), {
      wrapper: wrapper(client),
    });

    result.current.mutate({ path: "/Users/me/repo", dryRun: true });

    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.isSuccess).toBe(true));
    for (const key of [PROJECTS, STATUS, ...CONTENT, UNTOUCHED]) {
      expect(stale(client, key)).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  it("a delete refreshes everything that named the project", async () => {
    const client = seeded();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useDeleteProjectData(), {
      wrapper: wrapper(client),
    });

    result.current.mutate({ path: "/Users/me/repo", dryRun: false });

    await waitFor(() => expect(stale(client, PROJECTS)).toBe(true));
    expect(stale(client, STATUS)).toBe(true);
    for (const key of CONTENT) expect(stale(client, key)).toBe(true);
    expect(stale(client, UNTOUCHED)).toBe(false);
  });

Replace the whole of `src/hooks/useWorkspaces.ts` with:

```ts
/**
 * The projects the daemon knows, and their life cycle (storage design §6,
 * §9): one read per question, and three writes, each taken only on the
 * owner's say-so in Settings → Connection.
 *
 * Every write changes what other surfaces answer: a project's root is the
 * address of its conversations, runs, files and notes (R14), and
 * `GET /v1/status.project_root` — what the Memory view's `This project` and
 * the conversation sidebar read — is the daemon's resolution of a window's
 * path, which `Use` and a delete can flip for a folder with no git. So each
 * write invalidates those domains as well as its own; a dry run is a read
 * and invalidates nothing.
 */

import {
  useMutation,
  useQuery,
  useQueryClient,
  type QueryClient,
  type UseMutationResult,
  type UseQueryResult,
} from "@tanstack/react-query";

import {
  chooseProject,
  deleteProjectData,
  getWorkspace,
  listProjects,
  repointProject,
  type Project,
  type ProjectDataDeletion,
  type ProjectRepoint,
  type Workspace,
} from "@/lib/api/workspaces";
import { qk } from "@/lib/query-keys";

/**
 * `GET /v1/workspaces`. Re-read on every mount: no event announces a project
 * a chat turn or an upload registered, and the list changes too rarely to
 * poll.
 */
export function useProjects(): UseQueryResult<Project[]> {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.workspaces.list(),
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => listProjects(signal),
    refetchOnMount: "always",
  });
}

/** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=`. Disabled until there is a path to ask about. */
export function useWorkspace(
  path: string | null,
): UseQueryResult<Workspace | null> {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.workspaces.detail(path ?? ""),
    queryFn: ({ signal }) =>
      path === null ? null : getWorkspace(path, signal),
    enabled: path !== null,
    // What is recorded under a root changes only when work is filed there,
    // and a failed lookup should not retry against a path the owner mistyped.
    staleTime: 30_000,
    retry: false,
  });
}

/** What a re-point re-addresses and a delete removes. */
function invalidateProjectData(client: QueryClient): void {
  for (const key of [
    qk.workspaces.all(),
    qk.artifacts.all(),
    qk.sessions.all(),
    qk.tasks.all(),
    qk.memory.all(),
    qk.statusAll(),
  ]) {
    void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: key });
  }
}

/** `POST /v1/workspaces` — `Use`. */
export function useChooseProject(): UseMutationResult<Project, Error, string> {
  const client = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (path: string) => chooseProject(path),
    onSuccess: () => {
      for (const key of [qk.workspaces.all(), qk.statusAll()]) {
        void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: key });
      }
    },
  });
}

/** `PATCH /v1/workspaces` — `Re-point…`, on the owner's press. */
export function useRepointProject(): UseMutationResult<
  ProjectRepoint,
  Error,
  { from: string; to: string }
> {
  const client = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ from, to }: { from: string; to: string }) =>
      repointProject(from, to),
    onSuccess: () => invalidateProjectData(client),
  });
}

/** `POST /v1/workspaces/purge` — the plan (`dryRun`), then `Delete data`. */
export function useDeleteProjectData(): UseMutationResult<
  ProjectDataDeletion,
  Error,
  { path: string; dryRun: boolean }
> {
  const client = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ path, dryRun }: { path: string; dryRun: boolean }) =>
      deleteProjectData(path, dryRun),
    onSuccess: (_answer, { dryRun }) => {
      if (!dryRun) invalidateProjectData(client);
    },
  });
}
```

3. Replace the doc comment that begins `/**\n * The chosen project — one absolute path, kept on this machine.` and the
   whole `function ProjectCard(…) { … }` with:

```tsx
/**
 * What the Project card names (storage design §9: the resolved root, not the
 * typed text): the root `GET /v1/status` resolved the window's path to; the
 * stored path while the daemon has not answered; and the stored path,
 * flagged, when the daemon answered that it is in no project — a value an
 * earlier build kept as typed, such as a folder an `.openalpaca` directory
 * used to mark.
 */
export function projectCardRoot(
  path: string | null,
  resolved: string | null | undefined,
): { text: string; unresolved: boolean } {
  if (path === null) return { text: "none", unresolved: false };
  if (typeof resolved === "string") {
    return { text: resolved, unresolved: false };
  }
  return { text: path, unresolved: resolved === null };
}

/**
 * The window's project (storage design §3, §9).
 *
 * `Use` asks the daemon what the typed folder is — `POST /v1/workspaces`:
 * the git repository it is in, or, when there is none, the folder itself,
 * which becomes a project (R10) — and keeps the root it answered, never the
 * text typed. A refusal (`WORKSPACE_IS_HOME`, `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY`,
 * `INVALID_PATH`, `WORKSPACE_REGISTER_FAILED`) is the daemon's sentence,
 * shown as written, and the project the window had stays.
 *
 * Where a run's files go is said plainly: with no project, the home store;
 * with one, its folder under `projects/` in the home store — never the
 * project folder itself (ST-1). The home store is named from
 * `GET /v1/status`'s `home_root`, never from the literal `~/.openalpaca`
 * (G7): `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` moves the root, and a path printed from this
 * side would then be a confident lie. A daemon that has not answered yet is
 * "the home store".
 */
function ProjectCard({
  homeRoot,
  resolvedRoot,
}: {
  homeRoot: string | null;
  /** `GET /v1/status.project_root`; `undefined` until the daemon answered. */
  resolvedRoot: string | null | undefined;
}) {
  const path = useProjectStore((s) => s.path);
  const setPath = useProjectStore((s) => s.setPath);
  const showToast = useUiStore((s) => s.showToast);
  const choose = useChooseProject();
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(path ?? "");
  const [refusal, setRefusal] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const trimmed = draft.trim();
  // Only a genuine typo is an error: an empty box is "no project", not a
  // mistake, and Use is simply inert there.
  const invalid = trimmed !== "" && !isAbsolutePath(trimmed);
  const shown = projectCardRoot(path, resolvedRoot);

  function applyPath() {
    if (trimmed === "" || invalid || choose.isPending) return;
    setRefusal(null);
    choose.mutate(trimmed, {
      onSuccess: (project) => {
        setPath(project.root);
        setDraft(project.root);
        showToast(`Project set to ${project.root} — new runs will use it`);
      },
      onError: (error) => setRefusal(error.message),
    });
  }

  return (
    <Card>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-[10px]">
        <span className="text-md-plus font-semibold text-ink">Project</span>
        <span className="ml-auto font-mono text-xs-plus text-muted-fg">
          {shown.text}
        </span>
      </div>

      <div className="mt-[16px]">
        <Eyebrow tracking="narrow" tone="faint" className="mb-[4px]">
          workspace path
        </Eyebrow>
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-[6px]">
          <input
            aria-label="Project path"
            placeholder="/Users/you/code/your-project"
            value={draft}
            onChange={(event) => {
              setDraft(event.target.value);
              setRefusal(null);
            }}
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (event.key === "Enter") applyPath();
            }}
            className="min-w-[280px] flex-1 rounded-md border border-line bg-raised px-[8px] py-[4px] font-mono text-2xs-plus text-ink"
          />
          <Button
            variant="primarySm"
            disabled={trimmed === "" || invalid || choose.isPending}
            onClick={applyPath}
          >
            {choose.isPending ? "Using…" : "Use"}
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="ghostSm"
            disabled={path === null && trimmed === ""}
            onClick={() => {
              setDraft("");
              setRefusal(null);
              setPath(null);
              showToast("Project cleared");
            }}
          >
            Clear
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {refusal !== null && (
        <p className="mt-[6px] mb-0 text-base leading-[1.6] text-red-ink">
          {refusal}
        </p>
      )}

      {shown.unresolved && (
        <GapNote>
          {`${path} is in no project: no git repository holds it and it was not chosen with Use. Press Use to make it one.`}
        </GapNote>
      )}

      <GapNote>
        {invalid
          ? "An absolute path, please — a relative one would be read against the daemon's own directory, not this one."
          : path === null || shown.unresolved
            ? `No project: runs are recorded without one and their files go to ${homeStoreLabel(homeRoot)}.`
            : `Runs started here record this project. What they produce is kept under projects/ in ${homeStoreLabel(homeRoot)}; nothing is written into the project folder.`}
      </GapNote>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

(The unresolved note is one template string so it is one text node and the test's `^` anchor holds. A stored path
the daemon resolved to no project files its turns with none, so the last note says so rather than promising a folder
under `projects/`.)

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** Create `apps/openalpaca-gui/src/views/settings/ProjectsCard.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * Settings → Connection → Projects (storage design §6, §9; ST-7).
 *
 * Every project the home store records — one folder under `projects/` each,
 * whose `project.json` holds its id and its root (ST-13) — as
 * `GET /v1/workspaces` lists it, by folder name. A project whose root is no
 * longer a directory is marked `missing` and keeps everything recorded for
 * it (ST-7): nothing detects a move, and nothing is dropped on its own.
 *
 * The list is re-read whenever it mounts and after each write made here: no
 * event announces a project that a chat turn or an upload registered, and
 * polling a list that changes this rarely would only cost the daemon.
 */

import { Tag } from "@/components/ui";
import { useProjects } from "@/hooks/useWorkspaces";
import type { Project } from "@/lib/api/workspaces";

import { ListCard, ListRow, ListState } from "./primitives";

/** What the card says when the home store records no project yet. */
export const PROJECTS_EMPTY_COPY =
  "No projects yet. A folder becomes one when you Use it above, or the first time you chat from inside a git repository.";

/** What a missing project's row says under its root (ST-7). */
export const MISSING_PROJECT_COPY =
  "Its folder is gone. Everything recorded for it is kept until you re-point it or delete its data.";

export interface ProjectsCardProps {
  /** `GET /v1/status.project_root` — the project this window's turns go to. */
  currentRoot: string | null;
}

export function ProjectsCard({ currentRoot }: ProjectsCardProps) {
  const projects = useProjects();
  const rows = projects.data ?? [];

  return (
    <section aria-label="Projects" className="flex flex-col gap-[8px]">
      <h3 className="m-0 text-md-plus font-semibold text-ink">Projects</h3>
      <ListCard>
        <ListState
          pending={projects.isPending}
          error={projects.error}
          empty={rows.length === 0}
          emptyCopy={PROJECTS_EMPTY_COPY}
        >
          {rows.map((project) => (
            <ProjectRow
              key={project.id}
              project={project}
              current={project.root === currentRoot}
            />
          ))}
        </ListState>
      </ListCard>
    </section>
  );
}

function ProjectRow({
  project,
  current,
}: {
  project: Project;
  current: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <ListRow
      name={<span className="font-mono">{project.root}</span>}
      wrapName
      tags={
        <>
          {project.missing && <Tag value="missing" tone="warn" />}
          {current && <Tag value="this window" tone="live" />}
        </>
      }
      description={project.missing ? MISSING_PROJECT_COPY : undefined}
      meta={project.name}
      wrapMeta
    />
  );
}
```

      `Re-pointed to ${MOVED.root}: 2 conversations · 40 messages · 3 runs · 4 files.`,
    );
    // The list is re-read after the write.
    await waitFor(() => expect(api.list).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2));
  });

  it("leaves a window on another project where it is", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    useProjectStore.setState({ path: "/Users/me/other" });
    api.list.mockResolvedValue([REPO]);
    api.get.mockResolvedValue(recorded());
    api.repoint.mockResolvedValue({
      old_path: REPO.root,
      new_path: MOVED.root,
      moved: recorded().rows,
      project: MOVED,
    });
    renderCard("/Users/me/other");

    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Re-point…" }));
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog");
    await within(dialog).findByText(/^Recorded there:/);
    await user.type(within(dialog).getByLabelText("New project folder"), MOVED.root);
    await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Re-point" }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull());
    expect(useProjectStore.getState().path).toBe("/Users/me/other");
  });

  it("keeps the dialog open on the daemon's refusal and shows its sentence", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const sentence =
      "/Users/me/work/repo is already a project of its own, or OpenAlpaca's records already name it. Re-pointing onto it would merge two projects: delete that project's data first, or re-point onto another path";
    useProjectStore.setState({ path: REPO.root });
    api.list.mockResolvedValue([REPO]);
    api.get.mockResolvedValue(recorded());
    api.repoint.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(sentence, 409, "WORKSPACE_EXISTS"));
    renderCard(REPO.root);

    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Re-point…" }));
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog");
    await within(dialog).findByText(/^Recorded there:/);
    await user.type(within(dialog).getByLabelText("New project folder"), MOVED.root);
    await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Re-point" }));

    expect(await within(dialog).findByText(sentence)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("dialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(useProjectStore.getState().path).toBe(REPO.root);
  });

  it("fills the folder from the native picker", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    picker.pick.mockResolvedValue(MOVED.root);
    api.list.mockResolvedValue([REPO]);
    api.get.mockResolvedValue(recorded());
    renderCard();

    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Re-point…" }));
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog");
    await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Choose…" }));

    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(within(dialog).getByLabelText("New project folder")).toHaveValue(
        MOVED.root,
      ),
    );
  });
});

Create `src/components/overlays/RepointProjectDialog.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `RepointProjectDialog` — `Re-point…` on a project in Settings →
 * Connection → Projects (storage design §6 *Re-point*, ST-7, ST-20).
 *
 * A project is addressed by its root in five columns (R14), so a folder
 * moved or renamed outside OpenAlpaca strands its conversations, runs, files
 * and queued follow-ups at the old path; its notes are keyed by the
 * project's id and follow it with no rewrite. The daemon re-points all of it
 * in one transaction, but only the owner knows where the folder went — so
 * this asks, and shows what is recorded at the old root first.
 *
 * Built on `StopDaemonDialog`'s shell: the palette's veil and dialog, Escape
 * cancels. The confirm is `primarySm`, not the danger ghost — a re-point
 * deletes nothing and is undone by re-pointing back — and the folder field
 * takes the focus. `Re-point` stays off until the count on screen has been
 * read, while a run under the root is in flight (the daemon answers
 * `409 WORKSPACE_BUSY` and changes nothing), and for a path the daemon would
 * read against its own directory or that is where the project already is.
 * Every other refusal — `WORKSPACE_EXISTS` above all (ST-20: re-pointing onto
 * another project would merge two) — is the daemon's sentence, shown as
 * written, and the dialog stays open on it.
 */

import { Button, Scrim } from "@/components/ui";
import type { Project, WorkspaceCounts } from "@/lib/api/workspaces";
import {
  isAbsolutePath,
  normalizeProjectPath,
  RELATIVE_PATH_COPY,
} from "@/stores/project";

import { counted } from "./StopDaemonDialog";

/** What is recorded under a root, in the owner's words — non-zero counts only. */
export function rowsLine(rows: WorkspaceCounts): string {
  const parts = [
    rows.sessions > 0
      ? counted(rows.sessions, "conversation", "conversations")
      : null,
    rows.messages > 0 ? counted(rows.messages, "message", "messages") : null,
    rows.tasks > 0 ? counted(rows.tasks, "run", "runs") : null,
    rows.artifacts > 0 ? counted(rows.artifacts, "file", "files") : null,
    rows.followups > 0
      ? counted(rows.followups, "queued follow-up", "queued follow-ups")
      : null,
  ].filter((part): part is string => part !== null);
  return parts.length === 0 ? "nothing yet" : parts.join(" · ");
}

/** The folder a re-point would send, or `null` while the press must stay off. */
export function repointTarget(value: string, project: Project): string | null {
  const target = normalizeProjectPath(value);
  if (target === null || target === project.root) return null;
  return target;
}

export interface RepointProjectDialogProps {
  project: Project;
  /** `GET /v1/workspaces?path=<root>`'s counts; `undefined` until read. */
  rows: WorkspaceCounts | undefined;
  /** Runs under the root that are running or paused. */
  activeTasks: number;
  /** The fresh read of the counts is still out. */
  reading: boolean;
  /** Why the counts could not be read, or `null`. */
  readError: string | null;
  /** The new folder, as typed or picked. */
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  /** Open the native folder picker. */
  onBrowse: () => void;
  /** The daemon's refusal of the last press, as written, or `null`. */
  refusal: string | null;
  /** The re-point is in flight. */
  repointing: boolean;
  onCancel: () => void;
  onConfirm: () => void;
}

export function RepointProjectDialog({
  project,
  rows,
  activeTasks,
  reading,
  readError,
  value,
  onChange,
  onBrowse,
  refusal,
  repointing,
  onCancel,
  onConfirm,
}: RepointProjectDialogProps) {
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  const relative = trimmed !== "" && !isAbsolutePath(trimmed);
  const target = repointTarget(value, project);
  const busy = activeTasks > 0;
  const canConfirm = !reading && !busy && !repointing && target !== null;
  const countLine = reading
    ? "Counting what is recorded there…"
    : readError !== null
      ? `Could not count what is recorded there: ${readError}`
      : rows === undefined
        ? null
        : `Recorded there: ${rowsLine(rows)}.`;
  const paragraph = "m-0 mt-[10px] text-base leading-[1.6] text-secondary";

  return (
    <Scrim
      variant="veil"
      zIndex={50}
      closeOnSelfOnly
      className="fixed"
      onClose={onCancel}
    >
      <div
        role="dialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        aria-labelledby="repoint-project-title"
        onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === "Escape") {
            event.stopPropagation();
            onCancel();
          }
        }}
        className="w-[520px] max-w-[calc(100%-32px)] rounded-4xl border border-line-popover bg-raised px-[20px] py-[18px] shadow-dialog"
      >
        <h2
          id="repoint-project-title"
          className="m-0 text-md-plus font-semibold text-ink"
        >
          Re-point this project
        </h2>

        <p className={paragraph}>
          {project.missing ? "Its folder is gone from " : "It is recorded at "}
          <span className="font-mono text-2xs-plus text-ink">
            {project.root}
          </span>
          . Name the folder it is in now: its conversations, runs, files and
          notes follow it there. Nothing in either folder is touched.
        </p>

        {countLine !== null && (
          <p
            data-testid="repoint-counts"
            className="m-0 mt-[12px] font-mono text-2xs-plus leading-[1.6] text-ink"
          >
            {countLine}
          </p>
        )}

        {busy && (
          <p className={paragraph}>
            {`${counted(activeTasks, "run there is", "runs there are")} still in flight — a re-point is refused while one is; retry once it finishes.`}
          </p>
        )}

        <div className="mt-[14px] flex flex-wrap items-center gap-[6px]">
          <input
            autoFocus
            aria-label="New project folder"
            placeholder="/Users/you/code/the-project"
            value={value}
            onChange={(event) => onChange(event.target.value)}
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (event.key === "Enter" && canConfirm) onConfirm();
            }}
            className="min-w-[280px] flex-1 rounded-md border border-line bg-raised px-[8px] py-[4px] font-mono text-2xs-plus text-ink"
          />
          <Button variant="ghostSm" onClick={onBrowse}>
            Choose…
          </Button>
        </div>

        {relative && <p className={paragraph}>{RELATIVE_PATH_COPY}</p>}

        {refusal !== null && (
          <p className="m-0 mt-[10px] text-base leading-[1.6] text-red-ink">
            {refusal}
          </p>
        )}

        <div className="mt-[16px] flex justify-end gap-[6px]">
          <Button variant="secondarySm" onClick={onCancel}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="primarySm"
            disabled={!canConfirm}
            onClick={onConfirm}
          >
            {repointing ? "Re-pointing…" : "Re-point"}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </Scrim>
  );
}
```

In `src/components/overlays/index.ts`, after `export * from "./StopDaemonDialog";` add
