Replace the whole of `src/views/settings/ProjectsCard.tsx` with:

```tsx
/**
 * Settings → Connection → Projects (storage design §6, §9; ST-7, ST-20).
 *
 * Every project the home store records — one folder under `projects/` each,
 * whose `project.json` holds its id and its root (ST-13) — as
 * `GET /v1/workspaces` lists it, by folder name. A project whose root is no
 * longer a directory is marked `missing` and keeps everything recorded for
 * it (ST-7): nothing detects a move, and nothing is dropped on its own.
 * `Re-point…` is how the owner says where a moved folder went.
 *
 * The list is re-read whenever it mounts and after each write made here: no
 * event announces a project that a chat turn or an upload registered, and
 * polling a list that changes this rarely would only cost the daemon.
 *
 * A window follows its own project: after a re-point the old root is no
 * longer registered, so a window still sending it would file its next turn
 * under no project. It takes the new root.
 */

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

import {
  RepointProjectDialog,
  repointTarget,
  rowsLine,
} from "@/components/overlays/RepointProjectDialog";
import { Button, Tag } from "@/components/ui";
import {
  useProjects,
  useRepointProject,
  useWorkspace,
} from "@/hooks/useWorkspaces";
import type { Project } from "@/lib/api/workspaces";
import { useProjectStore } from "@/stores/project";
import { useUiStore } from "@/stores/ui";

import { pickDirectory } from "./AddExtensionForm";
import { ListCard, ListRow, ListState } from "./primitives";

/** What the card says when the home store records no project yet. */
export const PROJECTS_EMPTY_COPY =
  "No projects yet. A folder becomes one when you Use it above, or the first time you chat from inside a git repository.";

/** What a missing project's row says under its root (ST-7). */
export const MISSING_PROJECT_COPY =
  "Its folder is gone. Everything recorded for it is kept until you re-point it or delete its data.";

export interface ProjectsCardProps {
  /** `GET /v1/status.project_root` — the project this window's turns go to. */
  currentRoot: string | null;
}

type OpenAction = { kind: "repoint"; project: Project } | null;

export function ProjectsCard({ currentRoot }: ProjectsCardProps) {
  const projects = useProjects();
  const rows = projects.data ?? [];
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<OpenAction>(null);

  return (
    <section aria-label="Projects" className="flex flex-col gap-[8px]">
      <h3 className="m-0 text-md-plus font-semibold text-ink">Projects</h3>
      <ListCard>
        <ListState
          pending={projects.isPending}
          error={projects.error}
          empty={rows.length === 0}
          emptyCopy={PROJECTS_EMPTY_COPY}
        >
          {rows.map((project) => (
            <ProjectRow
              key={project.id}
              project={project}
              current={project.root === currentRoot}
              onRepoint={() => setOpen({ kind: "repoint", project })}
            />
          ))}
        </ListState>
      </ListCard>

      {open?.kind === "repoint" && (
        <RepointFlow
          project={open.project}
          current={open.project.root === currentRoot}
          onClose={() => setOpen(null)}
        />
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

function ProjectRow({
  project,
  current,
  onRepoint,
}: {
  project: Project;
  current: boolean;
  onRepoint: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <ListRow
      name={<span className="font-mono">{project.root}</span>}
      wrapName
      tags={
        <>
          {project.missing && <Tag value="missing" tone="warn" />}
          {current && <Tag value="this window" tone="live" />}
        </>
      }
      description={project.missing ? MISSING_PROJECT_COPY : undefined}
      meta={project.name}
      wrapMeta
      control={
        <span className="flex shrink-0 gap-[6px]">
          <Button variant="ghostSm" onClick={onRepoint}>
            Re-point…
          </Button>
        </span>
      }
    />
  );
}

interface FlowProps {
  project: Project;
  /** This window's turns go to `project` (`GET /v1/status.project_root`). */
  current: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
}

/**
 * The re-point, mounted only while its dialog is open. The counts are read
 * fresh on open, as `StopDaemonFlow` re-reads `busy`: the count confirmed is
 * the one on screen, not a cached one.
 */
function RepointFlow({ project, current, onClose }: FlowProps) {
  const counts = useWorkspace(project.root);
  const repoint = useRepointProject();
  const windowPath = useProjectStore((s) => s.path);
  const setPath = useProjectStore((s) => s.setPath);
  const showToast = useUiStore((s) => s.showToast);
  const [value, setValue] = useState("");
  const [refusal, setRefusal] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [reading, setReading] = useState(true);

  const refetch = useRef(counts.refetch);
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    void Promise.resolve(refetch.current()).finally(() => {
      if (live) setReading(false);
    });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);

  function confirm() {
    const target = repointTarget(value, project);
    if (target === null) return;
    setRefusal(null);
    repoint.mutate(
      { from: project.root, to: target },
      {
        onSuccess: (result) => {
          if (current || windowPath === project.root) {
            setPath(result.project.root);
          }
          showToast(
            `Re-pointed to ${result.project.root}: ${rowsLine(result.moved)}.`,
          );
          onClose();
        },
        onError: (error) => setRefusal(error.message),
      },
    );
  }

  return (
    <RepointProjectDialog
      project={project}
      rows={counts.data?.rows}
      activeTasks={counts.data?.active_tasks ?? 0}
      reading={reading}
      readError={counts.error?.message ?? null}
      value={value}
      onChange={(next) => {
        setValue(next);
        setRefusal(null);
      }}
      onBrowse={() => {
        void pickDirectory().then((picked) => {
          if (picked === null) return;
          setValue(picked);
          setRefusal(null);
        });
      }}
      refusal={refusal}
      repointing={repoint.isPending}
      onCancel={onClose}
      onConfirm={confirm}
    />
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.**

Create `src/components/overlays/DeleteProjectDataDialog.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `DeleteProjectDataDialog` — `Delete data…` on a project in Settings →
 * Connection → Projects (storage design §6 *Delete its data*, ST-19).
 *
 * ST-19: everything OpenAlpaca holds for the project goes — conversations,
 * runs, by-products, uploads, the notes of every owner, and its folder under
 * `projects/` — and the project's own folder is never touched; a file
 * another conversation still uses is kept (a by-product as its newest
 * version only). Nothing is deleted before the plan is on screen: the flow
 * asks the daemon for a dry run on open and this draws it as served — its
 * counts, what it keeps, its entries — and `Delete data` stays off until
 * that plan has arrived.
 *
 * The gate is the plan plus the existing danger ghost, never the default
 * focus (`Cancel` is, and Escape cancels), like `StopDaemonDialog`; no word
 * is typed. A refusal — `WORKSPACE_BUSY` while a run is in flight — is the
 * daemon's sentence, and the dialog stays open on it.
 */

import { Button, Scrim, Tag } from "@/components/ui";
import type {
  DeleteCounts,
  Project,
  ProjectDataDeletion,
} from "@/lib/api/workspaces";

import { counted } from "./StopDaemonDialog";

const COUNT_WORDS: ReadonlyArray<
  readonly [keyof DeleteCounts, string, string]
> = [
  ["sessions", "conversation", "conversations"],
  ["messages", "message", "messages"],
  ["tasks", "run", "runs"],
  ["spans", "subagent record", "subagent records"],
  ["run_events", "run event", "run events"],
  ["tool_calls", "tool call", "tool calls"],
  ["followups", "queued follow-up", "queued follow-ups"],
  ["uploads", "upload", "uploads"],
  ["artifacts", "by-product", "by-products"],
  ["memory_notes", "memory note", "memory notes"],
];

/** The plan's counts in the owner's words — non-zero ones only. */
export function deleteCountsLine(counts: DeleteCounts): string {
  const parts = COUNT_WORDS.filter(([key]) => counts[key] > 0).map(
    ([key, one, many]) => counted(counts[key], one, many),
  );
  return parts.length === 0
    ? "Nothing is recorded for this project but its folder under projects/."
    : `Deletes ${parts.join(" · ")}.`;
}

/** What the delete keeps because another conversation still uses it, or `null`. */
export function keptLine(kept: ProjectDataDeletion["kept"]): string | null {
  const parts = [
    kept.uploads > 0 ? counted(kept.uploads, "upload", "uploads") : null,
    kept.artifacts > 0
      ? counted(kept.artifacts, "by-product", "by-products")
      : null,
  ].filter((part): part is string => part !== null);
  return parts.length === 0
    ? null
    : `Keeps ${parts.join(" and ")} another conversation still uses, moved out of the project — a by-product as its newest version only.`;
}

export interface DeleteProjectDataDialogProps {
  project: Project;
  /** The dry run's answer; `undefined` while it is out or after it failed. */
  plan: ProjectDataDeletion | undefined;
  /** Why the dry run failed, as the daemon wrote it, or `null`. */
  planError: string | null;
  /** The delete's refusal, as the daemon wrote it, or `null`. */
  refusal: string | null;
  /** The delete is in flight. */
  deleting: boolean;
  onCancel: () => void;
  onConfirm: () => void;
}

export function DeleteProjectDataDialog({
  project,
  plan,
  planError,
  refusal,
  deleting,
  onCancel,
  onConfirm,
}: DeleteProjectDataDialogProps) {
  const paragraph = "m-0 mt-[10px] text-base leading-[1.6] text-secondary";
  const mono = "m-0 mt-[12px] font-mono text-2xs-plus leading-[1.6] text-ink";
  const kept = plan === undefined ? null : keptLine(plan.kept);

  return (
    <Scrim
      variant="veil"
      zIndex={50}
      closeOnSelfOnly
      className="fixed"
      onClose={onCancel}
    >
      <div
        role="dialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        aria-labelledby="delete-project-title"
        onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === "Escape") {
            event.stopPropagation();
            onCancel();
          }
        }}
        className="w-[560px] max-w-[calc(100%-32px)] rounded-4xl border border-line-popover bg-raised px-[20px] py-[18px] shadow-dialog"
      >
        <h2
          id="delete-project-title"
          className="m-0 text-md-plus font-semibold text-ink"
        >
          Delete this project&rsquo;s data?
        </h2>

        <p className={paragraph}>
          Everything OpenAlpaca holds for{" "}
          <span className="font-mono text-2xs-plus text-ink">
            {project.root}
          </span>{" "}
          is deleted: its conversations, runs, by-products, uploads, the memory
          notes of every owner, and its folder under projects/ in the home
          store.
        </p>
        <p className={paragraph}>
          The project&rsquo;s own folder is never touched. This cannot be
          undone.
        </p>

        {plan === undefined && planError === null && (
          <p data-testid="delete-plan" className={mono}>
            Reading what would be deleted…
          </p>
        )}
        {planError !== null && (
          <p className="m-0 mt-[12px] text-base leading-[1.6] text-red-ink">
            {`Could not read what would be deleted: ${planError}`}
          </p>
        )}
        {plan !== undefined && (
          <>
            <p data-testid="delete-plan" className={mono}>
              {deleteCountsLine(plan.counts)}
            </p>
            {kept !== null && <p className={paragraph}>{kept}</p>}
            {plan.entries.length > 0 && (
              <ul
                aria-label="What the delete does"
                className="m-0 mt-[10px] flex list-none flex-col gap-[4px] p-0"
              >
                {plan.entries.map((entry) => (
                  <li
                    key={`${entry.action}:${entry.entry}`}
                    className="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-[8px] text-base leading-[1.5] text-secondary"
                  >
                    <Tag
                      value={entry.action}
                      tone={entry.action === "delete" ? "warn" : "neutral"}
                    />
                    <span className="font-mono text-2xs-plus text-ink">
                      {entry.entry}
                    </span>
                    <span>{entry.holds}</span>
                    <span className="font-mono text-2xs-plus text-faint">
                      {entry.retention}
                    </span>
                  </li>
                ))}
              </ul>
            )}
          </>
        )}

        {refusal !== null && (
          <p className="m-0 mt-[10px] text-base leading-[1.6] text-red-ink">
            {refusal}
          </p>
        )}

        <div className="mt-[16px] flex justify-end gap-[6px]">
          {/* Cancel is the default focus, never Delete: Enter or Space on an
              opened dialog must not be what deletes a project's data. */}
          <Button autoFocus variant="secondarySm" onClick={onCancel}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="dangerGhost"
            disabled={plan === undefined || deleting}
            onClick={onConfirm}
          >
            {deleting ? "Deleting…" : "Delete data"}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </Scrim>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * The delete, mounted only while its dialog is open: one dry run on open
 * for the plan, and the delete itself only on the press. The two calls are
 * two mutations, so the plan stays on screen while the delete is in flight.
 */
function DeleteFlow({ project, current, onClose }: FlowProps) {
  const plan = useDeleteProjectData();
  const apply = useDeleteProjectData();
  const windowPath = useProjectStore((s) => s.path);
  const setPath = useProjectStore((s) => s.setPath);
  const showToast = useUiStore((s) => s.showToast);
  const [refusal, setRefusal] = useState<string | null>(null);

  // One dry run per open: StrictMode runs effects twice in development.
  const asked = useRef(false);
  const askPlan = useRef(plan.mutate);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (asked.current) return;
    asked.current = true;
    askPlan.current({ path: project.root, dryRun: true });
  }, [project.root]);

  function confirm() {
    setRefusal(null);
    apply.mutate(
      { path: project.root, dryRun: false },
      {
        onSuccess: () => {
          const follows = current || windowPath === project.root;
          if (follows) setPath(null);
          showToast(
            follows
              ? `Deleted the data of ${project.root}. This window has no project now.`
              : `Deleted the data of ${project.root}.`,
          );
          onClose();
        },
        onError: (error) => setRefusal(error.message),
      },
    );
  }

  return (
    <DeleteProjectDataDialog
      project={project}
      plan={plan.data}
      planError={plan.error?.message ?? null}
      refusal={refusal}
      deleting={apply.isPending}
      onCancel={onClose}
      onConfirm={confirm}
    />
  );
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Why `This project` is off (storage design §3): a project is a git
 * repository, or a folder chosen with `Use` in Settings → Connection.
 * `.openalpaca` marks nothing any more, and no copy names it.
 */
export const NO_PROJECT_TITLE =
  "Choose a project in Settings → Connection: a git repository, or any folder you Use there.";
```

### Spec conflicts

1. **Who edits `API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md`.** `interfaces.md` §0 gives both to S6, and the sheet is followed:
   S5b edits neither. (An earlier draft cited a brief giving S5b "`API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` updated where
   they describe these surfaces" and carried a task S5b.9 for it; no such brief is on record beside the sheet, so the
   task is withdrawn and its drafted rows are *Hand-off to S6*.) S6 also keeps `docs/GUI_Manual.md` (Project card
   `:99-101`, re-base `:987-1004`), the other manuals, `CLAUDE.md` and the records.
2. **The invalidation sets (interfaces §6.3) omit `GET /v1/status`.** `MemoryView.tsx` `useProjectRoot` (`:57-63`)
   enables `This project` from `GET /v1/status.project_root`, keyed `qk.status(path)` (`query-keys.ts:24`), and
   `useSessionSidebar.ts:134` compares sessions with it. `Use` on a folder with no git turns that field from `null`
   into the root, and deleting such a project turns it back; with the sheet's sets the Memory view would be a 30 s
   poll behind. A changed key covers most of this — the window's path changes with `Use`, a re-point and a delete
   — but not `Use` on the very path the window already holds (a folder with no git, stored as typed by an earlier
   build, which S5b.4's card invites the owner to `Use`): the key is unchanged and the cached `project_root: null`
   would stand. Correction: all three writes also invalidate `qk.statusAll()` (S5b.3). It is an addition to the
   sheet's sets, not a change to any other slice's contract. **Ratified (R-S6):** the lead accepted it, and
   `interfaces.md` §6.3's invalidation sets now name `qk.statusAll()` for all three writes.
3. **Accepted (R-S14).** **The window's own project through a re-point and a delete is unspecified.** Spec §3: "A path that cannot be
   canonicalised … is matched as written against the registered roots", so after a re-point a window still holding
   the old (gone) root resolves to no project and files its next turn there; after a delete a window still holding
   the root re-registers it on its next turn (§3 *Register*: a chat turn registers), recreating an empty project the
   owner just deleted. Correction (S5b.6, S5b.7): a window on that project takes `result.project.root` after a
   re-point and clears its project after a delete, each tested.
4. **`API_MAP.md:281` is stale beyond the shapes:** it says "`POST /v1/workspaces/purge` exists and the GUI never
   calls it" and "its type omits `queued_tasks`" — both false after S5b.2/S5b.7. S6 replaces the row (*Hand-off to
   S6*).
5. **DESIGN_SPEC's `StopDaemonDialog` entry is cited as "§3.32" (`:1619`, `:1697`) but sits under `### 3.34 Toast`
   (`:1300`, entry at `:1313`).** Pre-existing; the hand-off's four bullets go beside it and cite it by name ("the
   entries beside `StopDaemonDialog`"), not by number, so S6 neither repeats nor fixes the misnumbering.

### Open points

- **No typed word on `Delete data…`** (S5b.7). One danger-ghost press after the plan is on screen, `Cancel` the default
  focus — the GUI's precedents for data loss are click confirmations (`Remove` key, the arming `Forget`); the CLI's
  factory reset takes a typed word (D-B). The owner may want one here as T33 was asked for the stop; recorded, not
  built.
- **Accepted (R-S14).** **Clearing the window's project after a delete** (S5b.7) is this draft's choice (conflict 3). The alternative —
  keep the path and let the next turn register a fresh, empty project — is defensible if the owner keeps working in
  that folder; the toast says which happened.
- **Accepted (R-S14): the `Choose…` picker in `Re-point…` stays.** **No `Use` button on a Projects row, and no folder picker on the Project card.** Neither is in the spec; `Choose…`
  exists only in the Re-point dialog (reusing `pickDirectory`). The picker itself is not named by the spec either: it
  is kept as the dialog's way to name a folder that moved (an existing, shell-free helper; the field still works
  alone), and can go without touching anything else if the owner wants the dialog bare.
- **Hidden characters in a project root are not escaped** in the list or the dialogs: a root is the owner's own path
  and the plan entries are daemon prose, not text a tool, model or extension controls (the Gotcha's rule).
- **Freshness of the list:** no event announces a project a turn registered; the list re-reads on mount and after the
  app's own writes. A `workspaces_changed` event would be daemon work (S5a or later), not built.
- Settled against the S5a draft (`plan-drafts/stage1/S5a.md`, as read by the verifier): the `IsHome` and `Exists`
  sentences are `interfaces.md` §1.4's `Display` texts; the delete's BUSY sentence is `{n} run(s) under {root} are
  queued, running or paused; delete its data once they finish` (plus a live-conversation and a memory-slot variant),
  now the S5b.7 fixtures' wording; the purge **dry run** refuses `WORKSPACE_BUSY` too (both busy checks precede
  `if request.dry_run`), which `DeleteFlow` draws as `Could not read what would be deleted: …` with `Delete data` off;
  `entries` is nine fixed rows, zeroes included (`sessions/`, `runs (database)`, `projects/<name>/uploads/`,
  `…/artifacts/`, `…/memory/`, `projects/<name>/`, then three `keep` rows: `uploads/ (root store)`,
  `artifacts/ (root store)` and the project root), so `${action}:${entry}` keys are unique and
  `plan.entries.length > 0` always holds; the fixtures quote two of those rows. The UI shows whatever arrives either
  way. S5a also answers I/O failures with `500`s the sheet's table does not list, each with an existing
  code (its SC-7, as S5a's verifier left it: `IO_ERROR` for an unreadable `projects/` or resolution,
  `WORKSPACE_MOVE_FAILED` for a failed re-point, `DB_ERROR` for a failed delete — the earlier draft's
  `WORKSPACE_READ_FAILED` / `WORKSPACE_REPOINT_FAILED` / `WORKSPACE_DELETE_FAILED` are withdrawn); S5b shows any
  refusal's sentence, so nothing here changes for them.
- Settled: vitest 4.1.11's mock module is a `Proxy` whose `get` throws `No "<name>" export is defined on the … mock`
  only when a missing export is *accessed* (`startVitestModuleRunner` chunk), and its SSR transform turns a named
  import into a property access at the use site — so S5b.4's one-hook mocks are safe until a component calls another
  hook, and S5b.5 stubs all five before ProjectsCard calls them.
- Settled from the installed packages, not from a run (no bun command was run): vitest 4.1.11's reporter prints its
  `Test Files` and `Tests` summary rows; vite 7's build log ends `✓ built in <time>`; Prettier 3's check prints
  `All matched files use Prettier code style!`; vitest 4 names an unnamed `vi.fn()` mock `"vi.fn()"` in a
  call-count failure.
- The Stage 1 live check (§16) should exercise, on the rebuilt app under an isolated home: `Use` on a folder with no
  git and on a git subfolder, `Re-point…` after renaming a project folder, and `Delete data…` on a project with a

## Stage 1 plan — slice S6: the text, the records, and the stage's end (gate, live check)

Draft for the Stage 1 plan. Read at `32292608` (`feat/markdown-memory`). The spec is `spec-stage1.md` (design rev 0.8:
§1 R2, §8 *ST-9* and the reset preview, §9 *Text*, §16 Stage 1 step (6) with its gate and live check, §17 *Records*);
the shared names are `interfaces.md` (§0's S6 row, §7.1's last row); the lead's rulings in `rulings.md` bind it — R-S3
(§7's removal list), R-S5 (the build before any launch), R-S7 as amended (one answer for a failed registration;
the home-store overlap is `409 WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` on every route), R-S8 (deleting a project's data takes the project
exactly; `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` for a path inside one), R-S10 (no typed word), R-S11 (into §18), R-S13 (a turn
with no path has no project) and R-S14 (the accepted conflicts; two residue lines into §18). The brief is
`s6-brief.md`; every gap `consistency.md` lists for S6 that is not a ruling is taken here (*Spec conflicts*, first
item, names where each went).

**Every other slice lands before this one; the text below describes the tree after S5b.** Where the anchors come from:
no slice S1–S5b edits `docs/*.md`, the repository `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/openalpaca-gui/API_MAP.md`,
`apps/openalpaca-gui/DESIGN_SPEC.md`, `apps/openalpaca/src/commands/config_factory_reset.rs` with its tests (S5a
SC-2) or the records under `tasks/` and the vault — for those a `file:line` is HEAD's and holds (checked:
`grep -n 'docs/[A-Z]' S1.md … S5b.md` names no manual edit). Every anchor in a file a slice rewrites is quoted from
that slice's draft, not from HEAD, and says so: `store/mod.rs` and `store/tests.rs` after S3.7, S3.11, S5a.5 and
S5a.8; fixture 17 after S4.8 and S5a.10. Where this draft cannot know whether a slice already reworded a line (S6.2),
the task is a sweep: the grep that prints what is left, and the rule for each line it prints.

### What this slice does

It brings every sentence the stage made false into line with the tree, then proves the stage and records it. In code:
`ContentKind` loses the two reserved kinds that were never content, `skills` and `cache` (R2), and the seeded home
README gains a `projects/` row and `state/`'s `repl_history`, with the `kept/` folders a deleted project leaves (S6.1);
the factory-reset preview says `projects/` is left in place (spec §8; S6.1b); `artifact_write`'s description, the
CLI's `store` help line and the doc comments that still describe an in-project store or a marker walk are reworded
(S6.2). In the documents: the switch-over note — what an old in-project `.openalpaca/` holds, that nothing reads it,
how to carry a note over by hand, where projects live now, the old README (S6.3a); the Daemon and CLI manuals and the
repository README (S6.3b); the GUI manual, `API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` (S6.3c). Then one gate pass with all
four bun gates (S6.4), a live check on the rebuilt daemon under `loopback-only.sb` from its first launch, with the
app's surfaces checked live only where the session has screen access (S6.5), and the records (S6.6). No migration,
no route, no CLI verb, no config key, no event variant.

### Rules every task follows

- **One cargo process at a time.** A task's tests run as `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`; the workspace run is
  S6.4's, once. Never two cargo processes together (the GUI bundle build in S6.5 Step 1 runs its own cargo — nothing
  else runs then).
- **No test and no command touches `~/.openalpaca`.** S6.1's new test reads a constant and reaches no store; S6.1b's
  tests run under the CLI's `EnvSandbox`, as the module's tests already do; S6.5 points `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` and
  `OPENALPACA_CONFIG_DIR` at a scratch root before anything runs. Never read, list or write `~/.openalpaca`. (S6.4's
  workspace run holds to it: since S2.5 a turn with no workspace path resolves nothing — the lead's R-S13 — so the
  tests that run one read no `projects/` folder; *Open points* 11.)
- **Anchored edits only** — the Edit tool, or a Python script that asserts each anchor matches exactly once; never
  BSD `sed -i`. A heredoc carrying code, Markdown or paths is quoted (`<<'EOF'`; `tasks/lessons.md`, 2026-09). An
  old or new text quoted inline in this plan wraps at about 120 columns: a line break inside an inline span stands for
  one space in the file (fenced blocks are exact, line for line). A span written with double backticks (`` `x` ``)
  carries backticks of its own; they are part of the text.
- **Formatting.** rustfmt is not run on any file this slice edits (several carry drift at HEAD, and rustfmt follows
  `mod` declarations). The code below is written in rustfmt's style. For each Rust file a task edits, record
  `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file> 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^Diff in'` before the edit; after it the count is the
  same and no `Diff in` line falls inside the edited lines. At `32292608`: `config_factory_reset.rs` (with its tests)
  0, `artifact_write.rs` 4 — S3.7 edits the latter, so take its count after S5b, not from here.
- **`python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check`** at the end of every task that edits Rust. S6.2 regenerates first: the
  CLI's `store` help line is quoted in `docs/api/apps/openalpaca.md:31`.
- **Manuals name no ruling id.** User-facing text says what happens; the records carry the ids (R…, ST-…, R-S…).
  `docs/` keeps its existing links (T12, T22) as they are.
- **Records.** A design document's status line and revision log are bumped on every edit; `.md` under `tasks/` is
  checked with `git check-ignore -q <file>` (exit 1 = tracked; `tasks/storage-design/*.md` and
  `tasks/memory-redesign/*.md` are whitelisted, `.gitignore:120`, `:123-124`; `tasks/todo.md` is ignored and never
  staged). A range is written `first^..last` or as a list (`git`'s `A..B` leaves `A` out). Cite `path:line` only for a
  line opened in that session.
- **Commits** use a conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line naming the command and its result, and end with
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git add` names explicit paths: the tree carries an
  untracked `tasks/deps-upgrade/` that is another session's.
- **Never print the daemon's token** (S6.5): it is read inside the driver and passed nowhere else.

**Order.** S6.1 → S6.1b → S6.2 → S6.3a → S6.3b → S6.3c → S6.4 → S6.5 → S6.6. The text lands first so the gate covers
it; the live check runs on the gated tree; the records cite both. A FAIL in S6.5 stops the stage: the defect is fixed
in code with a test (in the slice's area, as its own commit), S6.4 runs again, then S6.5 from Step 1.

  (g) A new subsection. Insert immediately above the line `## Run and Verify`:

```markdown
### Projects live in the home store

Earlier builds kept a project's files inside the project: a `.openalpaca/`
folder at its top held the artifacts and uploads of its conversations and, on
a store an earlier build of the Markdown memory used, that project's memory
notes. This build writes nothing inside a project. Each project gets a folder
in the home store instead, `~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/`, named after the
project's path — `/Users/you/dev/app` becomes `-Users-you-dev-app` — with a
`project.json` that holds the project's permanent id and its path, and the
project's own `artifacts/`, `uploads/` and `memory/`. A project is the git
repository a conversation runs in (its top folder, wherever inside it you
are) or a folder you choose: Settings → Connection → `Use` in the app, or
`openalpaca chat --project <dir>`. A `.openalpaca/` folder no longer marks a
project, and a folder with neither git nor a choice is no project.
`openalpaca store list` shows every project; [CLI Manual →
`store`](CLI_Manual.md#store) says how to re-point one whose folder you moved,
or delete everything OpenAlpaca holds for one (a file of it that another
conversation still shows is kept, under `~/.openalpaca/uploads/kept/` or
`~/.openalpaca/artifacts/kept/`).

**An old `<project>/.openalpaca/` is never read again** — not its artifacts,
not its uploads, not its notes. Nothing converts it and nothing deletes it.
What it holds is yours:

- **Artifacts and uploads** (`artifacts/`, `uploads/`) are ordinary files. Keep
  the ones you want anywhere you like; the app no longer lists them.
- **Memory notes** (`memory/owners/<owner-key>/notes/*.md`, on a store an
  earlier build of the Markdown memory used) can be carried over by hand:
  1. Start a conversation in the project once — any turn from inside it, or
     `Use` in the app — so that it has its folder under `projects/`.
  2. Run `openalpaca memory doctor` from inside the project. It prints your
     owner key and, for the project, the folder of your notes there
     (`…/projects/<name>/memory/owners/<owner-key>`) — `ready` once it holds
     a note, `absent` until then.
  3. Copy the note files (`cp -p` keeps them private) into that folder's
     `notes/`, creating it, and any folder above it, if it is absent
     (OpenAlpaca makes its own folders `0700`; `chmod 700` makes yours the
     same). If `doctor` said `ready`, the running daemon records each copied
     file as a note edited outside OpenAlpaca — origin `external` — at its
     next scan, within 30 seconds, or at once with `openalpaca memory sync`.
     If it said `absent`, stop the daemon (`openalpaca daemon stop`), run
     `openalpaca memory doctor --repair` from inside the project — it builds
     the folder's record from the files, every note recorded as `external` —
     and start the daemon again.

  A note carried over keeps its text, not its history: its origin (whether you
  wrote it or it was learned) and the record of notes you forgot there do not
  come with it.
- **Then delete the folder by hand** (`rm -rf <project>/.openalpaca`) once you
  have what you want from it. A repository that committed files of the folder
  (its `.gitignore`, its `README.md`, artifacts) still tracks them: commit
  their removal too.

`openalpaca memory doctor` also lists the record an earlier build kept in
`~/.openalpaca/state/memory-control/` for each such project ("project snapshot
… carries no project id: an earlier build wrote it for …"). It is never opened
and nothing deletes it; it is small and harmless.

On a store an earlier build of this branch already used — one this build opens
without the message above — the first start also changes four things:

- The records of the files an earlier build stored inside a project's
  `.openalpaca/` are deleted (the database moves to schema 3). A message that
  was handed one of those files — in any conversation — keeps its text and
  shows the file as unavailable.
- A conversation bound to a folder that only an `.openalpaca/` marked keeps
  its binding. With no git repository above the folder, its turns run with no
  project until you choose the folder with `Use` or `openalpaca chat --project
  <dir>`; with one, its next turn runs in that repository's project and starts
  a new conversation there, once.
- A project an earlier build used has no folder under `projects/` until its
  first turn after the switch, or `Use`, gives it one. Until then
  `openalpaca store purge` does not know it, and learning that reaches its
  unread turns — as the catch-up shortly after a start usually does — drops
  them rather than learn them. A folder only an `.openalpaca/` marked never
  gets one unless you choose it.
- The memory search index is rebuilt from the notes in the background (about
  15 to 17 seconds at 100,000 notes); search answers from the note files
  meanwhile.

```

  (d) The `store` section. Replace everything from the line `` ### `store` `` (`:588`) up to, not including, the
  line `` ### `memory` `` (`:642`) with:

````markdown
### `store`

Your projects: list them, re-point one whose folder you moved, or delete
everything OpenAlpaca holds for one.

```bash
openalpaca store list
openalpaca store rebase /old/path/my-project /new/path/my-project --dry-run
openalpaca store rebase /old/path/my-project /new/path/my-project

openalpaca store purge /path/my-project          # prints the plan, deletes nothing
openalpaca store purge /path/my-project -y       # prints the same plan, then carries it out
```

A project is the git repository a conversation runs in — its top folder,
wherever inside it you are — or a folder you chose (`openalpaca chat --project
<dir>`, or `Use` in the app). Each has a folder in the home store,
`~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/`, named after its path: `project.json` (the
project's permanent id and its path) and the project's artifacts, uploads and
memory notes. Nothing is written inside the project's own folder. A project
is recorded the first time the daemon accepts work for it, and is listed from
then on.

`list` notes:
- Each project prints its path, then its folder under `projects/` and its id. A project whose path is no longer a directory is marked `missing — its folder is gone: re-point it, or delete its data`; its data is kept and its conversations still open. With no projects yet, it says how one is made.

`rebase` notes:
- Moving or renaming a project's folder on disk leaves it `missing` at its old path; nothing follows it on its own. `rebase <old> <new>` re-points it: the project's folder under `projects/` is renamed for the new path, and every row that names the old path — conversations, messages, runs, follow-ups and file records — is rewritten in one database transaction, so a crash leaves the old path or the new one, never half. The project's id does not change, so its memory notes come with it untouched. A re-point a crash interrupted is finished at the next daemon start.
- `--dry-run` changes nothing. It reads both paths and prints what is recorded under the old one (artifacts, conversations, runs, messages, follow-ups), the folder that would be renamed, and each refusal the real call would meet.
- The daemon refuses rather than guesses, changing nothing: an old path that is no project of yours is a `404`; a run there that is queued, running or paused, or a memory write that holds the project for more than a few seconds, is a `409` `WORKSPACE_BUSY` (retry once it finishes); a new path that is not a directory is a `422` `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY` (move the folder first); a new path that is already a project of its own, or that rows still name, is a `409` `WORKSPACE_EXISTS` — delete that project's data first, or re-point onto another path, because two projects are never merged; a new path that is the home store, lies inside it or contains it is a `409` `WORKSPACE_IS_HOME` (an old path there is no project of yours: the `404` above). Absolute paths only.
- The app's Settings → Connection → Projects → `Re-point…` does the same.

`purge` notes:
- **Without `-y` nothing is deleted.** The command prints the plan; `-y` prints the same plan and then carries it out. A direct `POST /v1/workspaces/purge` with no `dry_run` field is a dry run too.
- **`<project>` is a project's root, exactly as `store list` prints it** — or its folder as `store list` prints it, `projects/<name>` (`openalpaca store purge projects/-Users-me-code-my-project`). A path inside a project — `openalpaca store purge /repo/src` — is refused, and the answer names the project's root: one mistyped path never deletes a whole project's conversations and notes. A relative path is taken from the shell's directory.
- **What goes:** the project's conversations — messages, tool-call rows, queued follow-ups, and each one's log directory under `~/.openalpaca/sessions/`; its runs with their subagent spans and run events; its uploads and its by-products with every version; the memory notes of **every** owner in the project, with their control snapshots in `state/memory-control/`; the summaries of the deleted conversations in your global memory; and its folder under `projects/`. A follow-up queued from another project to run in this one goes too. The rows go in one transaction, then the files.
- **What is kept:** a file of the project that a message in a surviving conversation still shows — an upload, or a by-product as its newest version — is moved into the home store, under `uploads/kept/` or `artifacts/kept/`, and stays readable there; the plan counts them. The project's own folder is never touched: OpenAlpaca deletes only what it holds for the project.
- The plan names each entry with its retention class, the way the home store's `README.md` does:

```text
Would delete the data of /Users/me/code/my-project
  projects/-Users-me-code-my-project · id 3f6c2a1e-8b4d-4c7a-9e2f-5d1b0a9c8e7f
  delete  sessions/                                      3 conversations, 41 messages, 12 tool calls, 0 follow-ups — their logs live in the home store's sessions/
                                                         (size-capped, optional age sweep)
  delete  runs (database)                                2 runs, 5 subagent spans, 18 run events
                                                         (never swept — removed only when you ask)
  delete  projects/-Users-me-code-my-project/uploads/    4 uploads handed to this project's conversations
                                                         (swept: an upload attached to no message is deleted once past the grace period)
  delete  projects/-Users-me-code-my-project/artifacts/  9 by-products of this project's runs, with every version
                                                         (never garbage-collected — removed only when you ask)
  delete  projects/-Users-me-code-my-project/memory/     6 memory notes of every owner, in 1 partitions, with their history
                                                         (yours — never swept)
  delete  projects/-Users-me-code-my-project/            project.json — the project's id and path; OpenAlpaca forgets the project
                                                         (store metadata)
    keep  uploads/ (root store)                          1 uploads another conversation still shows, moved here under kept/
                                                         (swept: an upload attached to no message is deleted once past the grace period)
    keep  artifacts/ (root store)                        0 by-products another conversation still shows, moved here under kept/ as their newest version
                                                         (never garbage-collected)
    keep  /Users/me/code/my-project                      the project's own folder — OpenAlpaca never touches it
                                                         (yours)
  kept: 1 uploads and 0 by-products another conversation still uses, moved to the root store

Nothing was deleted. Re-run with -y to carry this out.
```

- With `-y` the same plan is followed by what was done — `deleted:` with every count, zeroes included, and `removed:` with the session-log directories, the memory partitions and the folder under `projects/`.
- The daemon refuses rather than guesses, deleting nothing: nothing of yours there is a `404`; a path inside a project is a `422` `WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` that names the project's root; a run there that is queued, running or paused — or a conversation with a run in flight — is a `409` `WORKSPACE_BUSY` (a queued run has not started yet, but it already named this project), and so, with `-y`, is a memory write that holds the project for more than a few seconds. A conversation with no project is never touched: `openalpaca sessions delete` is the verb for one.
- A purge is not reversible and there is no undo.
````

```markdown
**The project.** The Project card holds this window's project. Type a folder
and press `Use`: the daemon resolves it (`POST /v1/workspaces`) — the git
repository it lies in, else the folder itself, which is how a folder with no
git becomes a project — and records it, and the window keeps the root the
daemon answered, not the text you typed. The card names the root this window's
turns go to (`GET /v1/status`), and says so when a path stored by an earlier
build lies in no project. The window sends that root as `x-workspace-path` on
`POST /v1/chat`; runs started here record the project, and what they produce is
kept in its folder under `projects/` in the home store — nothing is written
into the project's own folder. `Clear` drops the window's project; with none,
the GUI sends no header and everything goes to the home store's own folders. A
refusal — the home store, or a path that is not a directory — is the daemon's
sentence under the field, and the window keeps its project.

**Projects.** Under the card, every project the daemon knows
(`GET /v1/workspaces`): its path, its folder under `projects/`, a `this window`
tag on this window's own, and a `missing` tag on one whose folder is no longer
at its path — its data is kept and its conversations still open. The list is
read when the panel opens and after each change made here; a project a chat
turn records elsewhere appears the next time it is read.

**`Re-point…`** tells the daemon where a moved project's folder is now. The
dialog counts what is recorded at the old path (`GET /v1/workspaces?path=`) —
conversations, messages, runs, files — and says when runs there are still in
flight; type the new folder or press `Choose…`, then `Re-point`
(`PATCH /v1/workspaces`). The project's folder under `projects/` is renamed for
the new path and every record of the old path is rewritten in one transaction;
its memory notes are keyed by the project's id and come with it untouched.
Nothing re-points on its own. The daemon refuses rather than merges: while a
run there is in flight (`WORKSPACE_BUSY` — retry once it finishes), onto a path
that is not a directory, and onto a path that is already a project or that
records name (`WORKSPACE_EXISTS`, which names both ways out); the dialog stays
open with the daemon's sentence. A window on that project follows it to the
new path.

**`Delete data…`** deletes everything OpenAlpaca holds for a project. On open
the dialog asks for the plan (`POST /v1/workspaces/purge` with
`dry_run: true`) and draws it as served: each entry marked `delete` or `keep`,
with what it holds and its retention class, the counts, and what another
conversation keeps. `Delete data` — there is no word to type — then deletes the
project's conversations, runs, uploads and by-products, the memory notes of
every owner, and its folder under `projects/`; a file a surviving conversation
still shows is moved to `uploads/kept/` or `artifacts/kept/` in the home store
and stays readable. The project's own folder is never touched. Refused while a
run there is in flight (`WORKSPACE_BUSY`). There is no undo. A window on that
project is left with none.
```

artifact, the note and the upload are found under the new name; (g) `openalpaca store purge` on a path inside the
project is refused with the root named (R-S8); (f) `openalpaca store purge <project>`, plan first, deletes the
project's data and leaves the repository's own files byte-identical. The app's surfaces are checked live only with
screen access (Step 13); otherwise their vitest suites, run in S6.4, are the proof and the report says so.

**Standing rules** (`tasks/lessons.md`, 2026-10, both entries; `plan-stage0.md` Task L; the owner):
- `~/.openalpaca` is the owner's real store: never read, list, write or name it in a command. Every command that
  starts or talks to a daemon has `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` and `OPENALPACA_CONFIG_DIR` pointing into the scratch root;
  no command runs with the repository as its working directory unless it says so.
- The daemon runs under `scripts/eval/memory/loopback-only.sb` **from its first launch**, the profile proven before
  the first model turn. Nothing leaves the machine. The model is the local Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` (the owner's
  standing authorization for live checks).
- A fresh store's first turns are persona onboarding (no `start_workflow`): one attended onboarding turn first, and a
  refusal during onboarding is not an attempt. A daemon started by hand logs to stderr — read `daemon.out`, not
  `state/logs/daemon.log`.
- Attended turns go through the HTTP API with `unattended: false`; every pending confirmation is recorded **before**
  it is answered through `POST /v1/chat/confirmations/{id}`, and only the tools a step names are approved — anything
  else is denied and recorded. The token is read inside the driver and never printed.
- `cargo build -p openalpacad -p openalpaca` runs immediately before the daemon is launched (R-S5): the daemon binary
  `cargo test` built carries the test guard.
- Never answer a macOS permission or keychain dialog: leave it on screen and say so in the report. No `git` command
  here may sign: every commit in the scratch repository passes `-c commit.gpgsign=false`.

- [ ] **Step 5: The driver.** Save as `$OA/driver.py` (scratch, not committed):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage 1 live-check driver over the daemon's HTTP API.

The port and the token come from $OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE/state/discovery.json;
the token is never printed or written. Every request and answer is appended to
evidence/<label>.jsonl beside this file.

  driver.py turn   <label> <message> [--workspace P] [--session ID] [--attach FILE_ID]... [--approve TOOL]...
  driver.py get    <label> <path> [--workspace P]          prints the JSON answer
  driver.py post   <label> <path> <json> [--workspace P]   prints the JSON answer
  driver.py upload <label> <file> [--workspace P]          prints the JSON answer
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import uuid

STORE = os.environ["OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE"]
EVIDENCE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "evidence")
os.makedirs(EVIDENCE, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(STORE, "state", "discovery.json")) as f:
    _discovery = json.load(f)
BASE = f"http://{_discovery['listen']['host']}:{_discovery['listen']['port']}"
TOKEN = _discovery["auth"]["token"]


def call(method, path, body=None, workspace=None, raw=None, ctype="application/json", timeout=120):
    data = raw if raw is not None else (json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None)
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"}
    if data is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = ctype
    if workspace:
        headers["x-workspace-path"] = urllib.parse.quote(workspace, safe="/")
    request = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            status, payload = response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        status, payload = e.code, e.read()
    try:
        return status, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)
    except ValueError:
        return status, payload.decode(errors="replace")


def record(label, kind, **fields):
    row = {"t": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), "kind": kind, **fields}
    with open(os.path.join(EVIDENCE, f"{label}.jsonl"), "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    shown = json.dumps(fields, ensure_ascii=False)
    print(f"[{row['t']}] {kind} {shown[:800]}", flush=True)


def turn(args):
    allowed = set(args.approve)
    stop = threading.Event()
    seen = set()

    def answer_prompts():
        while not stop.is_set():
            status, body = call("GET", "/v1/chat/confirmations")
            pending = body.get("confirmations", []) if status == 200 and isinstance(body, dict) else []
            for c in pending:
                rid = c.get("request_id")
                if rid in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(rid)
                ok = c.get("tool_name") in allowed
                record(args.label, "confirmation", request_id=rid, tool_name=c.get("tool_name"),
                       agent_id=c.get("agent_id"), task_id=c.get("task_id"),
                       tool_arguments=c.get("tool_arguments"), approved=ok)
                status2, _ = call("POST", f"/v1/chat/confirmations/{rid}", {"approved": ok})
                record(args.label, "confirmation_answered", request_id=rid, http=status2)
            time.sleep(1)

    body = {"content": args.message, "unattended": False}
    if args.session:
        body["session_id"] = args.session
        body["activate"] = True
    if args.attach:
        body["attachments"] = [{"file_id": i} for i in args.attach]
    status, answer = call("POST", "/v1/chat", body, workspace=args.workspace)
    record(args.label, "post_chat", http=status, body=answer, message=args.message, workspace=args.workspace)
    if status != 200:
        return 2
    threading.Thread(target=answer_prompts, daemon=True).start()
    url = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/stream/{answer['stream_id']}?token={urllib.parse.quote(TOKEN)}"
    done, deltas, event, data = None, [], None, []
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url), timeout=args.timeout) as stream:
        for raw in stream:
            line = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r\n")
            if line.startswith(":"):
                continue
            if line.startswith("event:"):
                event = line[6:].strip()
            elif line.startswith("data:"):
                data.append(line[5:].lstrip())
            elif line == "" and (event or data):
                payload = "\n".join(data)
                try:
                    obj = json.loads(payload)
                except ValueError:
                    obj = payload
                if event == "delta":
                    deltas.append(obj.get("content", "") if isinstance(obj, dict) else str(obj))
                elif event != "reasoning":
                    record(args.label, f"sse_{event}", data=obj)
                if event in ("done", "error"):
                    done = obj
                    break
                event, data = None, []
    record(args.label, "answer", text="".join(deltas))
    delegation = done.get("delegation") if isinstance(done, dict) else None
    task_id = delegation.get("task_id") if isinstance(delegation, dict) else None
    if task_id:
        started = time.time()
        while time.time() - started < args.run_timeout:
            status, task = call("GET", f"/v1/tasks/{task_id}")
            task = task if isinstance(task, dict) else {}
            state = task.get("status") or (task.get("task") or {}).get("status")
            if state in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted"):
                record(args.label, "run_end", task_id=task_id, status=state)
                break
            time.sleep(5)
    stop.set()
    return 0


def show(args, status, body, kind):
    record(args.label, kind, http=status, body=body)
    print(json.dumps({"http": status, "body": body}, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0 if status < 400 else 1


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    t = sub.add_parser("turn")
    t.add_argument("label")
    t.add_argument("message")
    t.add_argument("--workspace")
    t.add_argument("--session")
    t.add_argument("--attach", action="append", default=[])
    t.add_argument("--approve", action="append", default=[])
    t.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=900)
    t.add_argument("--run-timeout", type=int, default=2700)
    g = sub.add_parser("get")
    g.add_argument("label")
    g.add_argument("path")
    g.add_argument("--workspace")
    p = sub.add_parser("post")
    p.add_argument("label")
    p.add_argument("path")
    p.add_argument("body")
    p.add_argument("--workspace")
    u = sub.add_parser("upload")
    u.add_argument("label")
    u.add_argument("file")
    u.add_argument("--workspace")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "turn":
        return turn(args)
    if args.cmd == "get":
        return show(args, *call("GET", args.path, workspace=args.workspace), "get")
    if args.cmd == "post":
        return show(args, *call("POST", args.path, json.loads(args.body), workspace=args.workspace), "post")
    boundary = uuid.uuid4().hex
    name = os.path.basename(args.file)
    with open(args.file, "rb") as f:
        content = f.read()
    raw = (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="{name}"\r\n'
           f"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n").encode() + content + f"\r\n--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return show(args, *call("POST", "/v1/files/upload", raw=raw, workspace=args.workspace,
                            ctype=f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"), "upload")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

  Check it parses: `python3 -m py_compile "$OA/driver.py"`.

```markdown
From Stage 1, each found while planning, reviewing or checking it, and left as it is:

  by hand, or one of R11's two folders with one id, which `list()` leaves out — is skipped by the rebuild and the
  doctor and not listed by the doctor (`IdlessSnapshot` lists only id-less snapshots); `adopt` skips it with a WARN.
  Recorded, not built (the lead's ruling R-S11).
- **R11 is kept by `list` and `by_id`, not by `lookup`.** `lookup` reads two folder names, so it cannot see a copy of
  a project's folder elsewhere under `projects/` and still answers for the original; two folders recording one root
  under *different* ids (a copy whose id was edited) read as the plain-name one by `lookup` and as both by `list`.
- **A stranded `projects/.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp/`** after a crash in the middle of `register` is hidden, passed over by
  `list` and never swept (a few hundred bytes; a sweep would be a deletion path). Recorded, not built (the lead's
  ruling R-S14).
- **Case-insensitive home volumes** keep R6 by construction (`name_for` and `lookup` read the folder through the
  volume) but no test covers a case-sensitive project volume beside a case-insensitive home.
- **A write for a root that is not registered** takes the slot `unregistered:<canonical root>`; during a re-point's
  window it fails at open (`NotRegistered`) rather than waiting. **Learning drops** a chunk whose stored root was never
  registered — rows from before Stage 1's registration — besides a deleted project's (ST-21's explicit check).
- **The CLI's counts print "1 partitions", "1 uploads"**: the plural is not chosen by count.
- **`root_gone` reads a failed `lookup` as "not gone"**, so while `projects/` is unreadable each learning retry spends
  a model call before the write's own error holds the cursor (S4).
- **The delete's edges** (S5a): a chat turn — not a run — in one of the project's conversations is not refused, so
  its write between the transaction and the folder's removal is lost with the folder; a project only an earlier
  build's rows name cannot be deleted until a turn registers it (`404`); the delete and the re-point do their
  database and file work inside the async handler, and registration runs inline on the runtime at the chat turn and
  the upload (S2).
- **The delete publishes no `memory_changed`** for the partitions it drops (the event names one note): the window
  that deleted invalidates its own Memory queries (S5b); an open Memory view in another window keeps showing the
  deleted notes until a later `memory_changed` or a fresh read — the 30 s reconciliation scans the home partition
  and the registered projects' only, so it announces nothing for a deleted project. Recorded, not built (the lead's
  ruling R-S14).
- **The app's Projects list** (S5b): no event announces a project a turn registered, so the list re-reads on mount
  and after the app's own writes; a project root is shown unescaped (the owner's own path, not text a tool, model or
  extension controls); `Delete data…` takes no typed word (the lead's R-S10; T33 stays the owner's question).
- <anything the gate or the live check parked, one bullet each, with its evidence>
```

A test that reaches `store::projects::register` — a chat turn, an upload, a memory write or a dispatch with a project, or any test that registers a project — holds its crate's home-store guard (`crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard` in storage, `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard` in core and the daemon, `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox` in the CLI, the module guards in plugins and connectors); without it the test usually panics (`test-home-guard`, *Feature Flags*) — a backstop, not a guarantee: under parallel tests an unguarded test can pass the check while another test of its crate holds that crate's guard (interfaces §7.4), so the guard audit, not the panic, makes a test guarded. A test that only *resolves* a project path reads `~/.openalpaca/projects/` and takes the guard too (the lead's R-S2); a turn with no workspace path resolves nothing and needs none (R-S13). A daemon binary `cargo test` built carries the guard (`apps/openalpacad/tests/daemon_args.rs` builds it inside the run): run `cargo build -p openalpacad` before starting it by hand, or its first project turn panics.

### Choices made where the spec is open

- **The brief's six tasks keep their numbers; the gaps it did not name become lettered tasks beside the one they
  belong with** (S6.1b, S6.3a–c) — the slices' own S5a/S5b convention — so a reference to "S6.4, the gate" stays true.
- **The factory-reset preview is its own task (S6.1b), not part of S6.1**: a different crate and test binary, and the
  one change of this slice a reviewer reads as behaviour (a preview the owner types a word under).
- **`projects/` sits under the preview's *Left on disk, and orphaned until adopted*,** not under *unreferenced*: it
  holds both (by-products and uploads with no rows, notes waiting for `adopt`), and what makes it more than leftover
  files is the `project.json` id that lets `adopt` find a project's notes (R20).
- **`ContentKind::Scratch` gains a doc saying it is reserved until Stage 2**, and the enum's doc says why `projects/`,
  `config/skills/` and `state/cache/` are not kinds — the three names a reader of R2 would ask about.
- **The home README's `memory/` row says "outside any project"**; without it the README promises one place for notes
  while `projects/` holds the rest. The `artifacts/` and `uploads/` rows name `kept/` (S5a's open point).
- **`artifact_write`'s description changes two lines and keeps "deliverable"**: what the tool is for changes in Stage 2
  (ST-11), not here. `file_write`'s description and result are left — they name no in-project folder, stay true between
  the stages (spec §4) and are pinned by Round G's test.
- **The code sweep (S6.2) is a rule plus a predicted list**, not a closed list: whether S2–S5a reworded a given comment
  cannot be known before they land, and a closed list would either miss a line or edit one twice.
- **The manuals name refusal codes the routes answer, and no ruling id**; the purge plan the CLI Manual quotes is
  rendered from S5a.8's rows and S5a.11's printer by a scratch script, and S6.5 compares it with a live dry run.
- **The switch-over note's new subsection goes after *Keep the builds apart*,** at the end of the note: the reset
  procedure (steps 1–7) stays one numbered sequence, and the projects text applies to a store whether or not it was
  reset.
- **The live check drives the daemon through its HTTP API and the CLI,** as Stage 0's did; the driver is written out
  in full (S6.5 Step 5) because Stage 0's lived in a session scratchpad. It approves by tool name only and records
  every prompt before answering it.
- **(h), the delete's kept-file rule, is checked live** although the brief lists (a)–(g): it is the delete's one
  cross-project effect, S5b's open points asked the live check to exercise "a cross-project link", and it needs one
  upload and one turn. A link the turn cannot make is reported, not forced.
- **The GUI half of the live check builds the bundle first** (S6.5 Step 1), so the debug `cargo build` of R-S5 is the
  last cargo process before the launch, and runs the app unsandboxed against the sandboxed daemon, as the memory
  redesign's packaged check had to (`08-evaluation-report.md` §4.1).
- **The records' figures are tokens** (`<range>`, `<gate>`, …) filled from `git log` and the gate's record, as
  `plan-stage0.md`'s Task R did; S6.6 Step 8 greps that none is left.

- **The brief names six tasks; `consistency.md` lists more gaps for S6.** Taken: the factory-reset preview and fixture
  17's `preview_contains` (consistency §8; S4 open point 8; S5a SC-2) → S6.1b; `API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` (§9
  *Text*; S5b's *Hand-off to S6*, taken as drafted; S3's `reveal_path` row) → S6.3c; the module docs S2 left
  (`memory/service/mod.rs`, `routes/memories.rs`), the `store` help line S5a left, `STORE_DIR_NAME`'s doc → S6.2; the

   or a folder as `store list` prints it, `projects/<name>`; S6.3b's `purge` notes say so.
2. **R-S8's refusal code — settled.** S5a.8 answers `422 WORKSPACE_NOT_A_ROOT` naming the root (HEAD's code, kept for
   the purge); the Daemon Manual's purge row and the CLI notes name it, and S6.5 Step 14 expects it.
3. **The quoted purge plan** (S6.3b) is S5a.8's nine rows as S5a.11 prints them, rendered by a scratch script from the
   two drafts; it assumes neither changes in the rulings round. S6.5 Step 15 compares it with a live dry run and S6.6
   Step 7 corrects it.
4. **The app's surfaces are checked live only with screen access** (brief). Without it, design §16's Stage 1 clause
   is amended (S6.6 Step 1 (c)) and the report names the vitest suites that stand in.
5. **(h) depends on the chat route accepting another project's upload id on a turn in an explicitly named session
   with no project.** No draft says it refuses one; if it does, (h) is reported not exercised and the kept rule rests
   on S5a.1–S5a.2's tests. Between (h)'s setup and the delete no turn carries a project header (S6.5 Step 11), since
   a conversation with no project takes the first project a turn names.
6. **`/remember` over the HTTP API.** MD-13 answers memory commands on an attended turn of the app's or the CLI's chat;
   the driver's `POST /v1/chat` with `unattended: false` is the app's surface. If the daemon still answers with the
   memory commands' refusal, S6.5 Step 9 saves the note through `POST /v1/memories` (a registration site too) and the
   report says which path was taken.
7. **The workspace test total cannot be predicted** (every slice adds and removes tests); S6.4 records it and checks
   only `0 failed` and the 16 ignored.
8. **CLI output grammar** ("1 partitions", "1 uploads", "1 runs") is S5a.11's and S5a.8's; recorded in §18 by S6.6,
   not fixed here — a plural rule would change pinned test strings in S5a.
9. **The vault edits are outside the repository** and are not committed (as in Stage 0's records); S6.6 Step 10 lists
   each one so the owner can see them in Obsidian.
10. **QuickStart** names no in-project store and is unchanged; S6.3c Step 4 checks that it stays so.
11. **The gate's read of the real `~/.openalpaca/projects/` — settled (R-S13).** S2's *Open points* counted about 80
    tests that run a turn with no workspace path, whose CWD fallback would have resolved the daemon's working
    directory against the real home store from S2.5 on. The lead's R-S13 removes the fallback in S2.5 itself: a turn
    with no path resolves nothing, so S6.4's workspace run reads no `projects/` folder and S6's rule (*Rules*, second
    bullet) holds without a guard on those tests. The tests that do send a path hold a guard: S2.5 (l) as extended in
    the second round's verification (S2's *Second-round rulings applied*), which adds the four that resolve through a
    turn or a route. S6.6's §18 bullet for them is gone and CLAUDE.md's new Gotcha says
    a turn with no path needs no guard. No manual sentence changes for it: at `32292608` nothing that decides
    behaviour read the CWD-derived `workspace_id` (S2's *Second-round rulings applied*), so no user sees a difference.
12. **A switch-over consequence S5a recorded and S6.3a now states**: a project an earlier build of this branch used
